    - **Fire Flies** (enemies.json `fireFlies`, `Spawns`): the director sends them only while the train's under `stoppedBelow` (0.3 m/s, the "stopped" the Track Doll and Switchman use), at `stoppedWeight` (0.5) of their B.5 weight for "rare". **Spec reading:** App. A.5's break-off "the train pulls away at speed" now means getting under way, `pullAwaySpeed` 15 → 2 m/s (`pullAwaySeconds` 8 unchanged), so a swarm that hasn't ignited goes once the train's moving; B.5's gates and weights (dark sections, a lit lamp, ×2 at depth, ×0 lamps out) all stand. No spec test pins either number.
    - **Bots:** the walkers went *away* from boarded hounds to wait for the drop-off. With them staying, the first harness night had a pack sit on the rear car all night (`CinderHound:Commit` at the cap 1,000 samples, 58 car-fire beats). Now the fit (`Heed.PackFightHealth`, 55) go along the roofs at them and swing; the hurt keep clear. With `stayAboard` off they keep the old way.
    - **Harness** (`dt harness --route frontier:7 --bots 8 --enemies --seconds 600`), the old tuning vs this: sends 17 → 10, Fire Flies 9 → 2, car-fire beats 2 → 19, deaths 0 → 1 (mauled in the pack fight), fairness violations 0 → 0, no derail, 7.2 → 6.5 km, beats/min 5.8 → 6.4, longest quiet 19.4 → 14.1 s, quiet share 0.35 → 0.04; the director at the cap 0 → 148 of its decisions (the hounds aboard hold their slot until they're beaten). Max correction 0.41 → 0.24 m.
    - **Not yet / the director's call:** the rest of App. F's boarding rules (shut doors stopping some boarders, the Stoker's heat, the Track Doll's haunt) are other items. Whether a pack aboard should hold a cap slot all night, as it does now, is a pacing call.
    - **Verified:** `BoardingRuleTests` (hounds stay past every dismissal, eating and setting the car alight, start the fire only after 20 s alone, go with a cut car, v1.1's drop-off with the flag off; the director's Fire Flies weight null at speed and `stoppedWeight` stopped; a swarm goes once under way; left stopped, the car catches). `CarFireTests` restaged stopped (a walker's lamp, a driver getting under way); `EnemyTests.AGunnerWhoWaitsForRange…` aims at any running hound (the director's own pack came in its 90 s). All 881 Sim tests green, `NetcodeTests` included; Game tests 234/235 with `CrewAudioTests.ABotCrewIsHeardOverTheNetworkAsTheAppHearsIt` failing under load and passing alone.

270. **One night length for every tier: 24 km, a 51 min dawn; the tiers differ in density, and quiet is counted in kilometres (the director's decision of 6 Oct 2026, GDD App. F.1 and §11, spec B.8; T125).** "The time a run takes should always be the same. Difficulty scales not by time but by monsters and density of challenges." Before this, T125 was only the GDD's lines and note 13's open design call: routes ran 18–40 km by tier (route.json 18–22 / 24–30 / 30–36 / 36–40; the line generator's columns 18 / 23 / 29 / 34 / 40 km, lerped by severity), so a Deep night was twice a Local one.
    - **The length** (route.json `nightLengthKm` 24, gate to terminus, read by the line generator's `Limits` whatever the tier or severity). The reading that keeps spec B.8's own table true: 24 km at the 14 m/s cruise is 28.6 min, the table's 28 min floor (no stop made), and the total run's 45 is that plus a few stops. It's also the length of the Frontier night the director has been playing (frontier:7 was 24.3 km).
    - **The dawn** (spec B.8: route ÷ 11 m/s + 40%). The generated lines' dawn read its own copy of the formula in linegen/tiers.json `conflicts` (`dawnAverageSpeed` 11, `dawnSlack` 0.18), which the 100-night playtest's change to +40% (route.json) never reached: frontier:7's dawn left 2.4 min over the ideal run (note 188), and `StopDriver` skipped every stop. Those two numbers are gone from tiers.json; the line generator reads route.json's. Every night's dawn is now 3,055 s (51 min); the sweep's ideal transits are 23–35 min.
    - **The density.** Over one length, each line-generator column's counts are its density, and the director's per-night `baseBudget` (90 / 150 / 230 / 330, unchanged) is 3.8 / 6.3 / 9.6 / 13.8 a km. But the deeper columns were set for 29–40 km: at 24 km `dt linegen sweep` put Dead lines at 20–22% and Deep territory at 2–4% within two attempts (8 and 44 of 50 unpassed), every failure "no room on the main line" for a long climb. The space-hungry counts were cut until every tier's quotas fit (tiers.json, its comment lists each): facilities 3 on every tier (Dead lines and Deep 4, deep max 5 before; a stop is time, so more of them would lengthen a deeper night again), fewer junctions, alternates, dead lines, brass fields and momentum banks on Dead lines and Deep, and Dead lines' `climb_long` quota 2 → 1. What still rises steeply with the tier is what goes on each kilometre: the ruling grade and tightest bend, the terrain budget (0.6 → 2.6 a km; laid per night, measured, 6.8 / 9.3 / 14 / 17), washouts, weak bridges, Corruption, fog, cold, signage and the director's budget.
    - **Reading (ARCHITECTURE §8's rule).** B.8's "POIs per run 3–5" now reads 3: the decision makes time the constant, and a stop is the thing that costs it. If the director wants the deeper tiers to keep more stops, the length has to grow for every tier (a Deep night's quotas don't fit 28 km either: 8% first attempt, 33% within two at Deep's old counts).
    - **The legacy generator keeps its own lengths.** `RouteGenerator` (route.json `tiers`, "routes": "legacy") isn't the game's nights; it's the fixture much of the sim's suite is pinned to (StopCrewTests' stops, SwitchTests, HoldoutTests, SpurDrillTests: 20 tests failed on a fixed 24 km, one through a real bot overshoot at a stop that only the new geometry found). Left as it was, and said so in route.json.
    - **Quiet in kilometres** (enemies.json `pressure.quietRampMetres` 1,260, `quietBackstopSeconds` 120). Note 266's quiet term ramped over `quietRampSeconds` (90 s) since a threat was engaged; now it ramps over the line run since then (1,260 m: the old 90 s at cruise), or the seconds over 120 if that's sooner, so a stopped train can't wait it out. A train at 20 m/s meets its full pull in 63 s, one at 7 m/s or standing in 120 s. `quietRampMetres` 0 is the old ramp. `World.QuietMetres` counts the same for the pacing log beside `QuietSeconds`.
    - **Found, not fixed:** on every generated line about 1–2% of 20 m samples of the ballast 2 m out sit 0.1–0.65 m off the rail's height, in runs of 100–300 m, flat where the rail is on a grade (frontier:7 at 6,480–6,640 m beside a junction pad; frontier:9, frontier:1, frontier:4, local:2 alike). `ThereIsGroundWithinReachOfTheTrackAndTheFormationIsAtRailHeight` samples every 500 m and had missed it; on the new frontier:7 it lands on one, so the test now reads frontier:3 (clean at 500 m). Not pads, roads or the junction's own pad: a terrain follow-up.
    - **Tests.** New: `LineGenTests.EveryTierIsTheSameNightAndTheHarderOnesAreDenser` (every tier's line 24 km, its dawn 3,055 s, its ideal run inside it; challenges and terrain budget per km strictly rising by tier; the director's budget a km rising; a Deep night lays more than a Local one), `SpecTableTests.RunLengthMatchesSpecB8`, `PacingTests.QuietIsCountedInLineRunWithTimeTheBackstop`, `RunTests.AQuietStretchIsCountedInLineRunAndInTime`. Changed: `LineGenConfigTests` (the length no longer lerps; Deep's facilities), and tests pinned to one generated line's geometry re-pointed: `CabRideTests` (deepTerritory:1's first alternate; every alternate's run in to its rejoin on frontier:3), `LeftBehindAlongTests` (deepTerritory:1's last alternate), `WatersideTests` (frontier:2 has no shore now, so deadLines:3; deadLines:2 for the river; a dyke's fields skip a branch's own formation: frontier:7's dead line runs off across them). No spec test pinned the old lengths.
    - **Sweep** (`dt linegen sweep --seeds 20`, 3 / 10 / 20 cars): within two attempts Local 100%, Frontier 95–100%, Dead lines 95–100%, Deep territory 95–100%; first attempt 55–100% (lowest at 3 cars: the light train's descent check); no fallbacks, none unpassed.

271. **Stoker v3, the firebox half (the director's decision of 6 Oct 2026, GDD App. F.1).** The GDD reads: "In the firebox it's territorial: opening the door while it's in gets you a heavy burn, and a second kills. That's the mistake you learn from. The counter is to vent and starve the fire below a set heat; it then leaves the way it came, and a break of two to three minutes follows … A water hose through the open door kills it, at the cost of much of the fire. No chip damage." Note 263 already had the rest of v3: drawn by heat, boarding at the tender with a telegraph, driven off on the way in, and the 150 s break. In the firebox it still worked to App. A.5's old rule (open the door with a shovelful and club it, 12 burn a blow), and it ate the fire.
    - **Territorial** (`Stoker.Tick`, Interior.cs). The door opening on it (a shovelful, `Boiler.FireDoorOpen` rising) hurts whoever's nearest the door within `stoker.doorReach` (1.8 m): `doorBurn` 60 the first time, `doorKill` the second. Both are lethal-class hurts, kept per Stoker, so a fresh one starts over. It can't be clubbed in the firebox: `Reachable` and `MeleeRadius` hold only while it's boarding, so a crowbar does nothing and `burnPerBlow` is gone. That is the "no chip damage".
    - **Vent and starve.** While it's in, it still lurches heat in (`feedRate` ± `swing`), holds the safety valve shut and runs the regulator open (`Tamper`), so the boiler goes in about half a minute if left (`OnceInItEatsTheFireAndSwingsTheGaugeToARupture` unchanged). It no longer eats the fire (`eatPerSecond` 0.2 → 0), so the crew have to starve it. Under `starveFirebox` (2 of 6) it lets the valve go, takes its heat out (`BreakOff`) and goes back over the footplate to the coal over `boardSeconds` (`Extra2` 1 again, drawn there). It's then gone, and `World`'s break begins. The vent (12/s) outruns its heat and the fire's, so with the blow-off held and no coal it's gone before the boiler: 10–90 s in the test, 15 s for the bots.
    - **The hose** is an extinguisher held into the firebox (Fire, within `doorReach`) for `hoseSeconds` (2). The spray opens the door without the burn, kills it, and takes `hoseFireCost` (60%) of the fire. **Director's call:** the GDD says a water hose, and the cab has none, so the extinguisher stands in (one fetched from car 1: the engine has no room to mount one). A cab hose fitting (a slacking pipe off the injector) would be the real thing.
    - **Bots** (`FightStoker`). They club it while it's boarding, as before. Once it's in they never shovel or open the door: the vent held, the brake on, throttle shut, until it's starved out. The old "leave it if hurt" health gate went with the burns.
    - **Words:** the event hints are "it's in the firebox: don't open the door. Vent and starve it (no coal), or hose it" and "starved out: it's going back the way it came". The death line is "BURNED OPENING THE FIREBOX ON THE STOKER".
    - **Verified:**
        - `Build1121Tests.TheDoorOpenedOnItBurnsHeavilyAndTheSecondTimeKills`: swings do nothing; the first shovelful costs 60; the second kills.
        - `VentedAndStarvedItLeavesTheWayItCameAndNobodysHurt`: it goes back over the footplate, no rupture, nobody hurt, and the break holds.
        - `AHoseThroughTheDoorKillsItAndTakesMostOfTheFire`.
        - `CarFireTests.TheDriverVentsAndStarvesTheStokerOutBeforeTheBoilerGoes`: the conductor bot, at full health.
        - The rest of `Build1121Tests` and `CarFireTests`, and the Game `StokerTests`, `SafeYardTests` and `CreatureArtTests`, are green.
        - `dt audit cascades --only stoker` seeds 1–3: gone at 15 s, no rupture, no derailment.

272. **The damage model: a few big hits, rare healing, an edge flash (the director's decision of 6 Oct 2026, GDD App. F.1).** "Damage model: Lethal Company style. Health exists, but damage comes in a few big hits, never chip damage. Healing items are rare loot. Damage feedback is minimal: an edge flash and a sound. Creatures mostly don't take damage; they're driven off by their rules."
    - **Big hits** (`enemies.json` `damage`: `minHit` 30, `minGapSeconds` 2.5; a hit is 35, a heavy hit 60, as spec B.2's "most attacks 35–60" already said). Before → after: Cinder Hounds 45 every 2.5 s → 35 every 4 s; Grumbler 15 / 1.5 s → 35 / 3 s (`grabBelowHealth` 30 → 35); Climbers inside 25 / 1.5 s → 35 / 3 s; the Gaunt 35 / 2 s → 60 / 4 s; a Choir ghost's hit back 15 for every blow → 35 at most once every `hitBackEvery` 3 s (new, `ChoirGhost.Struck`); the marsh (the Drift) 6 a second → 35 every 2.5 s. Bites still can't kill (App. A.1, kills go through GRAB), so with these each grabbing creature takes two hits to beat you down, then grabs: two or three hits from death, and a clean escape after the first costs one. The Stoker's door (`doorBurn` 60, `doorKill`; note 271) already fits.
    - **Spec reading:** the marsh is a §22 hazard, but what's in the reeds has a telegraph, a commit and a bite, so it counts as a creature and is held to the rule. **Left continuous, on purpose:** a car fire's burn by the second (the director's own call, note 263: "a brush hurts, standing in it kills"); a leaking hose's gas (12/s while you stand in the cloud); the chemicals' fumes, a keg's blast and a wreck heap (single hits already); landings (spec B.3, one knock per landing scaled by speed, 10 to 80). These are the train's and the world's dangers, not something a creature does, and each is one decision: step out of it.
    - **The rule is pinned:** `DamageModelTests.NoCreatureHitIsChip` reflects over `EnemyTuning` and holds every int `...Damage` (plus the Stoker's `doorBurn`/`doorKill`) to 0 or at least `minHit`, so a future chip number fails CI; `ACreaturesHitsComeWithLongGaps` holds each creature's interval to `minGapSeconds`; `ACreatureOnYouIsTwoOrThreeHitsFromDeath` does the arithmetic for each grabber.
    - **Healing** (`loot.json` `healing`: `useSeconds` 2; bandages 30, medicine 50, morphine 80; `botBelow` 50). **Reading:** the carrier uses it on themselves, the simpler of the two (no "crewmate in reach, looking at"). Carried, hurt, at nothing Use works, Use held standing for 2 s uses it up (`Bodies.Dose`, the repair kit at a radio's pattern: a tap still puts it down, moving starts it over, at full health it's an ordinary find and Use puts it down). The host removes the body and `World.CrewAct` adds the health, capped at player.json's `health` (`Bodies.FullHealth`, from the sessions' player tuning). Clients send intent only; the progress rides the loot body's record (the ninth field, as a radio's mend does; **protocol 31 → 32**, after WP19 took 31) for the HUD's "[E] HOLD: USING THE BANDAGES (50%)". It costs the find's scrip: heal or sell. Bots (`Heed.Heal`, last in `BotCrew.Think`): carrying one below `botBelow`, stand still and hold Use. (Bots don't pick finds up today, so it's for when they do, and for a find handed over.)
    - **Rare:** measured over 20 nights a tier, the healing finds were 8.5 a local night, 6.2 frontier, 3.3 deep territory: a quarter of every find, since a cabinet held nothing else and a floor cache was a third medicine. Now a cabinet's list is 16 items with bandages twice, medicine and morphine once (candles, lamp oil, a pocket watch, treats and the like for the rest), and the floor cache no medicine: about one a frontier night. Each find's value is unchanged (it's the container's budget share). `HealingFindsAreRare` pins it (at most 2.5 local, 2 frontier, 1.5 deep a night, never over an eighth of the finds, never none).
    - **Feedback:** a red edge flash (`Hud.EdgeFlash`, drawn first so the HUD's text stays on top): bands round the rim, deepest at the edge, gone a ninth of the way in. `Hud.HurtStrength` watches this machine's replicated health per session: a fall flashes at its size over 60 (a heavy hit fills it, never under 0.35), fading over 0.6 s (squared). Presentation constants beside `HitMarkerSeconds`, not tuning. The sound is the existing `crew-hurt.hit`, already scaled by the hit (GameAudio.Crew). In a headset it's on the HUD panel's edge (VR is on the backburner). `dt screenshot --hud --hurt [s]` (or `--hurt` alone) stages it: out/shots/hurt.png (0.6) and hurt-heavy.png (1), looked at: the cab reads clear, the rim red.
    - **Follow-up for the director — "creatures mostly don't take damage":** not reworked here. Today, **killed by blows or rounds** (health in blows, `Struck`/`Hit` → gone): Cinder Hounds (3), Climbers (3), the Grumbler (6, regenerating unless two hit it), the Gaunt (8), Choir ghosts (6, and seizing is broken only by killing one), the Switchman (3; one cannon round), the Passenger (5), a Soot Child (2, more as it drinks), Followers (1, a nest 3), Ribbits (2), Tippy Toesie and the Whistler (struck off a victim they let go; enough blows kill them), the Car Hugger (regenerates; one player can barely out-hit it), the Track Doll (only cornered; a cannonball shatters her), the Stoker (a blow on the way in drives it off; the hose kills it). **Driven off by their rules, no health that matters:** the Fire Flies (blows do nothing; speed pulls away), the Draggers (a friend hauls you up), the marsh (stand still), the Track Doll's usual way out (stop short of her), the Stoker in the firebox (starve it), the hounds' break off (outrun them, or a cannon round in range). The candidates to move to rules are the ones whose counter is "club it": the Grumbler, the Gaunt, the Passenger, Climbers and the Choir ghosts.
    - **Verified:** see the log (docs/log/A1.4.md) for the run; `DamageModelTests` (10), `HudTests.AHitFlashesTheEdgeByItsSizeAndFades` and `AHealingFindInHandSaysHoldUseWhenYoureHurt`, and the full Sim suite (NetcodeTests included).

273. **T128, the director's notes on build 1121: falls, where a grab takes you, a player left behind, and the forts (GDD App. F; queue #7).** Four notes, each reproduced or measured headless before it was changed. Built on #189's pressure director (note 266).
    - **"Far too easy to fall off the train."**
      - *Cause.* Nothing held you on a roof. A step with your centre past the roof's 1.5 m half-width put you in the air, and at speed the ground killed you (spec B.3). Walking at roof-run pace while you looked 30–50° aside for under a second, with the key held, was enough. The wind (note 201) pushed you sideways on top of that. Thrown-on-a-bend (note 260) and the Draggers were already warned or telegraphed, so they weren't the cause.
      - *Measured.* `FallTests`' careless walker: a wandering aim, a glance aside every 5–10 s with the key held, a correction only once the edge has been in view for half a second, half the cars at a run, the gaps jumped, wind 1, 16 m/s on R 500 m bends. Over 4 × 300 s it fell **42 times (14 deaths) before and 0 after**. The before figure is the same walker with `edge.lip` 0, measured in the same test. With glances allowed during gap jumps too, it was 54 before and 13 after, all 13 off short jumps.
      - *Fix* (`PlayerMotor.HoldAtEdge`, `player.json` `edge`). On a roof or a coupler plate, a walking step that would bring your feet within `lip` (0.3 m) of where the footing ends is held. Across the car and along it are held separately, so you slide along the edge.
        - You go over a side only if you mean to: walking at it within `stepOffDegrees` (30°) of straight out. The careless walker's deliberate steps went over 7 out of 7.
        - Off a roof's end only by a jump, a ladder, or a step down onto more of the train within `catchDrop` (3.5 m): a coupler plate, a platform, the tender. A car's door steps, a running board and the chassis don't count as a catch. That keeps the bots' step off the end onto the plate (note 231) working.
        - The wind brings you to the lip and no further (`windOverLip` false; true restores the old wind).
        - Jumps, the Draggers' `PullOff`, thrown-on-a-bend and every creature's knock put you in the air, so the hold never sees them.
      - *Spec reading.* Spec B.2's "roof run: wind and balance penalty" is kept as the wind's stronger push while running, which now ends at the lip. The flag records the other reading.
      - Stateless, from the intent and the car shapes alone, so `PlayerState` and the wire are unchanged and prediction re-simulates it exactly.
    - **"A creature carried the director up a mountainside."**
      - *Cause.* The Whistler is the only creature that carries a player away from the train. The Corrupted drag theirs along the cars, and the Gaunt carries bodies away over the ground already. The Whistler ran `nestDistance` (60 m) straight out from its gap at the gap's height. That is past Line Plan §12.6's 40 m walkable corridor (`train.json` `recovery.corridorM`), and the run went through the land. Where the land rose, the carried player was held underground, and when let go `UpdateSupport`'s "the earth, however far up it is" stood them on the hillside.
      - *Fix* (`Whistler.NestSite`). The nest is straight out across the line from the gap. It tries the side the player was taken from first, at `nestDistance` (now 30 m, inside the corridor), shortening by `nestStep` (4 m) to `nestMinDistance` (8 m). The way there must be runnable:
        - no 2 m of it steeper than `nestMaxSlope` (0.4, about 22°);
        - never more than `nestMaxRise` (6 m) above or below the rail;
        - no water (a generated line's `TerrainField.WaterNear`).
        If neither side has such a spot, the nest is at the formation's edge. The carry runs over the ground (`GroundAt` each tick).
      - The run's length goes in the replicated `Extra2`, so `CreatureArt` puts the nest down when the Whistler arrives.
      - `GrabDestinationTests`: on flat land the nest is 30 m out, on the ground. With a 1.5 rise-over-run mountainside on the taken side it goes to the level side, within ±6 m of the rail's height, and the player stands on the ground there. A gentle bank is fine; in a cutting with walls on both sides the nest is at the formation's edge.
    - **"A player left behind should feel the world close in … They needn't die at once."**
      - *Rule* (`Director.Abandoned`, `enemies.json` `director.abandoned`). Once a second, alongside the night's pressure and whatever holds that (the grace, a ban, the caps), each crewmate gets a pressure of their own when they are:
        - alive and on the ground;
        - more than `behindM` (150 m) along the line from the train's nearest end;
        - outside the forts.
      - *Rate.* It builds by tier × the night's conditions term (note 266's `Terms.Conditions`) × (`perSecond` 0.05 + `rampPerSecond` 0.15 × min(1, seconds left / 60) + `perKm` 0.3 × km behind).
      - *Hunts.* Past `threshold` (6) a Ribbit pack comes for them alone. Ribbits fit because App. A.6 has them hop in on whoever they outnumber on the ground, and they can be outrun. The pack is:
        - `pack` 2 the first time, one more each time to 5, and always larger than the group the player is in;
        - put down `spawnOut` 35 m away the first time, closer each time to 18 m, on the line's side the player is on, on the ground and out of the forts.
        Each hunt takes `relief` (6) off. While a pack is still after them, no other comes.
      - Hunts don't come from the budget or count against the caps, and they use their own dice stream (`0xAB4D0`), so the night's own draws are unchanged. Back aboard, back near the train, or in a fort, the pressure is gone. The roster gate holds: an edition without Ribbits sends nothing.
      - `LeftBehindPressureTests`: 400 m behind a train at 12 m/s, the first hunt comes 20–90 s in. A player who gets away from each pack 8 s after it arrives sees at least 4 hunts in 4 minutes, never smaller and never slower to come, and is still alive. The Ribbits sent target only them. Beside the train or aboard, there are no hunts and no pressure.
    - **"Forts must be safe spaces that monsters never enter (§9)."**
      - *Found.* Note 263's `World.SafeYard` holds only while the run is in `RunPhase.Yard`: the departure yard before the gate. It didn't cover:
        - the departure fortress once the train is through the gate, for a crewmate left behind there or a creature chasing them in;
        - the terminus. Its last 500 m is spawn-free (`noSpawnFinal`, plan `terminus_safe`), but anything already about, or riding in aboard the train, could follow the crew in.
        No other stop is a fort. Facilities are freight stops (§16–18), and the holdouts aren't forts.
      - *Fix* (`run.json` `forts`, `World.InFort` / `TrainInFort`). The forts are safe all night: the main line up to the outer gate (the run's yard), and from the terminus gate on (the plan's `Terminus.GateM`, or the run's terminus zone on a hand-laid line; a silent settlement only if its plan keeps the gate safe), out to `halfWidthM` (80 m) either side of the line. While any of the train is in one:
        - the director holds ("in a fort");
        - the Stoker isn't drawn.
        Any creature found inside a fort after the enemies step is dismissed: it lets go and is gone. This covers spawns put down inside one, creatures riding the train in, and creatures chasing a crewmate in. Hazards (the marsh, the Sleepers) and in-car incidents (car fires) aren't creatures and aren't touched.
      - `LeftBehindPressureTests`: the forts end at the gate, start again at the terminus, and stop 80 m out. A crewmate left behind 100 m inside the gate gets no hunts. A pack hopping in after a player at the gate never has a member inside and never grabs them. A train standing in the yard holds the director.
      - *Not done.* The Choir's meter isn't stilled at the terminus. The fort buildings still have no collision (T124).
    - Tuning changes:
      - `player.json`: new `edge` block.
      - `enemies.json`: `whistler.nestDistance` 60 → 30, plus `nestMinDistance`, `nestStep`, `nestMaxSlope` and `nestMaxRise`; new `director.abandoned`.
      - `run.json`: new `forts`.
      No spec table pins any of these, so `systems-spec.md` and `SpecTableTests` are unchanged.

274. **The fortresses are solid, and the guns hit them (T124; build 1121's notes, GDD App. F: "Fort buildings have no collision, and gun shots hit nothing").** T114's `StopWalls` already stood a village's houses, barns and outbuildings as boxes that `PlayerMotor.Collide` pushes a crewmate out of and that `Guns.Solid` stops a ball at (`ImpactSurface.Structure`, the impact told to everyone as a `CannonImpact`). The fortresses were never in it: their walls, gun towers, gatehouse and houses were laid out only by the art pass (`WorldFeatures.Fortress`, from the line), so the sim had nothing there to collide with or hit.
    - **The layout moved into the sim.** `Sim.Run.Fortresses` holds the rules the art used: `Of(route, line, yardLength, terminusZone)` gives the home fortress's yard (0 to the gate at `YardLength`, its platform, lived in) and the terminus's (the plan's `Terminus.GateM`, or `TerminusZone` + 200 m short of the end on a hand-laid route, to the end of the line; dark and empty when `Terminus.Silent`). `InTheVillage`, `OnThePlatform` and `HouseAt` are the village's spacing and gaps; `LivedSize`/`House(variant)` a house's size from its seed (`HouseSeed` 7001, the draws `TownKit.LivedHouse` makes first). `WorldFeatures.Fortress`, `FortVillage`, `FortFolk`, `TownKit.LivedHouse` and `GreyboxScene` now read those, so a solid is wherever its piece is drawn, and nothing drawn moved (`dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 420 --view roof` looked at).
    - **The solids** (`Fortresses.Solids`, added to `StopWalls.Of` by `World.EnableRun`, alike on the host and every client): each 10 m wall bay a box 1.6 m thick, 14.8 m out, up to the crenellations' tops (8.9 m); each gun tower 5.4 m square, 14.4 m high; the gatehouse's two towers (3.5–8.5 m out, 7 m deep, 14.9 m) and the arch over the line from 7.8 to 13 m, above anyone on a roof; each lived-in house its footprint up to its ridge. Every box stands on the rail's height where it is and runs 3 m into the ground, as the pieces are set. These are the art's own sizes, not design numbers, so they stay in code beside the rules (as `StopWalls`' 9 m does).
    - **Bodies too.** `Bodies.Contact` now takes every `StopWalls` box as well as the cars and the ground: a crate, lamp or ragdoll thrown at a house or a fort wall comes to rest against it (it had passed through every building, villages included). Its contact is the world's (`touchedCar` −2), as the ground's is.
    - **Not solid (the director's call if they should be):** the yards' sheds and hero buildings (unchanged from T114: their crates and crane bays are worked at and in them), a Holdout's building, the home fortress's platform (a low floor with thin posts), the facilities' buildings (`StructureKit.Facility`, still placed by the art alone) and the dead towns, churches and windmills far out on the lineside (`WorldArt` settlements, `PlanArt`: placed with the art's own `System.Random`, beyond where a crew walks). Creatures don't read `StopWalls` (keeping them out of a fortress is T128).
    - **Verified:**
        - New: `StopWallsTests.WalkingAtTheFortWallStopsAtIt` (both sides: a player walking straight out at the wall stops a radius off its face, never inside a box; without the fortress's solids the same walk goes through it), `TheFortressesStandTheirWallsTowersGatehouseAndHousesOffTheTrack` (counts, the arch overhead, nothing on the ground nearer the line than the gatehouse's passage), `HitConfirmTests.ABallFiredAtTheFortWallStopsAtItWithAnImpact` (the engine's gun laid on the wall either side from the yard: one `Structure` impact, inside a solid, short of the wall's far face).
        - The Sim suite; the Game suite's `LookTests` and `LinesideArtTests`; `dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 420 --view roof` with and without `--impact structure --impact-at -20,-8.2` (a burst on a fort house's front) looked at.

275. **Tools matter: which tool, how hard, at what; the fireman's shovel; breach with a tool (GDD §12, §13, App. C.2, D.7; WP19, renumbered from its old branch's note 191).** WP19's branch (`wp19-melee`) was written before notes 197–274 and merged with main here; main is the source of truth wherever both touched a thing. Every tool dealt one blow, the shovel was nobody's, coal went on by hand, and a Holdout's lock could be smashed with empty hands.
    - **Superseded by main, dropped:** the branch's own swing record (`MeleeSwing`, with the tool in hand) and its drawing of a crewmate's swing (`CrewActs.Swinging`, a `Crewmate.Swing` field, the host's tick passed from `NetPlaySession`). Note 197's `SwingEvent` (`RecordKind.Swing`) already puts every swing on the wire, landed or not, and `GreyboxScene.Swung` draws and `GameAudio.Crew` sounds it; the tool in hand is already on the replicated player record. The branch's swing-replication tests went with it (`HitConfirmTests` covers it).
    - **Kept from WP19:** a swing is played once from its start (`CreatureArt`: `CrewPose.Swing` is one of the `fromStart` poses). Without it, main's swing was put off by each crewmate's idle beat (variant × 0.41 s, up to 2.9 s into a 0.8 s clip), so most of the crew were drawn at the end of their swing. `dt art clip crew swing --tool` passes the time unshifted for it too. `dt screenshot --act swing,swing,swing` stages each swing further into its blow (`Crewmate.Phase`) with the shovel, the crowbar and the wrench in turn.
    - **Damage by tool** (enemies.json `melee`, where melee lives; App. C.2 gives no numbers): shovel 1.5 blows, crowbar 1, wrench 0.75, empty hands 0.25 (T108). Enemy health stays in crowbar blows, everyone's tool from the start, so no creature's numbers moved; a 3-health creature takes two of the shovel's. Only what a blow does to a creature changed; nothing here touches player damage (note 272's). **Reading:** "the boiler player's shovel doubling as the crew's best club is intended tension" is about the damage, and the tension needs there to be one shovel. **Flag:** the director's damage-model decision (GDD App. F.1, 6 Oct 2026: "Creatures mostly don't take damage; they're driven off by their rules"; note 272, in flight) may take creature health away altogether, and with it what a tool's blow is worth. The tool-by-tool numbers are one table (`MeleeTuning.Blow`), so they can become a knock-back or drive-off strength, or go, without touching the rest of this note.
    - **The shovel is the boiler's** (boiler.json `shovelInHand`, a tuning flag; §8 reading). There's one, stood by the cab's tool rack (`Boiler.ShovelOut`, bit 64 of the boiler record). Use at the firebox (the keyboard's hold or T29's stroke) puts it in hand first (`CrewActions.TakeShovel`): out of your own kit, else off the rack into the first free slot. Out with someone else, nothing goes on (the HUD says the shovel's out). Use at the rack with it in hand hangs it back. A body keeps it and `Bodies.TakeTools` always takes it, like the wrench. A shovel that's nowhere (no crewmate's kit, no body: its carrier dropped out, or its body went with a car) is back on the rack (host, `World.Step`), so the train can't be left with no way to fire. `player.json` kit stays `["crowbar"]`: §12 gives nobody a starting tool, App. C.2 gives the shovel to the boiler role, and roles aren't assigned (§12 Fluidity), so it's a fitting on the engine and not part of anyone's kit. Predicted like the wrench: the take and the hang-back change the player's kit and the boiler's flag the same way on host and client. Main's Stoker rules are unchanged by it (notes 263, 271): it's reachable only per its own rules (`Enemy.Reachable`: only while it's boarding at the tender; in the firebox no tool does anything, and a blow at the shut door only rings), and opening the door on it burns whoever's nearest, whatever's in their hand. The bots' `FightStoker` clubs it while it's boarding with whatever tool is in hand, and never shovels once it's in. The App. F.1 note "the coal shovel is fun" is about firing; that's unchanged except that the shovel comes into hand as you start.
    - **Breach needs a tool (D.7: "any melee tool: shovel, wrench, crowbar").** `Holdouts.CrewAct` takes `tool` (a tool in hand). Without one, Use at the door does nothing unless it's the repair kit at a lock, so the kit's silent breach is unchanged. A barricade still wants a tool.
    - **Bots.** They use the same intents. A breacher with empty hands presses the first tool's number (`Kit.ToolToHand`, `StopHand.Breach`). A bot fires only with the shovel to hand (`CrewActions.HasShovel` in `ConductorBot.Work`), so a driver doesn't stand at the firebox pressing Use while the fireman has it.
    - **Not yet:** bots never hang the shovel back, so one who takes it out of the cab (a stop's job) leaves the fire to wait until they're back. No lag compensation beyond the reach.
    - **Protocol 31** (the boiler record's shovel bit). Tuning: enemies.json `melee` (`damage` replaced by `shovel`, `crowbar`, `wrench`), boiler.json `shovelInHand`. No spec-pinned number changed. Tests: `MeleeTests` (blows by tool), `ShovelTests` (the take, out with someone else, hung back, nowhere is home, replication, the flag off), `HoldoutTests` (empty hands breach nothing, any tool breaches, the kit at a lock in empty hands, a bot takes its tool up), `KitTests`.

276. **The engine, cab forward (the director's sketch of 6 Oct 2026: "the current front of train design that I want to change to the desired design where controls are at the front with full vis of the rail"; then "put a coal bunker in the cab").** GDD's open item ("a redesign of the front of the train … for a lone driver's view of track hazards. Every function stays") is done. Before, the boiler and stack led, the cab sat behind them with the cannon on its roof, and the coal tender followed. Now the order is reversed, as on the Southern Pacific's cab-forwards.
    - **The layout** (train.json `geometry.engine`, built by `CarShape.Engine`; `EnginePlan` is where everything reads it from, so nothing recomputes it).
        - Front to back: the pilot (`pilotLength` 0.6: buffer beam, plough, the headlamp on the cab's nose), then the cab (`cabLength` 5.0), then the boiler with its smokebox and stack at the rear, where car 1 couples on.
        - The unit is still 20 m (spec B.4), and every function stays.
    - **The cab.**
        - **Front, the driver's end:** the front windows either side of a narrow post; the driver's console under the right-hand one, with the regulator, brake and reverser; the whistle cord in that corner, hung against the side so it's out of the window. The levers still come back (+Z) towards the driver as they're worked, so `CabLevers`, `VrLevers` and the bots' driving are unchanged.
        - **Back, the fireman's end:** the firebox door in the back wall, where the boiler comes through. The coal bunker (`bunkerLength` 1.8, `bunkerDepth` 0.85, `bunkerHeight` 1.0, the director's "coal bunker in the cab") stands against the left wall ahead of the left doorway. Its gate is low in its inner side by the fire door, so the fireman's turn from coal to fire is the quarter turn it was.
        - **Roof:** the coaling hatch over the bunker, which a tower's spout pours through (`EnginePlan.CoalFromFront` replaces the tender's offset in `Run`, `StopCrew` and `dt`). The cannon stands at the roof's front, and the gun rail is the cab roof's.
        - **Ways in and up:** the doorways are at the back of each side. The running boards run from them back along the boiler to the rear deck, and a footplate off car 1's plate meets them (T90). A ladder climbs the cab's back wall from the boiler's top to its roof, and the hatch ladder goes up from the floor in the front left corner.
        - **Sandboxes:** on the boards over the drivers (`sandboxBehind` 2.5), since nothing is ahead of the cab now.
        - The tuning fields `tenderLength`, `tenderTop` and `tenderGangway` are gone. The coal store is still the boiler's `Tender` in the sim, and its capacity (spec B.5's 400 units) is unchanged.
    - **The driver's sight (T101, re-stated):** the line is in sight through the right-hand window from 8 m past the plough; with the boiler ahead it was 30 m. Spec B.7's "the stack masks the rail closer than ~60 m" is gone from it.
        - **Driver's gauges.** The backhead is now behind the driver. As on the real cab-forwards, a second set of the four gauges stands in front of them, two rows of two over the right-hand window beside the run map (`TrainKit.DriverGauge`). The scene turns both sets' needles.
        - **Backhead.** It's drawn in its own frame (`TrainKit.BackheadFrame`: the engine's turned round, +Z out into the cab), and so are everything on it, the shut fire door, the fire seen through the hole (`InFirebox`), the furnace's light and the firebox camera. A Stoker in the fire looks out of it at the cab ahead.
    - **Art** (`TrainKit.Engine`).
        - The drivers move back under the boiler with the cylinders ahead of them under the cab's back; the pilot truck is under the cab and a trailing truck under the smokebox. `Drivers` and `CrossheadRestZ` read the cab's back, so `SceneArt.Gear` turns them where they are.
        - The cab's sides have window posts. The smokebox door looks back down the train, with the tail lamp on its corner.
        - The headlamp is on the cab's nose under the windows: `World.LampHeight` is 2.0, where it was 2.8 high on the smokebox door.
        - The whistle and safety valves stand on the boiler just behind the cab (`WhistleZ`, `SafetyValveZ`; `Effects` plumes there).
        - The Stoker perches on the stack at the rear, facing forward along the boiler at the cab.
    - **Knock-ons in the sim.**
        - `PlayerMotor.SpawnInCab` used to put a crewmate at the cab's middle, which is now the bunker. A second crewmate spawned to the left (the harness's, the tests') was shoved out through the wall onto the ballast. `CabFloorZ` puts them on the open floor between the driver's console and the bunker, clear across the cab.
        - A ground switch stand's lever no longer counts from inside the cab (`SwitchStands.AtStand`). Cab forward, the cab can stand right over a toe, and getting down to the lever is the excursion the powered thrower saves (spec F.3).
        - The bots' loading give-up is 360 s; it was 300 (`StopDriver.LoadingGiveUp`, a bot's patience, in no spec table). The warm a cold hand goes back to is now 10 m further from the cars. A lone bot's crate stop already ran to the give-up on main (311 s) and now left a door open at it.
    - **Bots.** `ConductorBot.FiringSpot` is in front of the fire door, facing it (`FacingFire`). On the bunker's side, the way out of the cab goes down the middle of the cab past the bunker before turning out (`Route`, `StopDriver.GetDown`). The way out to car 1 (`Route`) runs through the left doorway, along the left board, over the rear deck and onto the plate. `SandWay`, `CabDoorZ` and the kit run read `EnginePlan`.
    - **Views.**
        - `fireman` looks back across the footplate at the fire door and the bunker.
        - `coaling` looks up at the bunker's hatch.
        - `gangway` looks along the boiler from the plate.
        - New `engine`: the whole engine three-quarters on.

277. **The art checklist's open rows to L1 (C1, the art session; the director: "keep getting L1s in there").** Eight rows had nothing of their own drawn, or only part. Each is drawn now, with a `dt` path to look at it and a test.
    - **The boiler rupture** (spec B.6, GDD §23 "loud, spectacular, run-changing"). The sim had it (the drag down to coasting, the fire and pressure to nothing) and the audio, but nothing was drawn.
        - **The burst** (`Effects.Rupture`): a flash, then a white cloud blown out of a seam torn in the boiler's left flank (`TrainKit.RuptureSeam`, between the first two straps behind the cab, seen from the left doorway and the line). A hard core of steam stands out of the tear. The jet is checked by the air and laid back down the train by its going, full for 4 s, then a hiss that thins over half a minute. Scale and grit fly from the tear. In the cab, the fire is blown back out of the firehole in steam, ash and embers.
        - **The tear** (`TrainKit.RuptureTear`, drawn while ruptured): a ragged black hole in a scorch of soot, a lip of raw bright iron, the plate peeled back in rusted petals, and burst copper tubes curling out.
        - **The seized engine:** the stack dead (a last grey wisp, no cinders), no whistle, valve or cylinder-cock steam. While she's still dragging down to `ruptureCoastBelow` the drivers are locked (`GreyboxScene.DriversLocked`: the rods stop turning and pick up where they stopped once she's coasting). Each tyre slides in a stream of sparks over a glow on the rail. The cylinder cocks' steam now comes from the cylinders (it was at the old front).
        - `dt screenshot --view rupture --ruptured s` (0.8: the blast; 30: the hiss; the train dragged down from `--speed` as the sim does), and `--view fireman` for the cab.
    - **Noisy toys** (App. C.4, C.7). Three models in `tools/models/recipes/train_stores.py`: `toy_squeaker` (a papier-mâché pig on a pleated bellows), `toy_musicbox` (walnut, lid up, the comb and cylinder under glass, a dancer on her spindle, the key) and `toy_drummer` (a tin drummer boy, sticks up mid-beat, the key in his back). `SceneArt.ToyModel` draws a toy by its `Body.Noise`; quiet ones keep the bear, horse and doll by id.
    - **The headlamp out** (train-lights: "lit and dark must both read"). Switched off or smashed (`World.LampShining` false), the beam and the halo go (`Effects.Train` `lamp`), and dark glass with a crack star covers the lit lens (`SceneArt.HeadlampOut`). The greybox lamp box is on the cab's nose at `World.LampHeight`. `dt screenshot --headlamp-out`.
    - **Lockers that don't block each other** (App. F.1). The open door swings 105°, standing out into the aisle; at 150° it lay back across the next locker's face. `LockerArtTests` pins it standing out more than three times as far as it leans back.
    - **Bend limits on the route card** (the line plan: "speed ticks on derailment bends that show the max speed"). `LineGen.PostedSpeeds` is the cab map's list of posted stretches, now shared. The route card's profile rules each stretch red along its foot with its km/h over it: B for brass, W for a weak bridge, the slower winning where two would overprint. Its key reads "IN RED: KM/H OR OFF". `dt screenshot --hud --route deepTerritory:2 --card`.
    - **Smaller prompts** (App. F.1: "they're good but they are too big"). The prompt is fine print a hand's breadth under the crosshair (`Hud.PromptDrop`), on a thin iron strip rather than a riveted plate, its hold bar along its foot. The canvas is 480×270 and its 5×7 font is already its smallest, so the overlay now draws text and keycaps at fractional scale (`Overlay.Text(..., float scale)`, `UiStyle.Keyed(..., scale)`). The scale is half the HUD's where that still gives a font pixel two screen pixels (1080p up) and whole steps bigger below (`Hud.PromptScaleAt`: the app passes the renderer's height over the canvas's, the VR panel 2). `dt screenshot --hud` now renders at `--scale` with the canvas laid over it, as the app does; it used to render at 480×270 and enlarge, so fine print showed as mush.
    - **A lighter HUD out of the cab** (hud-look: "too much UI ... not enough in world or embodied"). Off the engine, a steam-drive train's panel is gone: the driver's gauges are in the cab, the supplies view is on I, and a rupture or a bend too fast still takes the screen's middle. `HudTests` pins it.
    - **The overspeed telegraph, seen** (App. F.1: "cars straining and leaning, flanges grinding, sparks"). `BendStrain.PerCar` works each car's strain on the bend under it as `TrackRules.Assess` works the train's (0 at the board's speed, 1 at derailing), and which rail it's crowding. `Effects.Flanges` grinds sparks off each truck's leading wheel on the outer rail, more and hotter toward 1; a glow on the rail and an orange light on the ballast from 0.35; hot-iron haze past halfway. A rider on a straining car is juddered (`BendStrain.Offset`, the eye only). Presentation only, from the train and the line. `dt screenshot --view flanges --strain 0.9`.
    - **The crew in the wreck, caught mid-task** (App. F.2 take 4: "arms-up and awkward, not people mid-task"). `FilmPlayer.Task` (the host reads it from what they were at: the gun's seat, a body in their hands, the cab's controls as the driver, else the fire) starts each body in its work's pose (`WreckFilm.TaskPose`: on the throttle, bent into the shovel, sat with the knees either side of the breech, leaned back under a load). Each pose is laid bone by bone at the skeleton's lengths, and its muscles hold it for `film.taskHold` (0.4 s of the recording) before they go over to the brace and the hands go out. The gunner's hands and knees are clear of the gun, so they still go up and over it. `dt screenshot --view poses --wreck-poses --dawn 0.8`.
    - **Not yet / the director's call:**
        - A carried crate isn't in the ragdoll's hands in the film; the film has no loose bodies.
        - The cars don't lean on a bend: the frames are the sim's, and a visual roll that moved the riders' eyes but not the riders was left out.
        - No in-world toy staging for `dt screenshot`; the toys are reviewed on `dt art show prop-toy_*`.
        - The tear isn't left as a patch after a mend.
    - **Verified:** `EffectsTests` (`TheBoilerTearsInItsFlankAndTheBurstBlowsOutOfItThenHisses`, `ABendTakenTooFastGrindsSparksOffTheOuterRailHarderTheNearerItIsToOff`), `WreckDeathTests.EachGoesIntoTheWreckFromWhatTheyWereDoing` (and the gunner's test unchanged), `LockerArtTests`, `HudTests`; every view above looked at.
278. **Bends worth braking for: every night carries its tier's hard bends (queue #13, B1; note 265's open call; the director, 6 Oct 2026: derailing on a bend is the core fear, and always "a mistake by the driver, someone not paying attention to the map").** With the Sleepers gone, nothing guaranteed a night anywhere the train could come off. frontier:7's sharpest bend was 707 m (it holds √707 = 26.6 m/s, over the engine's 22), and `dt linegen sweep --cars 6 --seeds 30` found a bend that derails under 22 m/s on only 8/30 Local nights, 11/30 Frontier, 4/30 Dead Lines and 12/30 Deep. The only pieces that laid one (the Drop, the Blind Throat, the Ledge, a curved tunnel) were random picks from whatever budget the quotas left, and on frontier:7 the quotas took it all.
    - **The count is the tier's** (tiers.json columns `bends` [min, max] and `bendDerail` [m/s]; level-design.md Part B has the rules): Local 1–2 at 20–21 m/s, Frontier 3–4 at 16–19, Dead Lines 3–4 at 15–18, Deep 4–5 at 13.5–17, Deep max 5–6 at 12.5–16 (one fewer for Dead Lines and Deep than first set: note 270 made every night 24 km, and the deep tiers' 29–40 km counts didn't fit). Rolled on its own stream (`script/bends`) so it doesn't move the rest of the script. The radius is v² / a_derail (plan §8.5's 1.0), never under the tier's `minRadius`: Local's stay at 400–450 m, so its bends teach the board (it derails at 72–76 km/h, boarded 58–61), and a Frontier one is 256–361 m (58–68 km/h, boarded 47–54).
    - **The piece** (setpieces.json `hardBend`, kind `bend`, `LineBuilder.BendShape`): one curve of 40–90° at that radius with 120–260 m of straight either side, so it's seen coming; where room is short, shorter straights, then a smaller turn, and none under 60% of the least. Weight 0: never a budget pick. Not a crunch: like brass it's a demand, and the lethal spacing check (§7.3) keeps it a braking distance from the next lethal check, so a driver who brakes for one can brake for the next.
    - **Where** (`AssignBends`, `CarveBends`): after the quotas, hazards and signatures are handed out, one in each equal share of the line between the threshold and the home straight, to the stretch with room nearest the share's middle. That first try came up short on Dead Lines and Deep (a stretch's musts each reserve a whole recovery they seldom use, so the room estimate says "full" where the filled line has slack): 75 of 30×3 attempts failed the count. So a share still without its bend once the stretches are filled gets one where the line already is: cut into its longest plain connector (a run-up and a run-out of straight either side), or laid on a climb, descent, summit or roller as that piece's own turn (`Params["hardBend"]`), the line going round a hill on its grade. Dead settlements every 4–8 km no longer take room a stretch still owes its queued pieces (`Settlement(…, end − s − Owed(queue))`).
    - **The land says why** (`IntentsFor`): `LedgeUp` 8–20 m on the bend's inside (positive curvature turns left: forward is −Z, right +X), which also hides the way out of it, the reason for the board; `Embankment` 2–6 m down on the outside, what a train would go off into. The geometric sightline round a 283 m bend at the shoulder's 5 m is about √(8 R m) ≈ 106 m, so most aren't blind enough (under `blindSightM` 70) for a restricted zone of its own. One that is (deepTerritory:1's 186 m bend behind its hill) had no board: the restriction before it took the bend's demand, and the board pass skipped any bend under a curve limit as if that limit's demand had boarded it. It skips now only where a curve, bridge or brass demand stands on that limit (`LaySignage`).
    - **By a branch** (`AwayFromBranches`): within `bendDeadLineClearM` (1500 m) past a dead line's toe a hard bend turns away from it, and in an alternate's window towards the alternate's side. A line that turns only one way lies the far side of its chord, and the alternate bows out on its own side of the chord, so the two stay apart; turned away, the main line bowed over toward the alternate and crossed its way back in (frontier:7).
    - **Told as note 265 tells every bend:** the board at floor(√(0.7 R)) on any bend that derails under 22 (T111), red on the cab map with its figure, the bell and the stress. Nothing new was needed there; `CurveBoardTests` and `BendWarningTests` now run over many more bends.
    - **Tags:** `curve_tight` over every stretch that derails the train under its top speed (geometry, whatever laid it; `LineBuilder.HardBendSpans`), for A1.8's #22 ("slowing opens the doors": boarding at tight curves); `pre_curve` 400–900 m before each hard bend for the Long Whistle.
    - **The validator** (plan §16.3): `hard bends` fails a night with fewer main-line bends that derail under top speed (past the gate) than the tier's least count. Spans less than 30 m apart are one bend; a reverse curve's halves are two. The metrics report `hardBends` and `hardBendSlowestMs`. `crossings` fails a night with a branch over the main line (below); `crossings` is also a metric.
    - **Found on the way: branches crossing the main line.** The bends' first cut put frontier:7's main line over its alternate, and checking every branch against the main line (more than 2 m to the wrong side, past 200 m from its turnouts) found it on main's own nights: an alternate crossed the main line about 300 m past its toe on nearly every night with one (frontier:7, frontier:2's two, local:1's two, local:3, deadLines:3). The cause: an alternate shorter than the main line has the main line bow away from it (`AltWindow.MainBow`, the alternate's side negated, right +1), but `Guide` added it to a heading that turns left for positive, so the main line bowed toward the alternate's side and swept across it just past the turnout. Sign fixed. What still crosses (the main line's own meander, a closure that overshoots: 11 of 59 alternates over 40 nights, ten a tier) is refused when laid (`CrossesMain`, after `Separated`, for alternates and dead lines): retried, lengthened and flipped as any refused alternate is, then dropped, with a dead line in its place where the junction count needs one. Over the same 40 nights 56 alternates were kept and none crosses. A shore's sea side also keeps off the side an alternate runs on from its toe to its rejoin, not only near its toe (`LayWaterside`): frontier:7's alternate left 2 km short of its shore and ran out across the flats.
    - **Found on the way: a halt's ground past its end.** A long pad laid along the line (a halt's or a town's, the fortress's, the terminus's) now leaves the rail's formation its own, as a box pad (a stop's) did: its 30 m blend held the ballast at the halt's level 20 m past its end where the line had started down (frontier:3's Mile 13 Halt, 8 cm over the rail; `LineGenTests`' formation check).
    - **Others' tests the line moved.** B4's fog blend (note 313) averaged nine samples 37.5 m apart, so its ends were 300 m apart, three of the exposure's 100 m runs: two run edges 300 m apart stepped it twice in one sample (frontier:7 at 15450, once its shore moved). It's the runs' exact mean over the window now. D1's Car Hugger nights (notes 305, 310) started at 7700 m on deadLines:2, 270 m short of its trestle; the line moved the trestle 23 m nearer, inside the 250 m it lurks from, and it never came. They start 270 m short of the trestle, taken from the line (`CrewOfTwoTests.ShortOfTheTrestle`). The rescue test also runs with the mail cranes down (`cranes: false`, `SightTuning.DropFrom` past the end; every board stays): the drops are dealt along the line skipping bridges and tunnels, so the moved features re-dealt them, and an ammo crane 100 m past the trestle had both walkers in car 4 at its side door for the bag when the Car Hugger took hold. Seeds 1 and 10, each of which eats two walkers without note 310's ladder rescue and has every one pulled out with it (1 and 3 were the seeds with cranes up).
    - **After** (`dt linegen sweep --cars 6 --seeds 30`, against main the same hour, every night 24 km): a bend that derails under 22 m/s on 30/30 nights of every tier (main: Local 7/30, Frontier 9/30, Dead Lines 3/30, Deep 10/30); median sharpest radius Local 351 m, Frontier 270, Dead Lines 215, Deep 186 (main 848, 584, 500, 500). Every night passes, no fallback seed used. First-attempt pass rates Local 1.0 (main 1.0), Frontier 0.83 (0.90), Dead Lines 0.80 (0.87), Deep 0.77 (0.90); within two attempts 1.0, 0.97, 0.97, 0.87 (1.0, 1.0, 0.97, 0.97); mean attempts Deep 1.43 (1.13), worst 5 (3). What's left is a Deep line too full for a share's bend ("nowhere to lay a hard bend") and Frontier's junction count when a crossing alternate is dropped. Alternates over the 30 nights: Local 21 (main 23), Frontier 36 (41), Dead Lines 37 (42), Deep 44 (46), the ones that crossed. Mean generation (four at once) Local 5.4 s (4.0), Frontier 9.0 (6.0), Dead Lines 6.4 (8.0), Deep 8.8 (10.7): the extra attempts and the refused alternates' rebuilds. frontier:7 has its bends at km 7.8, 15.7 and 21.7 past the gate (derailing at 63–67 km/h).
    - **Not yet:** with the cranes down, deadLines:2 seeds 6–9 still lose a walker to the Car Hugger with note 310's rescue in (two swallowed, one pulled out: D1's). S-bends (done: note 359); hard bends on alternates and dead lines (the main line only); the boarding rules reading `curve_tight` (A1.8, #22). The run-length change (#207, A1.3: one night length for every tier) shortens the deep tiers' lines; the counts are per night, and the carving keeps them laid where stretches are full.
    - **Verified:** `HardBendTests` (`EveryNightHasItsTiersHardBendsSpreadAlongIt`: local:1, frontier:2, frontier:7, deadLines:3, deepTerritory:4, the tier's count, each derailing within its band, one in each half; `AHardBendIsBoardedAndGoesRoundAHill`: a required board before each at no more than floor(√(0.7 R)), LedgeUp inside and Embankment outside; `AFrontierNightAlwaysHasSomewhereToComeOff`: Frontier seeds 1, 3, 8 at 10 cars, at least three, one derailing 3 m/s under top speed). `LineGenConfigTests` (the new fields are in the files). `HardBendTests.NoBranchCrossesTheMainLine` (local:1, local:3, frontier:2, frontier:7, deadLines:3, on the built rail, not the validator's traces; each of the five had a branch over the main line with the old sign and no refusal). `CurveBoardTests` (deepTerritory:1's blind bend), `WatersideTests` (local:3, frontier:7), `LineGenTests` (the formation), `FogTests`, `CarHuggerRescueTests` and `CrewOfTwoTests` as above. The Sim and Game suites.
279. **The world is solid (queue #14, B1; the director's decision of 6 Oct 2026, GDD App. F.1: "The carry that clipped straight through the mountain made everything feel like 2D billboards. Creatures, carries and players must respect the terrain and geometry").** T128 (note 273) put the Whistler's carry over the ground and its nest out of the hills, and T124 (note 274) stood the fortresses up. A survey of what still went through what (players, creatures, carries, balls, bodies; the fortress towns are B2's, #194) found, most visible first: the Hounds and Climbers running beside the train inside a tunnel's rock, in the air beside a bridge and inside a cutting's walls (`Enemy.WorldPosition`: rail + right × lateral, the land never asked); a crew walking through every yard building but the village's (sheds, the hero, the powerhouse, signal boxes, water towers, wells); anyone walking up a cutting's 2:1 wall or a cliff, and out of a tunnel through its lining onto the hill 18 m over it (`TerrainField.Ground` held the bore's floor to 4.5 m either side, the lining is 3.1); a Ribbit keeping the height it was put down at, and a Gaunt, a feral Grumbler and the Choir going straight through houses; the Whistler's run through a building on its way to the nest.
    - **The stops' buildings** (`StopWalls`, run.json `walls`): shut, each its footprint, are now the powerhouse, signal boxes, lamp rooms, water towers, lockups, prison cars and wells (a well's kerb `wellTopM` 0.85 high), beside T114's barns and outbuildings and B4's dead-town station, goods shed and derelicts (note 302); B4's open houses keep their walls, door and furniture (note 326). Sheds and the hero stand as their walls (`wallM` 0.3), as StructureKit.Shed draws them: a roofed length either side of a gantry's cut, each with its bay door (`bayDoorM` 4) in the middle of its side to the track it serves (`StopWalls.Shell`, `StopWalls.Doors`). The cut stays open: the gantry's legs and its operator's stand are in it (`Crane.Controls`), so the art's low wall behind it is drawn, not stood. The crates inside are fetched through the door. A Holdout stands as its walls with its door (`personDoorM` 1.2) open on the face it's breached at: its occupant still comes back inside it (GDD App. D.14, `HoldoutTests`) and walks out. Every user of `StopWalls` gets them: the crew (`PlayerMotor.Collide`), bodies and dropped things (`Bodies.Contact`), the cannon's balls (`Guns.Solid`).
    - **A facility's machinery comes first** (`StopWalls.Clear`, `Site.WorkPoints`): its modules are laid from the spur, not round the stop's buildings, so a crane's stand could fall in a shed (the foundry's did: its operator was stood off the controls, and its crew never got to them). A stop building with a module's work point in it or within 1.5 m (a crane's stand, legs and castings, the spout and its lever, the ramp and pen, the hose stand, the capstan and the sled's run, the crate stacks) gives way, whole. Each wall knows its building (`Wall.Owner`).
    - **Tunnels' linings** (`TerrainField.Confine`, through `ITrackConditions`): a point down in a bore (under its crown, `boreCrownM` 7.5) is held `boreHalfM` (3.1, StructureKit.TunnelHalf) less its radius either side of the rail. The crew and bodies are held by it; nobody is stood on the hill over the bore any more.
    - **No walking up a cliff** (`PlayerMotor.Walkable`, player.json `climbSlope` 1.25, about 51°): on foot on the land, a step that would climb steeper than that isn't taken; what's left of it goes across the slope while that stays walkable. A cutting's walls (2:1), a ledge's upslope and the sea cliffs stop you; plan §12.6's walkable ground (slope 1 with its noise) never does. Down is free. Stateless, from the step and the land, so prediction re-simulates it exactly.
    - **What runs beside the train** (`Enemy.WorldPosition`, `ITrackConditions.LateralRoom`): in a tunnel inside the bore, on a bridge on the deck (`deckHalfM` 2.6), each less `besideClearM` 0.6; out past the formation on the land, its own height over it. A pure function of the creature's replicated line position, so the sim, a client and the art all put it in the same place; the creatures' own steps are untouched.
    - **What's loose in the world** (`Solidity.Settle`, after the enemies step; enemies.json `solidity`): out of every building and inside a tunnel's lining by its body's widest sphere (note 290's `bodies`), and again until nothing holds it (out of one part of a house can be into the next), and by kind: `ground` (the Ribbits, the Gaunt, a feral Grumbler) on the land, but within `climbM` 2.5 of a car it may be up its side, boarding; `air` (the Choir) never under `airClearM` over the land; `none` its own way (the Whistler's run is laid clear, a Follower crawls along the cars, the Soot Children answer a voice). A Grumbler on its casting rides it until it's turned feral. A Gaunt asleep or stirring lies where B4's roost put it (note 309, in the building); awake, it's held out of the walls like anything else that walks. Not a fortress's walls (`Wall.Fort`): a fort drives off whatever comes into it (note 273), and a Ribbit pack held at a gate pier never came in to be driven off.
    - **The Whistler's run** to its nest misses every building: B4's #53 (note 314, `Whistler.InWall`, half a metre clear of a stop's or a fort's walls) landed first, so this note's own check went for it. Two changes to B4's code for the walls this note adds: the run checks the walls every 0.5 m, not each 2 m pace (a shell's wall is 0.3 m thick), and a stop's nest is placed where the way from the front of the stopped train misses every building by a metre (`StopGenerator`'s lairs; `SpawnSiteTests` holds 9 in 10 at their nest).
    - **Where it lives:** in `StopWalls`, `TerrainField`, `PlayerMotor`, `Enemy.WorldPosition` and one pass in `World.StepEnemies`, not in each creature's own file (A1.8's #22 and A1.10's #25 change those).
    - **Not yet:**
        - The sheds', the hero's and the Holdouts' doors are painted on closed boxes in the art: walking in through one shows the inside of nothing (single-sided walls); and a gantry cut's low back wall is drawn where the crew can walk. An art row for C1.
        - No path finding: a creature held at a wall slides along it or stays, it doesn't find the door.
        - Lineside props (trees, rocks, telegraph poles, signs) are the art's alone, placed by its own random draws: the sim doesn't know where they are, so nothing collides with them. *Done for a generated line's trees, boulders and telegraph poles (note 371), and the rest of its furniture: the road's homesteads, poles and cars, the shores' sheds, lighthouses and rocks, the biomes' buildings, walls and big rocks (note 389). E1's railway leavings stay passable.*
        - The dead towns' and halts' dressing (`PlanArt.Places`: houses, the church and the windmill drawn by the art from the town's name, 16–66 m out), facility silhouettes and the `OpenRooms` cottages aren't in the sim either; the villages a halt gets (PlanStops) are.
        - Bridges have no parapet: over the deck's edge you fall, as before.
        - Water isn't solid or swum: everything walks or sinks on the bed.
        - The derailment's wreck and film collide with the ground and the cars only (GDD E.3 asks for bridges, bores and props within 50 m).
        - Doors that shut. The village houses' interiors and their search are B4's (note 326), the towns' houses B2's (note 281).
    - **Verified:** `SolidWorldTests`:
        - `AShedIsWallsTheCrewGoesInByItsDoorNotThroughItsBack`: from 10 m behind, held at the back wall; from 8 m in front of its door, in to its middle.
        - `TheYardsShutBuildingsAndWellsAreWalls`.
        - `ATunnelsLiningHoldsWhoeverIsInIt`: walking out from the rail in deepTerritory:2's bore for 5 s, held inside it, never lifted.
        - `NobodyWalksUpACuttingsWallButTheFormationIsWalked`.
        - `WhatRunsBesideTheTrainIsInTheBoreOnTheDeckAndOnTheLand`.
        - `WhatsLooseIsOutOfTheBuildingsAndOnTheLand`: a Ribbit put down 6 m up in a shut building is out of it and on the ground; the Choir is out of it, still in the air.
        - `AGauntSleepsInItsRoostAndWalksOutOfItAwake`.
    - **Others' tests the walls met:** `CraneTests` and `StopCrewTests` (the foundry's crane stand in a shed, above), `SpawnSiteTests.TheWhistlerCarriesItsVictimToTheStopsNestAndThroughNoWall` (B4's, above), `LeftBehindPressureTests` (the fort's gate pier, above). The Sim and Game suites.
        - `TheWhistlersRunToItsNestGoesThroughNoBuilding`.
280. **The cab facing forward, run by one (queue #15, C1; the director, 7 Oct 2026: "I don't like the new design, I feel like the controls and firebox need to be in front not facing the back"; then "I like firebox at the front but no need to turn around for coal, the whole cab being operable by one person … the rest of the crew is gunners and labourmen. Remove role names on lockers").** Note 276's cab put the firebox in its back wall, where the boiler comes through: the driver faced the line and the fireman faced the other way.
    - **The front of the cab is the work** (`EnginePlan`, train.json `geometry.engine`). Across it under the windows, from left to right:
        - The coal bunker, in the front left corner and back along the left wall (`bunkerLength` 1.8, `bunkerDepth` 0.62). Its gate is low in its inner side, just behind the firebox.
        - The firebox, standing against the front wall under the sill (`fireboxWidth` 0.96, `fireboxDepth` 0.7, `fireboxHeight` 1.05; `PartKind.Firebox`, a solid). Its door faces back into the cab.
        - The driver's console under the right-hand window.
        - The blow-off cock on the right side wall a step behind the console. Its pipe goes up the side window's post, so it isn't in front of the line.
    - **Reach.** One person stood behind the fire door has the coal at the left hand, the fire ahead, the levers a step to the right and the vent a step further, and never turns round (`CabSightTests.OnePersonRunsTheCabFacingForwardTheCoalTheFireAndTheControlsInReach`). Driving already worked from anywhere in the cab (`CabControls.CanDrive`).
    - **The firebox's frame** (`TrainKit.BackheadFrame`) is now the engine's own, set at the firebox's face. It carries the shut door, the fire seen through the hole, the furnace's light, the Stoker in the fire and the firebox camera.
    - **The art.** The backhead's full-height plate, its four gauges and the modelled fittings (`cab_backhead`) would stand in the windows at the front, so they're gone. In their place is a squat riveted firebox: a firebrick-lined firehole, the door's frame and hinges, the water glass, the ashpan damper, and a steam pipe up the front wall. The driver's four dials over the right window are the one set now. The back wall is plated across where the boiler's end was. The Stoker in an open door is turned to look out of it at the cab.
    - **The crew is the driver, gunners and labourers.** `BotCrew` makes no fireman bot. T75's fireman, a second `ConductorBot` in crews of six or more, goes, and that place is a labourer now. `ConductorBot { Fireman = true }` stays for a player-made second hand, and its tests stand. GDD §12's roles table is now Driver, Gunner and Labourer.
    - **The lockers are numbered 1–12** (train.json `kit.lockers.names`). The kit's locker is 8 (`kitLocker`), and the stock goes by number. The HUD says "LOCKER 8".
    - **Knock-ons.**
        - `PlayerMotor.CabFloorZ` puts a spawn on the open floor between the bunker's end and the doorways.
        - The cab's hatch ladder up to the gun is behind the bunker (the front left corner is the coal's).
        - The bots fire from behind the door facing forward (`ConductorBot.FiringSpot`, `FacingFire` 0) and step across to the vent (`VentWay`).
        - With a Climber in the cab, the driver keeps to the front right corner and a second hand to the back left (`KeepClear`).
    - **Views:** `fireman` looks forward from behind the work at the coal, the fire door, the console, the dials and the line. `firebox` looks into the open door.
    - **Verified:** Sim suite green, apart from the locker, vent, firing-spot and kit-position tests restated for the new places. Game suite: `CabSightTests` (the line from 8 m past the plough unchanged, plus the one-person test above). Looked at: fireman, cab, firebox and engine.
284. **The bend's stress heard building, and main's synth sounds on the audio checklist (AU1, queue #20; build 1121, the director: "we'll want to telegraph using sound design that the train is going under stress").** Note 265 made the stress a telegraph (the flange squeal up to the board, the creaks, the slack's lurch, the scream over the last half, the cab's bell) and left the bell, the roof warnings (note 260) and five other synth sounds without checklist lines.
    - **`dt audio render --scenario bend [--listener n] [--route r] [--cars n]`** (`AudioBench.RenderBend`): `Staging.BendWarning`'s train on deepTerritory:2's first bend that can derail it, at its board until the engine's on the bend, then up steadily over 8 s to 1.1× its derailing speed and held there until it comes off. It reports, a second at a time, the speed, the stress (`TrackRules.Assess`), whether the warning's up, each of `AudioBench.StressSounds`' levels and the mix; a WAV and a spectrogram beside it.
    - **What it found** (the cab, 6 cars, board 38 km/h, derailing at 45.5): the flange squeal 23 dB under the mix as the bend began (−41.6 dB against −18.7) and silent most of its loop (three swells in 10 s); the scream one held chord, so nothing built.
    - **Changed:**
        - New candidates `bed-wheel-rail.flange.sing` (a squeal that holds, never dropping out) and `state-derail.flange-scream.shriek` (four wheels beating against each other, the contact chattering), both real bell and plate metal frozen into held rings (`tools/audio/recipes/stress.py`). They play first (install.py `FIRST_CHOICE`) until the director keeps one.
        - The scream climbs two semitones with the stress: `GameAudio.BedWheels` sets a "stress" param, the scream's share of the stress's last half; install.py's `LAYER_EXTRAS` puts the rate (0.94 → 1.06) on it, on every candidate.
        - The squeal 8 dB up (`CUE_GAIN_DB`). Not more: it sounds on any bend past 0.35 of its derailing pull, most bends at cruise, so louder is a constant whine, not a warning.
        - After, with #190's cab forward: the squeal −34 dB as the bend begins, the scream −26 → −17 climbing, creaks −22 to −31, the lurch −33, the bell −7, the derail at 13.2 s.
        - #207 (one night length) moved deepTerritory:2's bends: the first that can derail the train is now boarded 59 km/h and derails at 70.6. There, the squeal at its loudest is −28 dB against a −13 dB mix, the scream −24 → −15, the bell −12, the derail at 10.3 s.
    - **Main's synth sounds on the checklist:** eight lines (the line's warnings `warn-overspeed`, `warn-curve`, `warn-low-clearance`; `crew-gun-lay`; `crew-cannon-impact`; `crew-noisy-toys`; `place-depot`; `ui-stranded-outro`), two candidates a cue (`recipes/warnings.py`, `recipes/toys_outro.py`). install.py's `SWAPS` (line.cue → the game's sound and the param it drives) swaps the picked takes in as `TELL_SOUNDS` does for the tells, keeping the synth's tier and range; `swaplevel.py` puts them at the synth's loudness (`SWAP_GAIN_DB`), which main tuned its mix against. The toys go by note 174's test instead (carried on a roof, within 0.8 dB of each other, 10 dB over the wind): a squeaker that squeaks now and then and a music box's decaying plucks measure quieter than their loudness says. Not the gun's laying: merged with D1's note 329 (the director, App. F.3: "a weird high repeated sound when the cannon turns"), these candidates were that too (ten chuffs and fifteen gear teeth a second), so `gun-lay` stays main's low, slow synth until a candidate low and slow is kept; `crew-gun-lay` is L0 till then.
    - **install.py fixes:** a cue with no first choice keeps its candidate order (a library candidate's missing key matched the missing choice and jumped the built one: `bed-wheel-rail.roll-fast` had gone to a library loop); a definition that says the same isn't rewritten, so files main tidied by hand keep their notes.
    - **Verified:** `AudioTests.ABendTakenTooFastIsHeardBuildingInOrderFromTheCab` (the squeal before the scream before the bell, the squeal within 20 dB of the cab's mix, the scream 4 dB louder at the end than the start, the bell only while warned); `AudioTests`, `CrewAudioTests`, `EndingSoundTests`, `MusicManifestTests` 62/62.

285. **The HUD: your hands and the dark (B3; the director, 7 Oct 2026: "UI/UX needs a serious overhaul. There's too much UI on screen. I like the way Repo and Lethal Company do their UI/UX designs").** In the cab in the yard, nine things were on screen at once, each on a riveted iron plate at the HUD's full size: the engine panel, the route strip, the link block, "NO RADIO", the cold line, the noise meter, the driving prompt, the night block and the hotbar, plus the lobby list for a networked night. (A 5×7 font on the 480×270 canvas is 28 screen pixels a letter at 1080p.) Note 277 took the panel off out of the cab and put the prompt in fine print. This note takes the rest down to what Lethal Company and R.E.P.O. keep. The design is GDD §32 "The HUD: your hands and the dark".
    - **What those two do, and the rules taken from them:**
        - Always there: a dot to aim with and your hands (Lethal Company's four slots, R.E.P.O.'s three). Nothing else.
        - What you're looking at is said at the crosshair, short. What you're holding lets you do is said in a corner in small print (Lethal Company's "Drop : [G]").
        - The rest comes up when it matters, then goes: Lethal Company's clock only outdoors, a moon's name once on landing; R.E.P.O.'s haul goal at the extraction point.
        - The world says it first: the ship's monitor and terminal, R.E.P.O.'s map as a thing you hold. Here that's the cab's gauges and run map (note 276), the route card (C), the supplies (I) and the roster (Q).
        - No frames in play: text sits on the picture with a shadow.
    - **Element by element** (`Hud`, `Hud.Hands`):
        - **The engine panel** is gone. The driver gets the speed as the corner's head (the one number read against the boards); the rest is the backhead's gauges.
        - **The route strip** is gone. The next place's name comes up at the top centre for `placeSeconds` once it's within `placeAheadMetres` (`Hud.Ahead`, the landmarks `NextPlace` reads). The route card pencils where the train is on its profile (`PlanHud.RouteCard(..., at)`).
        - **The link:** in the lobby the ping stays big (spec E: "shown prominently in browser and lobby"), with PING TO HOST under it. On the line it shows only past `pingWarnMs`, or when the link's lost, with what's being done about it. The host shows nothing. The crew's count and roles are the roster's.
        - **The radio:** "NO RADIO" and "RADIO [T]" are gone. A radio you wear is a slot of its own at the hotbar's right, with its key; a broken one is drawn red. With no radio, nothing is drawn.
        - **The cold step** is said at the top centre for `coldSeconds` when you go into a deeper one. The countdown once you're chilled stays an alarm.
        - **The noise meter** shows only once the crew's at `noiseShowAt` of the Choir's threshold, or while the Choir's gathering or here.
        - **The driving prompt** moved to the corner (`Hud.Hints`): the brake, the vent and the lamp, and the reverser only when it's in reverse. Carrying something, the corner says what it is, what it's for, and put down and throw. Sat at the gun, its shot, fire and get up. At the crane, its controls. `Hud.Prompt` is now only what's in front of you; carrying, it's null (Use puts the thing down).
        - **The night block** is gone. The dawn clock comes up at the top centre in the last `dawnClockSeconds`. What a stop's waiting on is top left in fine print while the train's at one, and the solo yard's way out is there too. The route's name, the next place and IN TUNNEL are dropped.
        - **The hotbar** is small squares at the bottom centre. Each has an 11×11 picture of its tool (`Hud.Pictures`) and its number in the corner, and the one in hand is lit. The tool's name shows for `toolNameSeconds` after a change of hands. With something in both hands, the slots dim.
        - **The lobby** is fine print, top left, with no plate.
        - **The crosshair** is a dot, with four dots round it when something under it can be used.
        - **Alarms** have a double-size headline only when urgent: a rupture counting, a grab, a bend you're coming off on, a tunnel mouth. Others are at the HUD's size. What to do is in fine print with keycaps.
        - **The dead** get no plate: DEAD is big and the rest is fine print. The ballot is fine print on a dark backing, lit along its top while there's a vote to cast.
        - **The panels you open** (supplies, roster, route card) and the run's end keep their plates: you asked for them.
