    - **Timings** are in `content/tuning/hud.json` (`HudTuning`; `Hud.Tuning`, loaded by the app and `dt screenshot`). A thing pops up at once, as a call should, and fades over `fadeSeconds`. The HUD remembers per session what changed and when (`Hud.Memory`, on the session's tick), so a still frame and a test see what a player would at that moment.
    - **VR** passes `pixels: 2`, so the panel's fine print is the HUD's own size (`PromptScaleAt`). Nothing else changes for the headset.
    - **Round two (the director on the overhaul, 7 Oct 2026).** "Keep: speed numbers, pull chord, setting to hide corner controls, max speed on rail sections on the map that can't handle top speed without derailment. Discard: long prompts that foretell the consequence of actions. Consequences need to be learned."
        - **Prompts are an action and its key**, Lethal Company's form: "PULL CORD : [E]", "SHOVEL COAL : HOLD [E]", "THROW TO THE SPUR : HOLD [E]". A short state only when it stops you ("POINTS HELD", "NO SHOT", "OUT OF RHYTHM"), and a hold's "(40%)", which the prompt's bar is drawn from.
        - **Nothing foretells.** Gone: LOUD, QUIETLY, SILENT, (FASTER), (SLOWER), IT NEEDS TWO, (CRANE LOADING), the kit that "MENDS IT", KEEP AT IT, GET CLEAR, BRING A LAMP, "THEY HEAR YOU AT THE DOOR", "STRANDED WHEN SHE STOPS", "GO QUIET", "SHOUT FOR HELP" and the like. The corner says what's carried and how to put it down, not what it's for. `RepairKitWhere` says where the kit is ("REPAIR KIT: THE FITTER'S LOCKER, CAR 1"), not what it does. A stop's status (`PrototypeSession.SiteStatus`) says what's there and what's under way ("crates on the platform", "winch STALLED"), not how to work it; its parts are joined with "; " so the HUD gives each a line.
        - **Kept:** the hazard telegraphs (note 260's tunnel mouth and bend, note 265's bend in the cab, the rupture countdown) keep their warnings and speed figures; only their how-to tails are cut down to a key. The dead's ballot is unchanged (it's a menu).
        - **The speed stays a figure** in the cab's corner (decided). The powered points' lever says its limit as a figure too ("POINTS IN 120 M: UNDER 18 KM/H").
        - **CONTROL HINTS** (`Settings.ControlHints`, on by default; the settings screen's row under HUD): off, the corner keeps its head (the speed, what's in your hands) and drops the keys. The crosshair's prompts stay.
        - **Every stretch that derails under top speed is on the map.** `PostedSpeeds` put a demand's board on the sharpest bend after it, and stopped at the straight. An S-bend has a limit on each curve and one board before both, so its second curve had no figure: on deepTerritory:2, 190 m at 33.3 km would come off at 79 km/h with nothing on the card or the cab's map. Now each curve limit of a board's figure in its reach is inked; a board with none is still for the bend it stands before.
        - **Main's prompts since, in this form** (F1, folding #201 and #202 into #217, B3's readings on #217): #201's shovel is "HANG THE SHOVEL BACK : [E]", with "THE SHOVEL IS OUT" and "HANDS FULL" as plain state. #202's healing find in hand is the corner's: its name as the head, and "USE : HOLD [E]" over PUT DOWN and THROW, only when you're hurt with nothing else in reach (`Hud.CanHeal`). At the crosshair only the use under way, "USING IT (50%)". Gone: "(+N WHEN HURT)", "INTO ANY CAR TO KEEP IT" and "(+N)". `HudTests.AHealingFindInHandSaysHoldUseWhenYoureHurt`.
        - **Verified:** `HudTests.PromptsNameTheActionAndItsKeyAndNeverWhatItDoes` (every cab control, the vent held, the kit's locker shut and open, the kit carried: each key is an action's, nothing foretold, at most 48 characters), the restated prompt tests, `QuietHudTests.WithTheControlHintsOffTheCornerKeepsOnlyWhatItsAbout`, `FrontEndTests.SettingsAreSavedAsTheyChange` (the row), and `MapSpeedTests` (four tiers: every 5 m that derails under top speed has a figure, and each figure is under its bend's derailing speed; a sweep of 24 lines, four tiers by six seeds, had none bare).
    - **Not yet / the director's call:**
        - Health isn't drawn. The damage model's edge flash and sound (note 272) are the feedback, as in Lethal Company.
        - ~~The supplies and roster panels are still riveted plates at the HUD's size.~~ Done, note 316.
        - ~~The settings take effect from the next night, as the rest do (the app reads them as a night starts).~~ Done, note 292: the in-night menu's settings take effect at once.
    - **Verified:** `QuietHudTests`:
        - on a roof with empty hands, only the crosshair and the hotbar are drawn;
        - a change of hands is named, then gone;
        - the ping is big in the lobby, and on the line only when bad or lost;
        - a place is named coming up, then gone;
        - the noise meter shows only when loud;
        - hud.json is the record's defaults.

      `HudTests` pins the prompt and corner split. Before and after shots at 1080p (`dt screenshot --hud --scale 4`) were looked at: the cab, the roof under a tunnel warning, the cab's bend warning, a locker with the kit in hand, the dead with a ballot, the lobby, the cold, the supplies, the cord.

286. **Boarding-first across the roster, the Switchman's lines that lead nowhere, and the Fire Flies' credit (the director's decisions of 6 and 7 Oct 2026, GDD App. F.1; queue #22 and #24, A1.8).** The GDD's words: "Nothing acts inside the train unless it boarded. Players must be able to understand or learn the rule for how each creature gets on." "Each creature has its own boarding rule at a specific, known point, with a telegraph and a counter." "Slowing opens the doors. Stops, facilities and tight curves are where things board." "Shut doors stop some boarders, not all. Some creatures can open, force or get around doors, each by its own rule." And on 7 Oct: "The switch itself shouldn't cause derail, it should be lines that lead nowhere." (First numbered 281; renumbered, 281 being the towns session's.)
    - **The roster, creature by creature.** Where each gets on, what tells you, what answers it, and what a shut door does to it. **Changed** marks what this note changed; the rest was already so (notes 263, 268, 269, 271 and before).

        | Creature | Boarding point | Telegraph | Counter | A shut door |
        |---|---|---|---|---|
        | Track Doll | The rail ahead: struck by the train, she haunts it (the director's exception: an apparition) | White face in the headlamp; aboard, the giggle, restless before each stage (note 268) | Stop short or shoot her on the rail; aboard, mind her, a toy, or corner and club her | Nothing: she's a haunting |
        | Cinder Hounds | The rear car's roof, leaping from the line at a train under their 19 m/s | The howl behind, closing (4 s) | Outrun them over 19 m/s, or a rear cannon round; aboard, the pack fight, or cut the car loose | Nothing: they ride the roof, and their fires come through it |
        | Car Hugger | The rear car's end, from a marsh or bridge it lurks at (twice as likely under 8 m/s) | Heavy grinding at the rear, the speed capped | Cut the caboose, or club it as a group | Nothing: it eats through the end wall (a breach) |
        | Draggers | **Changed:** under a car's edge, only with the train under `draggers.boardBelow` (14 m/s): a stop, or a slow bend (`bendWeight` 2 on a tight one). They wait there for a roof walker | A limb over the lip, the scrape (1 s) | Stay off the edges; haul a friend back up; keep her over 50 km/h and none get on | Nothing: they're outside, under the lip |
        | Whistler | A coupling gap, at a stop | The whistle with no hand on the cord, at the next stop | Check the gaps after the whistle; move in pairs at stops | Nothing: it lives in the gap |
        | Climbers | **Changed:** the coupling gaps, getting a grip only with the train under `climbers.mountBelow` (14 m/s). Faster, the pack runs alongside, pacing it, for `waitForSlowSeconds` (30) and gives up; the director sends them at speed at `atSpeedWeight` (0.25), and slow on a tight bend (`tightBendRadius` 350 m under or 300 m ahead) at `bendWeight` (3) | The pack pacing the train; the scrabble at the gap (2.5 s) | Keep her over 50 km/h, or hold the gaps (outnumber them) as she takes the bend; club any that mount | Unchanged (decided 1 Oct): a dark car they force through the roof (a breach), a lit empty one they open. `litShutCarKeepsOut` (off) would keep them out of a lit car shut up tight: **the director's call** |
        | Stoker | The coal bunker, drawn by a firebox over 4.5 for 20 s (note 263) | On the coal with a sick glow, then across the footplate (8 s) | Club it on the way in; once in, vent and starve, or hose it (note 271) | The firebox door is its door: opened on it, the heavy burn |
        | Tippy Toesie | **Changed:** slips aboard only at a stop (`tippyToesie.boardBelow` 0.3 m/s), then hidden aboard till it's fled three times. Before, it appeared behind an idle player anywhere, at any speed: something acting inside that never boarded | Faint tiptoeing behind you | Don't stand still alone; look at it; a friend pulls it off | Nothing: it opens doors without a sound |
        | Fire Flies | A lit car lamp, only while the train's stopped (note 269); **changed:** only a car with a way in (`fireFlies.shutCarKeepsOut`: a door or the hatch open, or a breach) | The buzzing glow round the lamp (20 s) | The lamp out, get under way, or shut the car up at a stop | **Changed:** a car shut up tight keeps them off its lamp |
        | Ribbits | Never board: the ground at yards and villages | Throats swelling | Never be outnumbered; get aboard | — |
        | The Gaunt | Follows its waker aboard, at arm's length | It stirs as you near; its lean as its anger climbs | Keep talking; kill it as a group; or lead it to a car, where it takes the best thing and goes | Nothing: it opens a door to leave with what it took |
        | Followers | On a crewmate's back, from the facility grounds | The lump on a back, seen by friends | Check each other's backs; club it off, or the nest | Nothing: it's carried in |
        | Soot Children | Never board as themselves (a real child is carried aboard as cargo) | The call; the eyes from five metres | Check the eyes from five metres | — |
        | The Passenger | The rearmost car with a room, during a facility stop | Silence: it never speaks | Make everyone speak; kill it as a crew | Nothing: it opens doors, as crew do |
        | Grumbler | Craned aboard with a crate | Gnawing on the crates | A spotter checks the crates before each lift; gang up or leave it alone | Nothing: it comes in the crane's load |
        | The Choir | Never boards: it seizes whoever's outside, on the roofs or behind no shut door | Layered voices, multiplying as it gathers | Hush; shut every door | A shut door is its counter |
        | The Switchman | Never boards: it works a dead line's points ahead. **Changed** (below): it never derails the train by its switch | The figure at the lever, the lamp wrong (300 m); the cab's dead-line lines and bell | Kill it before the points (**changed:** its lever falls back); or stop and set them back by hand; or stop short of the dead line's end | — |

    - **Slow on a tight bend** (`Enemies/Boarding.cs`): `Boarding.OnTightBend` reads the line's curvature under the train and `bendAheadM` ahead of it the way it's going, from the train and the line alone, so every machine agrees. A frontier line's tightest bend (`minRadius` 300 m) is boarded at 14 m/s, under the Climbers' grip, so a driver who reads the boards opens the door there; on frontier:7, whose sharpest bend is 707 m (note 265), the slow places are the stops and the facilities until B1's bends (queue #13) land. Climbers keep their `minSpeed` (5 m/s): they board a moving train, never a standing one.
    - **The Switchman** (the director's decision of 7 Oct 2026; enemies.json `switchman.throwsUnderTrain`, false). The reading that keeps the spec's own tables true: linegen plan §6.3 already says "a switch the Switchman threw costs the clock, never the train", and C.9's Switchman row stays (it names the forward cannon). So no Switchman throws points under the train any more (the derailing kind and its `derailChance` draw stay behind the flag for a mod; the director's dice are still drawn, so the rest of the night runs as it did). Every Switchman throws the dead line's points ahead, the train goes down a line that leads nowhere, and the crew stop, back out and set the points back by hand (the bots already do: `StopCrew`'s `OffDeadLine`, `SetBack`).
        - **A dead line's end** (`Train/DeadEnds.cs`; train.json `overspeed.deadEndDerailAbove`, 6.9 m/s, 25 km/h). Its buffers hit over that, and the train goes through them and off the end: "ran off the end of the dead line the Switchman threw it down, at 36 km/h (over 25 km/h it goes through the buffers)". It's the bend warning's rule (note 265): the cab's warning goes up when the buffers are within the distance to stop under the limit (the same `WarnDistance`: 4 s at the speed now, a service stop at 0.6 of the rated brake, 30 m), the host counts its seconds (`World.DeadEndWarnSeconds`), and the derail commits only after a full lead (4 s). A hit short of that is the buffer stop's damage alone, counted in `World.DeadEndsSpared`. Only dead lines (`BranchKind.DeadLine`): facility spurs keep their buffers' damage. C.9: down a line a Switchman threw (`World.SwitchmanThrew`), the forward cannon, as the row says; any other dead line, the throttle.
        - **Told in the cab** (`Hud.DeadEndLines`): down a dead line, "DOWN A DEAD LINE / THE LINE ENDS IN 2992 M. STOP, BACK UP, SET THE POINTS BACK BY HAND"; within the warning, flashing, "BUFFERS AHEAD: THE LINE ENDS / END OF THE LINE IN 96 M, OFF IT OVER 25 KM/H. YOU'RE AT 36: BRAKE", and the bend warning's bell (`GameAudio.BendWarning`). From the line and the train on each machine: nothing new on the wire.
        - **Killed before the points, its lever falls back** (`switchman.killedSetsBack`): "kill the Switchman before the switch" now means what it says. A cannon round or three blows while it's at the lever and the train's short of the points sets them back for the main line.
        - **A bug found and fixed:** the routing Switchman threw its points every tick it waited, and `World.SetSwitch` returns false for a switch already set, so it went the tick after it threw: the lamp read wrong with nobody at the lever to see or shoot (the baseline night's Switchman was such a one). It throws once now and waits there. Not a switch-mechanics bug (A1.11's #26): the Switchman's own.
    - **The Fire Flies' credit** (queue #24; `IncidentLog.FireFliesDrawn`). Car lamps start lit (note 269), so C.9's line "Nobody lit that lamp." came every time. It says what drew them now, in the clerk's voice: "Drawn by the car's lamp, lit since the yard." or "Drawn by the car's lamp, relit by {actor}.", and the way in: "Door left open.", "Hatch left open." or "In through the breach.". A burn death in a car names "Lamp lit since the yard." or "Lamp out." where it said "Nobody lit that lamp.".
    - **The bubbles** (`CreatureArt.FireFlies`). Looked at in `dt screenshot --threats --view flies`: the moths' wing rims (`ember_core.firefly_rim`, emissive) were lit all round while the wings themselves were dark against the lamp, so each moth on the wing drew as a hollow orange ring: a bubble. Drawn now with the rims as the wings' charred paper (`FireFlyLook`, unlit) and the tail's ember brighter, and each moth on the wing sheds `FireFlySparks` (3) sparks behind it along its loop, falling and dimming: embers round the lamp. The model is unchanged (`art check` within every budget). The ceiling's round rivet heads are lit the same orange near the lamp; if the director meant those, they're C1's.
    - **Not yet / the director's call:**
        - Climbers and a lit car shut up tight (`litShutCarKeepsOut`, off): on, every car leaves the yard lit and shut, so they'd go over every car to the cab. Off, as decided 1 Oct.
        - The numbers are first guesses: 14 m/s (50 km/h) for the Climbers' grip and the Draggers' boarding, a 350 m tight bend, the dead line's 25 km/h.
        - The Hounds, the Hugger, the Gaunt, the Passenger and the Grumbler already had a boarding point; no door rule was added to them (shut doors don't stop them, each for its own reason in the table).
        - Whether the dead line's end should be boarded on the line (an end-of-line board, buffers drawn in the headlamp): the cab's lines and the bell tell it now; the lineside isn't this note's.
    - **Harness** (`dt harness --route frontier:7 --bots 8 --enemies --seconds 600`). Before this work (main at the start, 13:05 UTC): 6.46 km, 4 deaths (all burned), 4 sends (a Climber, Cinder Hounds, Fire Flies, a Switchman), punishes CarFire 4 and CinderHound 2, beats/min 4.2, longest quiet 22.4 s, quiet share 0.13, max correction 0.40 m. Main as merged (D1's #212, #213, #215 and the rest in, without this note): 7.51 km, 0 deaths, 11 sends (3 Tippy Toesies at speed, 4 Draggers, 2 Climbers, Fire Flies, a Switchman), beats/min 4.6, longest quiet 45.3 s, quiet share 0.68, max correction 0.34 m. With this note: 6.83 km, 1 death (dragged off a roof by a Dragger), 11 sends (4 Draggers and 4 Climbers boarding on the slow stretches, Fire Flies to a car left open at a stop, the Track Doll, a Switchman), punishes Dragger 2 and Switchman 1 (the train down the dead line: the clock's cost), no Tippy Toesie (no idle crewmate alone at a stop), no derailment, fairness violations 0, beats/min 5.1, longest quiet 67.5 s, quiet share 0.81, max correction 0.24 m. The km lost is the dead line; the longer quiets are the cruise between the places things board, which is the decision's "relative break" (a pacing call for the director's pressure tuning, note 266, if it's too long).
    - **Verified:** `BoardingFirstTests` (Climbers pacing a fast train never mount and give up; slowed, they get on, fairly; the director's weights at speed, slow and on a tight bend; the flag's lit shut car kept out and an open door let in; a dark shut car still forced; Draggers only on a slow train, waiting dormant; Tippy Toesie only at a stop; a train shut up tight draws no Fire Flies and an open lit car does). `SwitchmanDeadLineTests` (no Switchman throws under the train by default; it throws the junction ahead and the train goes down the dead line, fairly; running off the end derails it only after a full lead of the cab's warning, and says so; a driver who brakes 3.5 s into the warning at 18 m/s stops short; shot before the points, its lever falls back and the train stays on the main line; buffers hit short of the lead are the buffer stop alone). `IncidentEventTests` (the Fire Flies' line, the way in). Updated: `DraggerTests.TheDirectorPutsThemUnderTheCarsOnlyOnASlowTrainAndTheyWaitForSomeoneOnTheRoofs` (was "only with someone on the roofs"), `BoardingRuleTests` (an open door for the Fire Flies), `AuditTests` (the insisted Fire Flies need a way in; the look-out's walk to a Dragger under any car gets 60 s). `DerailCauseTests` keep the old under-train throw, as a mod has it. No spec test pins any of these numbers; the spec's tables are unchanged.

287. **The night's first threat is drawn by something a crewmate did, the dark answers it, and the report names it (queue #23, A1.9; GDD App. F.1 second session: "Run start: nothing makes the player feel they've done something that draws a monster they need to worry about", T131; §14 "Noise", §23.1 "Owned", C.9; design decision, 2026-10).** Note 266's pressure already rose with loudness and cargo, but nothing the crew could see or hear tied the first threat to anything they'd done: it came when the quiet had built the pressure to 10, whatever anyone did. Now the first threat follows a draw, and the crew is told.
    - **The draw ledger** (`Enemies/Draws.cs`, `Director.Draws`, host-side, a `SortedDictionary` by cause then player, so every read is deterministic): each crewmate's draws by cause, fading by half about every `halfLifeSeconds` 30 (first-order, plain arithmetic, the same bits on every OS). The acts are credited where they happen in `World`: the whistle (only a crewmate's pull; the Whistler's is nobody's) 1.5 /s; a raised voice, the mic level above `voiceFloor` 0.4 scaled to the rest, 0.5 /s at full (the bots' working chatter, 0.27, never draws); a noisy toy carried 0.15 /s; a cannon round 3; a car lamp lit 2. Once a second `Director.Listen` adds the states: the firebox above `fireboxFrom` 4.5 (of 6, the Stoker's own heat) 0.25 /s at full, to whoever tended it last (`Attribution.Tender`); the engine at speed 0.03 /s at `engineFullSpeed` 20 m/s, to whoever drove (at most about 1.3 stands, so it never answers alone); cargo come aboard, 4 a car-load × note 266's cargo value, to the crewmate nearest that car (what she left the fortress with isn't counted). Nothing is credited in the safe yard (note 263).
    - **The answer.** After the grace and before the first threat, the first time one crewmate's draw of one kind stands at `answerAt` 3 (a proper whistle blast of two seconds, one cannon round, six seconds of shouting, a car-load aboard), the director answers it. `World.Answer` (replicated on the world record, protocol 34; 33 is F1's emotes, note 298) holds it for `showSeconds` 7 at a point `answerDistance` 60 m out from the engine's nose the way the lamp shines, `answerLateral` 12 m to a side (alternating by the second), 0.7 m off the ground. Every machine hears a call from there (`GameAudio.Answer`: the audio chat's hook `tell-draw.<cause>` when it's installed, until then the pack's `hound-howl`, distant) and sees a pair of eyes at the lamp's edge (`Effects.Eyes`: eyeshine, green-gold, open, one blink, gone before the threat; `dt screenshot --view cab --answer 4`). The threat follows `leadSeconds` 5 later, pressed for (the cooldown and the budget's curve give way as at `pressAt`), and what the draw calls weighs more for it (`answers`: the whistle the Whistler ×3 and hounds ×2; a cannon hounds, Ribbits, Climbers ×2; voices Soot Children ×3, Tippy Toesie and Followers ×2; a toy the Track Doll ×4; the firebox hounds ×2; a lamp the Fire Flies ×3; cargo the Car Hugger ×3, Grumbler and hounds ×2). Only what the night could send anyway: its gates, caps and roster hold.
    - **Listening.** With no draw that big, the pressure past its threshold waits (`HeldBecause` "listening") until `holdUntil` 16 (the same as `pressAt`), and then the biggest draw standing takes it: a quiet crew buys itself time (§14: "sometimes the correct response to a monster is to go quiet"). The Stoker is the firebox's own draw (note 263: drawn by heat), in the last tender's name; the Choir, if it comes first, the loudest's (A.7), by whichever of their noises was biggest.
    - **Owned** (C.9, §23.1): `IncidentKind.Drawn` (appended; not an "event" for the punish bookmarks), written once by `Director.Came`: "Cinder Hounds came first at km 2. Drawn by the whistle: Dave." (the clerk's names: "The Track Doll came first…", "Drawn by the engine's noise: Dave."). The director writes the line and never reads the log. The harness report has `firstThreat` (run seconds, after the grace, km, kind, cause, actor, the draw, answered and when, the report's line).
    - **Ambiguities, read:** "the loudest/most drawing recent action" is one crewmate's one kind of draw, not a crew's sum, so it has a name; the GDD's "no fixed timers" holds (the answer and the lead are sim seconds of the host's, after a draw, not a clock). "Eyes in the treeline" is at the lamp's edge wherever the lamp is; there may be no trees. The Choir meter's first tick wasn't used: it's HUD-less already and F1 owns the UI. All of it is in `enemies.json` `director.draw`; `enabled` false is note 266 exactly (the harness's before), `holdFirst` false keeps the answer but not the wait.
    - **Measured** (`dt harness --route frontier:7 --bots 8 --enemies --seconds 600`, this branch, the draw off against on; grace 28.4 s):

      | | draw off (before) | on (after) |
      |---|---|---|
      | first threat (run s; after the grace) | 66.7; 38.3 | 94.7; 66.3 |
      | what came | Climbers | Climbers |
      | drawn by | (nothing named) | the engine's noise: Crew 1 (the driver bot), not answered |
      | director's sends in 600 s | 11 | 10 |
      | held "listening" (s) | — | 28 |
      | deaths | 0 | 0 |

      The bots draw nothing a crew would: they chatter under the voice floor, don't whistle, fire only at threats, and kept the firebox under 4.5 here, so a bot night is the quiet crew, listened for until the pressure pressed, and the engine takes it. The answered path is pinned by `DrawTests` (a two-second blast after the grace: the eyes and the call at once, 60 m out; the threat 5 s later; the report's "Drawn by the whistle: Dave.").
    - **Not yet:** the bots don't whistle or shout, so harness nights never see an answer; a driver bot's two toots at the gate would make one. The answer's own sounds (`tell-draw.*`) are the audio chat's. A grab or death by the first threat doesn't repeat the draw in its own line (the Drawn line sits before it in the report). Later threats aren't attributed: the ledger keeps running, if they're wanted.
    - Tests: `DrawTests` (the whistle answered and followed; a quiet crew listened for, sooner without the hold; switched off nothing named; the same night the same first threat; the ledger's fade and tie-break; cargo in the nearest crewmate's name); `RejoinTests` and `CrewCapTests` pin protocol 34; the director's weights tests that spend at once (`Tuning.Eager`: conflict seeding, roster, cargo, Climbers, Draggers) take `Tuning.Unheld` (`holdFirst` false). Sim suite 953: the 7 of those failed on the hold before it, all green after.

288. **Driven off by their rules, killed by the crew together (queue #25, A1.10; GDD App. F.1's damage model, "creatures mostly don't take damage; they're driven off by their rules", and the director's clarification of 7 Oct 2026: "They should be driven off by rules but they should also be able to be killed like in Lethal Company if the team coordinates effectively").** Note 272's follow-up listed the creatures still killed by blows. The five whose counter was "club it" (the Grumbler, the Gaunt, the Passenger, Climbers and the Choir's ghosts) now have two ways out. Following the rule drives one off: the normal answer, a break, and it can come back. A coordinated team can kill it, which is riskier and costlier, and rewarded: it's done for the night and the incident report names the gang.
    - **The coordinated kill** (`enemies.json` `coordinatedKill`: `gang` 2, `windowSeconds` 5). Each creature's blows wear it down only while two or more different crewmates have struck it within the window (`Enemy.Strikers`, `Ganged`), plus whatever setup its rule asks for. A lone player swinging never kills one. Killed, `Enemy.Slay` writes a `Slain` incident line ("Killed the Grumbler together … By Ana, Ben.") and, for a kind that comes once (the Grumbler, the Gaunt, the Passenger), adds it to `World.Slain`; the director doesn't draw that kind again tonight. A Climber or a ghost is one of many, so a kill takes only that one. Driven off, the Passenger and the talked-down Gaunt go into `World.DrivenOff`, and `SpawnContext.Once` lets that once-a-run kind come again.
    - **Per creature** (each behind its block's `drivenOff`; `false` is the old health fight, kept):

        | Creature | GDD rule (§21, App. A) | Before | Drive-off rule (after) | Coordinated kill | A lone player gets |
        |---|---|---|---|---|---|
        | Grumbler | "Gang up or leave it alone"; A.8 "gang up and kill it, or leave it alone" | 6 blows' health, regenerating 1.5/s unless two had struck it in 5 s; a lone player could barely dent it | Feral, with two or more of the crew within `gangRadius` 3 m of it and no gang striking it, for `outnumberedSeconds` 2: it lets go of a maul, scuttles off for `fleeSeconds` 8, and goes back to gnawing, calmed. Left alone, it never comes off the crates | Blows from two or more crewmates in the window take its 6 health (it still regenerates against one). While they're on it, it fights and bites the last to hit it | Feral at them and no harm to it. A friend's blow still breaks its maul |
        | The Gaunt | "Keep talking to it"; A.6 "kill it (a group job; it hits hard) OR lead it to a car → it takes the most valuable item → leaves for the run" | 8 blows' health, any blow | `talkingCalms`: talk brings its anger down a step every `silenceSeconds` (5), as silence raises it. Calmed under `attackAt` it stops attacking and follows again; calm and talked to for `talkedDownSeconds` 45, it leaves empty-handed (and may wake again tonight). Leading it to a car still works as before | The gang's blows while someone near it keeps talking (a voice over `talkingAbove` within `listenRadius`) take its 8 health. A blow in silence angers it a step instead | Nothing on it. A friend's blow still breaks its crush |
        | The Passenger | "Make everyone speak"; A.8 "interrupt: other crew kill it (the victim can't break free alone)" | 5 blows' health; only killing it freed its victim | Found out: a crewmate's blow (not its victim's) makes it let go, stand `unmaskedSeconds` 2.5 facing them, and bolt off the back of the train at `fleeSpeed` 2.2. It may board again at a later stop | The gang's blows (on it as it's found out, or run down before it's off the back) take its 5 health | One blow frees their friend and drives it off |
        | Climbers | "Outnumber them at the gaps"; A.4 "outnumber them at the gap; bludgeon any that mount" | 3 blows' health, any blow (a ball took it on the roofs) | Up on the roofs or in a car, outnumbered where it is (more crew than Climbers within `countRadius` 8) with no gang striking it, for `outnumberedSeconds` 2: it lets go and drops back off for an untried gap (`Retry`, its `maxTries` as before). A ball that doesn't kill it knocks it off the roof the same way. At the gap, unchanged | The gang's blows take its 3 health. Killed, only that one is gone | A blow knocks it off a friend it holds, no harm to it |
        | Choir ghosts | "Hush, and shut every door"; A.7 "interrupt: kill the one holding them (many hits; they hit back hard)", "DISPERSE quiet held → they leave" | 6 blows' health, and only killing a ghost broke its seize; hushing dispersed the rest but the one holding on kept its catch | A seize breaks when the meter's under its threshold for `hushBreakSeconds` 3 (the ghost goes), or when its catch is behind a shut door (it goes back to the doors). Blows don't break it. The swarm still disperses on `disperseQuietSeconds` and rests `restSeconds` | The gang's blows with the crew holding quiet (meter under threshold) take a ghost's 6 health, and each striker still takes its hit back. The last of the swarm killed and the Choir is spent for the run, as when it takes its one | A hit back for every 3 s of swinging, and nothing else |

    - **Readings.** The Passenger's "found out" is a blow. The truer "make everyone speak" would be a crewmate calling it out (looking at it and talking), but nothing in the voice layer says who's addressed, so a blow stands in for it. The 2.5 s it stands unmasked is the gang's one chance. Without it, a Passenger in the rearmost car was off the back before a second crewmate could swing. The Gaunt's `talkingCalms` answers half of GDD Part Eleven Q9 ("does talking lower its aggro") yes, as a tuning flag. A ball (note 290: a blow by the gunner) rides each creature's blow rule, so a gunner alone is one striker; a ball and a crewmate's blow together are a gang.
    - **Bots.** `Heed.Rescue` no longer swings at a Choir ghost holding someone: its hush (`Heed.Voice`) is the rescue, and a swing only earns the hit back. Everything else already answers by the rule: they go to a held crewmate together (two of the crew drive a Grumbler or a Climber off, a blow drives the Passenger off), and they talk near the Gaunt, which now talks it down.
    - **Presentation.** The cues follow (`PrototypeSession.Cue`): the Passenger's "hit it and it runs" and "found out: it's running for the back", the Grumbler's "backing off: let it be", the Gaunt's "leaving: if it took something, run it down". A ghost let go by quiet is seen leaving as a dispersing one is (`GreyboxScene.Leaving`).
    - **Director's calls.** (1) A ball alone can no longer kill a Climber on the roofs; it knocks it off instead (§21 says no cannon answers the flank; note 171 let it). (2) The Passenger's unmasking by a blow rather than by a voice. (3) Q9: talking lowers the Gaunt's anger (`talkingCalms`), and a talked-down Gaunt may wake again that night. (4) The window and the gang (2 within 5 s) are one number for all five; at a crew of two, the kill takes both of them. (5) Whether a coordinated kill should earn something in the settlement (scrip, a named commendation) beyond the report line: commendations are player-to-player today (D.12). (6) Found in the harness, before and after alike: the bots never answer the Passenger. It takes walkers who are 84–99 m from anyone, and nothing in `Heed` makes a bot keep company or count heads, so one blow would now save them and none lands. That's bot work for a follow-up.
    - **Verified:** `DrivenOffTests` (12: per creature, the drive-off, a lone player's blows doing no harm, and the gang's kill; the old rule kept behind `drivenOff`); tests that pinned the old rule now say so (`HitConfirmTests.ABallOnAGrumblerMaulingACrewmate…`: a gunner alone no longer hurts it; `CargoTests.TheGauntCarriesABodyOut…`: two swing, one talks; `EnemyTests.TheChoirSeizesOnlyWhoeverIsExposed`: the crew stay loud; `AGunnerWhoSprays…`: seized, and his quiet frees him; `BreachTests`, `ChoirShareTests`: who it takes, under the old rule; WP19's `MeleeTests.EachToolLandsItsOwnBlow` measures a tool's blow on a Cinder Hound, since a lone blow no longer wears a Climber down). `AuditTests` (every grab broken at crews 2 and 8) and the Sim suite, NetcodeTests included. `dt audit grabs --only Grumbler,Gaunt,Passenger,Climber,Choir --crews 2,4,8`: all freed, before and after (the Passenger "killed" in 1.5–4.7 s before, "broken off" in 1.2–1.5 s after; the Choir "fled" 3.0 s after, by the hush). `dt harness --route frontier:7 --bots 8 --enemies`, the same build with every `drivenOff` false and then true (600 s night, then 400 s with `--insist` each kind): the night identical (0 deaths, 1 car-fire punish, 0 fairness violations; none of the five engaged); the Choir 1 death (seized) and 1 punish → 0 deaths, 5 grabs all broken by the bots' hush; the Passenger 3 deaths (uncoupled) either way (no bot was within 25 m of the lone walkers it took, 84–99 m off, so nobody struck it); Climbers, the Gaunt and the Grumbler (never drawn: no crane stop in 400 s) no deaths either way; 0 fairness violations everywhere.

289. **The switch audit (queue #26, A1.11; the director, 7 Oct: "audit switches, in a recent playtest I felt like they weren't working").** Everything a switch does, end to end: the generated junctions, the levers, the lamps, the prompts, replication, the facility drill, the bots and the Switchman's hook. The points, the routing and the replication were sound. What was broken was around them: the bots stopping for points set wrong, the Switchman's hook, the prompt at an alternate, and the lock on the branch's leg.

    | Checked | How | Verdict | Fix / test |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | A train takes the route the points are set to, on generated nights | Every branch of 32 line-generator nights (4 tiers × 8 seeds), set for it and run through at 4 m/s | Sound: every branch taken, and the engine's nearest track is the branch | `SwitchTests` (existing) |
    | Alternates rejoin; toes past a rejoin | The 32 nights | Sound: no toe within 600 m past a rejoin, so `TakeSwitches` skipping a rake still coming off an alternate never misses one | none |
    | Lever and lamp on the branch's side, clear of every track | The 32 nights; `dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --junction 1 [--diverge] --stand 1`, `--view cab`, `--cam` | Sound: every lever 2.6 m off the main line on the branch's side, clear of yard tracks; the lamp reads green/red and the lever lies over, from the stand and from the cab | none |
    | The route card's default route | `PlanRoutes.ToRoute`, `LayRouteCard` | Sound: a junction whose main line is washed out starts set for its alternate, and the card says so | none |
    | **The bot driver stops for a dead line set wrong at line speed** | The frontier:7 harness night (8 bots, 9 cars): both Switchmen's dead lines were taken and backed out of (`ToSwitch` then `OffDeadLine`) | **Broken.** `StopDriver` planned stops on half the bare brake. With steam driving (T97) the engine pulls against the brake under the speed its steam makes, so a full-brake stop from 14 m/s takes 112 m, not 64. The driver set off for the points 200 m out and ran 1 m past the toe | `BrakeRate` is half of what the brake does now (fade included), and never more than 0.8 of what it does net of the steam's pull; `StoppingDistance` and `Toward` use it (the cap keeps a slow set-back's closing speed, `RollBackTests`). `SwitchAuditTests.ABotDriverAtLineSpeedStopsShortOfAJunctionSetWrongAhead` (frontier:7, points thrown 600 m ahead at 14 m/s) |
    | **The Switchman's hook, `World.SetSwitch`** | A routing Switchman put at a junction 900 m ahead | **Broken.** `SetSwitch` returned whether the switch moved, so one already set read as "a wheel on the points". The routing Switchman threw the points, then left the next tick: the points stayed wrong, nothing stood at the stand, and nothing reached its telegraph, PUNISH or attribution | `SetSwitch` returns whether the switch now stands as asked (false only under a wheel). The Switchman's code is unchanged (A1.8 owns its behaviour). `SettingASwitchThatIsAlreadySetSaysItIsSet`, `ARoutingSwitchmanStaysAtTheLeverItThrewUntilTheTrainComes` |
    | **The prompt at an alternate's stand** | `Hud.Prompt` on frontier:7's alternate | **Broken.** Anything not a spur was "THE DEAD LINE", so the crew choosing the card's high line was told it was throwing the train down a dead line. The powered thrower's prompt was the same | The alternate goes by the route card's name for it ("THROW TO THE HIGH LINE : HOLD [E]"), "THE ALTERNATE" off a plan. `HudTests.AtAnAlternatesStandThePromptNamesTheRouteCardsLineNotADeadLine` |
    | **The points' lock** | A car stood 3 m inside a spur | **Broken.** Only the main line's leg was counted, so the points went over under a car at the mouth of a branch, which a main-line train then sideswiped | `PointsOccupied` counts a wheel within `pointsLength` on the branch's leg too. `ACarStoodJustInsideTheBranchHoldsThePoints` |
    | A client throws a switch by hand over the wire | Host and two clients on loopback: a client on the ground at the stand holds Use | Sound: the prompt is offered on the thrower's machine, the host throws it, both clients' switches follow, and the train runs down the branch on every machine | `AClientThrowsASwitchByHandAndEveryoneSeesItAndTheTrainTakesIt` (new, passing) |
    | Locked points under a train; the powered thrower | `SwitchTests`, `UpgradeTests`, `HudTests` | Sound | existing |
    | The facility drill and the yard (cut, spur in, load, back out, recouple, set back) | `SpurDrillTests`, `StopCrewTests`' set pieces, `FacilityWork` | Sound | existing |
    | Bots setting a wrong switch back, the driver alone, a cut-off car behind | `StopCrewTests` | Sound once they stop short (above) | existing |

    - **The Switchman (A1.8's, #22; note 286 landed beside this).** Note 286 fixed the same vanishing from the Switchman's side (it checks `Diverging` before it throws), so both fixes stand: the hook now means what its callers read, and the Switchman doesn't lean on it. Reported, not changed:
      - With `switchman.throwsUnderTrain` set (off by default since note 286), the throw "under the train" never moves the points: `SetSwitch` honours the lock, and with the engine over the toe they're locked. The split or derail still happens, but the lamp stays green and the lever doesn't move.
      - While it's `Dormant` it throws the points again whenever they're set back, so a crew that walks out and sets them back before it reveals itself (`revealAt`, 300 m) has them thrown again.
    - **Not yet:** the driver bot doesn't use the powered thrower (note 196). Holding Use at a stand with something to pick up in reach does both: the pick-up and the throw (the HUD offers only the pick-up).
    - The frontier:7 harness night (8 bots, 9 cars, enemies) delivered with no facility stop worked: two Switchman set-backs (75 s and 88 s, each down the dead line and back) ate its slack. Not re-run here after the fix (the machine is shared); `SwitchAuditTests` covers the stop.
    - Protocol unchanged; no tuning changed.

290. **The guns' effect on creatures: every body a ball can meet stops it, and a ball lands as a blow (GDD App. F.1, build 1121: "Bug: the guns do nothing. Rounds don't collide where they land and have no visible effect on the monsters"; queue #28, D1).** Note 171 gave four creatures a hit volume (Cinder Hounds on the line, the Switchman at his lever, Climbers in the open, the Track Doll on the rail), each a single sphere centred at the feet, sized in code. The rest had none "by design", so a ball laid on a Gaunt, a Grumbler, a Ribbit pack or a Whistler carrying a crewmate went straight through it and came down on the ground behind. A ball that did find one of the four, and didn't kill it, did nothing at all in the sim.
    - **Bodies.** `enemies.json` `bodies`: every creature's body as a stack of spheres, each [radius, height over where it stands], fitted to its model as drawn (`content/art/models`; the Ribbit at its 1.4 scale). A tall thing is three or four spheres up its height (the Switchman 1.8 m, the Gaunt 3.5 m), so a ball laid on its shoulders no longer passes over a sphere at its feet. A long, low one (a hound, a Climber, the Whistler) is one sphere round its middle. A sleeping Gaunt curls to `gauntAsleep` (0.35) of its height. The body stands while the creature is in the open, `Enemy.Exposed`: by default wherever a tool's blow can land on it (`MeleeRadius > 0`), so what the crew can club, the gun can find. The exceptions: hounds only loose on the line (aboard, the car is round them; unchanged), Climbers on the roofs or at the gap (unchanged), the Switchman revealed at his lever, the Track Doll on the rail with `cannonShatters` (unchanged), the Car Hugger and the Gaunt whenever they're about (a great body by the line; asleep in a village). No body: the Fire Flies (a ball goes through a swarm) and the Choir's ghosts (every round still feeds the meter). A real child among the Soot Children never has one; a Soot Child only once it's shown itself. `World.Targets` holds every sphere (`Enemy.Body`), lag-compensated as before. The gun's arcs, the train's own body and the land still decide what a ball can reach, so the flank (Draggers under the cars, a Whistler folded in its gap) is still "no cannon answers" (§21), and anything inside a car is behind its walls. `HitRadius`/`HitHeight` in code and `trackDoll.railHitRadius`/`railHitHeight` are gone.
    - **A ball lands as a blow.** `Enemy.Hit(ctx, by, damage)` is now the creature's own rule for a blow (`Struck`) by the gunner, of `combat.json` `guns.damagePerRound` (4 of a tool's 1): hurt (a ball takes a Ribbit, a Follower, a Whistler or a Soot Child; two take a Gaunt; a Grumbler heals between one gunner's shots, so only a ball and a crewmate's blows together kill it), a crewmate held by it freed as a friend's blow frees them (a ball on a Whistler running off with someone, or a Grumbler mauling them), and a Grumbler struck by a ball goes feral on the gunner (App. A.8: "hunting whoever hit it last"). The Track Doll is still shattered, the hounds still killed or driven off by the rounds. Whether each creature can be killed at all, and by how much, stays with each creature's health and with queue #25 (A1's "driven off by their rules, killable by a coordinated team"): the ball rides whatever rule a blow has.
    - **The gunner bot** lays only on what the gun answers (`Enemy.GunAnswers`: the four of note 171) or on anything holding a crewmate, to free them. It never fires at a Gaunt asleep in a field or a Ribbit pack minding its own business, so the Choir's meter isn't fed for nothing.
    - **Seen.** A ball on a creature now throws its insides (`Effects.Ichor`): a dark cloud at the wound, a spray out the far side along the ball's way and a third of it back at the gun, arcing down to spatter the ground under it (`GreyboxScene.Strikes` passes the ground), and a splash there that lies as long as the scorch. Near-black blood for most, a Cinder Hound's embers and ash, soot for a Soot Child and the Stoker; the doll's porcelain as before. A ball on a wall leaves its scorch on the wall's face (`WallDecal`), as one on the ground always did. The hit flash, the flinch, the creature's hit clip and the gunner's marker (note 171) now play on every creature a ball can find. `dt screenshot --impact creature:gaunt --impact-at 60,2 --impact-age 1.5 --view ahead` stages one; `--impact structure` the wall's.
    - **Not yet:** a ball on the train's own body leaves no scorch (its impact is in the world, the car moves on). Per-creature pain sounds for a ball belong to the audio chat; a ball plays the generic hit cue as before.
    - **Verified:** `HitConfirmTests.EveryCreatureABallCanFindConfirmsTheHit` (all 15 kinds with a body, staged on the line ahead: the ball lands on the body, within its reach of its feet), `ABallGoesThroughASwarmAndAGhost`, `EveryBodyIsUprightOverWhereItStands`, `ASleepingGauntIsCurledUpLowAndWakingItStandsTall`, `ABallOnAGrumblerMaulingACrewmateFreesThemAndTurnsItOnTheGunner`; `CreatureBodyTests` (each body inside its model, up its height); the Sim suite (NetcodeTests included); screenshots of the ichor at 0.15, 0.5, 1.5 and 5 s and the wall's scorch looked at.

292. **The in-night menu (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #30).** In a night, Escape freed the mouse and a second Escape ended the night at once, with no word: a host's, for the whole crew. Nothing in a night opened the settings (B3's "settings take effect from the next night", #206). Now Escape opens Lethal Company's quick menu over the night, which goes on (it's the crew's, not this player's to stop): **RESUME**, **SETTINGS**, **INVITE** and **LEAVE**.
    - **One menu, the front end's.** It's `FrontEnd` with two more pages (`Screen.Night`, `Screen.Leave`) and a `NightMenu` record the app reads off the session as Escape opens it: hosting or joined, the other people aboard (bots not counted), a campaign night, a lobby that takes invites, the address friends type, the night over. So the keys, the mouse, the cues and the settings rows are the front end's own, and `MenuInput.Apply` works both. The settings' BACK, and Escape on them, come back to the menu; Escape on its first page shuts it, and where the front end was is put back.
    - **Nothing reaches the night while it's open.** The app's `Held`, `Hit` and `Pressed` read nothing, and the mouse doesn't look, so a player standing in the menu stands still. The night is drawn under it, dimmed, in place of the HUD (the HUD's corners under a list were a muddle), with no nameboard.
    - **It follows the night while it's open:** who's aboard, the report coming up, the gate passed (`FrontEnd.RefreshNight`, each frame), on the page it's on.
    - **Leaving is asked twice.** LEAVE (END THE NIGHT, for a host with others aboard) opens a confirmation with STAY lit, so the Enter that chose LEAVE, pressed again, stays. Both rows say what leaving costs: the night ends for the others aboard (a host), the crew carries on (a joiner), the slot carries on from the last stop the train left (a campaign night), or nothing from tonight is kept. These are a menu's plain words about the session, not a prompt foretelling the night (GDD §32 on #206). Over the report, LEAVE goes at once, as Enter does, keeping what you were commended for.
    - **Settings take effect at once.** The app takes a changed `Settings` up the same frame: the mouse speed, every rebound key, the HUD, push to talk, the mic level and the display (`ApplyDisplay`, which the menus already used). The volumes were always live. The microphone itself is still from the next night (its row says so). The player's name is sent as you join and the headset's comfort is set as a night starts, so those rows aren't on the in-night page.
    - **INVITE** opens Steam's overlay (F2 still does) when there's an open lobby with room. A host on the network without one is told its address to type on JOIN. A night nobody can join (alone, loopback only) has no INVITE.
    - **Not here:** in a headset the mirror window keeps the old Escape (VR is on the backburner), and the night never pauses, solo included.
    - **Verified:** `NightMenuTests` (8), `FrontEndTests` unchanged; `dt screenshot --menu night|leave [--others n] [--joined]`, and the app headless with `--night-menu --capture` (the menu over a real frontier:7 night) looked at.

293. **The profile screen (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #31).** GDD App. D.12 keeps commendations in "the player profile, not the character. Characters change on death; the tally survives", and note 180 kept them there (`PlayerProfile`), but nothing showed them: the art checklist's commendations row, "there's no profile screen showing the tally yet". The title has PROFILE now, between SETTINGS and CREDITS.
    - **The page:** your name, then the five badges of the starter set, a row each in D.12's order, with how many times a crew has given it (`FrontEnd.Tally`). One never given is drawn faint under a veil, with a dash for its count. Over them: how many in all, or, for a new player, that a crew gives them at the end of a night. Under them: where the nights' bookmark stills are kept (note 203's folder). BACK is the only thing to choose.
    - **Kept as it was:** the app loads the profile into the front end at the start and again after each night, once the run-end screen has recorded what you were given. Social only, as D.12 says: nothing on the page buys or unlocks anything.
    - **The menus' hints** say LEFT/RIGHT CHANGE only on a page with a value to change (the profile, the in-night menu, LEAVE's confirmation and the credits have none).
    - **Verified:** `ProfileScreenTests` (3); `dt screenshot --menu profile` looked at.

294. **Blocked sidings: derelict cars on a yard's sidings, by tier (B4, queue #32; level-design D.1, D.2, P18; I.4's "derelict cars on the sidings").** D.2's lever "Blocked sidings 0 / 0–1 / 1–2 / 1–3 (never all)" and D.1's cost ("two more [throws] for every blocked siding that has to be cleared", "one [reversal] per clearance", "clearances ×5") were in the design and in nothing else. Note 187's standing rakes (`TrainOnLine.Stand`) made it a generator change, not an engine one.
    - **The layout** (`StopGenerator.BlockSidings`, its own seed `StopSeed.Blocked`, after the yard and its power, so a stop's track and buildings are what they were): the tier's `blocked` count of tracks (stops.json), each holding `derelict.cars` (1–3, at most what its face takes) at the buffer stop: `YardTrack.Derelicts`. **Never the facility's own track** (its loading modules are there), so never all; a new Z.5 check, "Blocked sidings leave a way in", holds it. **Never at a switchyard:** its sidings have its own standing cars (note 187).
    - **The measure** (`StopGenerator.Measure`, P15): a trip into a blocked siding clears it first, `StopMoves.Clearances`, two more throws (the switch of the track the derelicts are put away on, set and restored) and a reversal, plus `score.clearance` (5). The planner still picks tracks by supply, so a blocked siding costs only if the yard needs it.
    - **The bands moved up by about one clearance** (stops.json, the sim's own calibration, level-design I.3): frontier yard 14–36 → 14–38, dead lines 28–56 → 28–64, deep territory 34–100 → 34–112. D.2's own bands (16–38, 36–64, 62–125) assumed blocked sidings all along. `dt site sweep --seeds 60`, kept medians before → after: frontier yard 23.8 → 26.7, dead lines 38.1 → 46.1, deep 58.1 → 71.9; every tier and kind 100% in band (dead lines yard + village was 98.3%), mean attempts 1.05–2.13; the clearances a kept yard's measure makes, on average, 0.43 frontier, 1.08 dead lines, 1.87 deep.
    - **In the world** (`Run.StandCars`, after every switchyard's cars so theirs keep their ids; host and clients alike, from the route): each blocked track's derelicts stand `derelicts.back` short of its buffer stop, handbrakes on (facilities.json `derelicts`). They're `Vehicle.Derelict` (and `YardCar`): empty, unlit, their shells at `integrity` (0.4, so the bite and scar kit draws them battered: the consist kit "in damage states", linegen plan §11.3), anything loaded into one paying `pays` (0.3) of itself (`CargoIntegrity`).
        - **Never the crew's:** a rake of derelicts alone is `Standing` wherever it's been put away (on any track, the main line too), so it's never a car lost (`Run.Tally`, the report's lost-car lines), never in the wreck's bodies, never boarded at the start. Coupled up and brought home they're delivered cars, paying what's in them at 0.3; they never cost repairs (they came battered).
        - **Clearing one** is the crew's own shunting: run in onto them at a crawl (they couple, as note 187's), back out, set them on a track already worked (or keep them, ahead of the engine, for the rest of the night: the cab's view of the line goes with that choice).
        - **Bots don't fetch them:** `Run.StandingOn` (the stop crew's pick-ups) counts a switchyard's cars, not derelicts; `Run.DerelictsOn` counts those. The bots work a facility's own track (I.4), which is never blocked, so they're unaffected.
    - **Readings:**
        - "Blocked" is derelicts on the loading face, standing at the buffer stop: the siding's useless for loading until they're out.
        - "Cleared" puts them away on a track already worked: that's D.1's two more throws and a reversal. Keeping them ahead of the engine instead is legal and costs the crew in a different way, so the measure doesn't count it.
        - "Never all": the facility's own track is always open, so a yard with one track never has one blocked.
    - **Headless:** `dt site --route deepTerritory:2 --stop 5` (three of four tracks blocked; `derelicts` on each track, `clearances` in the moves; the plan PNG draws them in rust at the buffer stops); `dt site sweep` adds `blocked` (stops by how many) and `clearances` (the mean) per tier and kind. In the world: `dt screenshot --route deepTerritory:2 --site --facility 2 --cam 27985,-34,13 --target 27925,-30,0` (the yard's derelicts at their buffer stops between the shed rows), `--cam 27962,-17,4.5 --target 27935,-25,1.8` (one up close).
    - **Not yet:** the bots never clear a blocked siding, since they don't load from a yard's other tracks at all (I.4). No new art: the derelicts are the cargo car at 0.4 integrity, unlit, and at night their scars barely read; a derelict look of their own (rust, a missing door, a lean) is the art checklist's.
    - **Verified:** `StopGeneratorTests.BlockedSidingsFollowTheTierAndNeverTheFacilitysOwn` (each tier's range over 40 yards, never the primary, derelict counts, none at a switchyard), `ClearingABlockedSidingCostsTwoThrowsAReversalAndTheClearance` (the same layout measured with and without its derelicts); `FacilityTests.ABlockedSidingsDerelictsStandAtItsBufferStopAndArentTheTrains` (where they stand, flags and shells, a client's ids the same, the bots' pick-up count blind to them, coupled up ahead of the engine, cut off and never lost); `EveryStopPassesEveryInvariant` and `DeeperTiersAreHarderToWork` on the new bands. No spec table pins these numbers; systems-spec unchanged.

295. **Tunnel name plates on both portals (B4, queue #33; linegen plan §13.3 "Tunnels: Number + name, plate on both portals").** Tunnels were named ("Tunnel 2 - Blackwell", `LineBuilder.Stations`) and on the route card, and the signage kit had a post-less `tunnelPlate` board that `PlanArt` stood on the track's centre line, but the generator never put one up: `LineBuilder.Signage` skipped tunnels where it plated bridges.
    - **Two plates a tunnel** (`LineBuilder.Signage`): at its `S0` and `S1`, the tunnel's name, required (cut in the stone, so never fallen or missing, and drawing nothing from the signage's survival roll: no other sign's state moves). A plate's `Side` is the way it faces, not a side of the line: +1 faces a train coming up the line into the near portal, −1 the far portal's, facing the other way.
    - **Over the arch** (signage.json `tunnelPlate`): its top at 10.6 m and 5 m wide, between the arch's crown (7.5 m, `StructureKit.TunnelSpring` + `TunnelHalf`) and the portal's top (11.5 m); it was 6.8 m, which would have hung in the opening. `PlanArt` squares it on its portal (no lean toward the track) and turns the far one round as `WorldFeatures` turns that portal. `SignKit` casts it in iron with cream letters, as the station boards are (the pale board was lost in the grey stone), the number over the name ("TUNNEL 1" / "FENWICK HEATH"), as it's called on the radio, rather than a word a line.
    - **Headless:** `TunnelPlateTests.EveryNamedTunnelHasItsPlateOnBothPortals` (frontier:7, deadLines:2, deepTerritory:2 and :5: two plates per tunnel, at its ends, facing out, named, standing). Seen: `dt screenshot --route deadLines:1 --at 14000 --cam 14172,4,4 --target 14210,0,8` (Tunnel 1's near portal) and `--cam 14385,-3,4 --target 14357,0,8` (its far one); `dt linegen generate --route deadLines:1` lists both plates of both tunnels, one on alternate alt2.

296. **T128's caveats: the Choir stilled in the forts, and a Gaunt among the left-behind's hunters (queue #34, D1; note 273's "Caveat" lines, GDD App. F.1 "The fort" and "Abandoned player").**
    - **The Choir in a fort.** Note 273 made both forts safe from creatures all night, but "the Choir's meter isn't stilled in the terminus": a crew loud in the terminus fort (or in the departure fortress after the gate's opened) still gathered it. With the train in a fort (`World.TrainInFort`), the meter isn't stepped: what it had gathered falls away at `choir.quietDecayPerSecond`, as in the quiet, and a swarm that followed the train in disperses on the spot (`Choir.Disperse`, its rest after it), its ghosts driven off by the fort's own rule. The safe yard before the run is as before (note 263).
    - **A Gaunt hunts the left-behind.** Note 273: "only the Ribbits hunt so far. Hounds or the Gaunt could join once their own rules allow a lone player on the ground." The Gaunt's do (App. A.6): it follows its waker at arm's length and attacks after enough silence, and talking holds it off, so a lone player can live with one; brought back aboard, the crew deals with it by its rule (lead it to a car, or kill it as a group). From the hunt numbered `director.abandoned.gauntFrom` (2, the third) a Gaunt comes with the Ribbit pack, woken on them (`Gaunt.WokenBy`), put down `gaunt.spawnOut` (25 m) off on the land they're on (`Director.HuntSpot`, out of the forts), one at a time per crewmate, never at a crew under `gaunt.minCrew` or on a night that bans it. `Director.Hunt.Gaunt` records it. A Gaunt woken from far off walks the rest of the way: it gets onto the train with its waker only from at their back (`Gaunt.Follow`, within three times `followAt`), so it no longer jumps aboard from wherever it stands, and one the train pulls away from is left standing, and goes by the linger rule (note 158). The Cinder Hounds still don't hunt off the line: their rules are the train's (running the line behind it, boarding its rear car).
    - **Verified:** `LeftBehindPressureTests`: `FromTheThirdHuntAGauntWokenOnThemComesWithThePack`, `AGauntStillWalkingUpDoesntJumpAboardWithThem`, `TheChoirDoesntGatherWithTheTrainInAFortAndASwarmThatFollowedItInIsGone`, and the existing hunts (their packs and the Gaunt shaken off between).

297. **Comfort settings: field of view, invert mouse, camera shake (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #35).** The eyes were drawn at a fixed 75° (vertical: about 107° across a 16:9 screen), the mouse looked one way only, and the boiler's shake (T109) and a strained car's judder (note 277) moved the eyes at full strength for everyone. Each is a setting now, in the settings and on the in-night menu's (note 292), and taken up at once there.
    - **FIELD OF VIEW**, 60° to 90° in fives (`Settings.FieldsOfView`), 75 by default: the game as it was drawn and its frame cost measured (`dt perf`'s views keep their own cameras, so its budgets are at 75). Wider draws more of the line, so it costs more. Only your own eyes take it: the chase view, the film, the replay and the Stranded outro keep their authored lenses. A hand-edited value that isn't on offer is drawn at 75.
    - **INVERT MOUSE** turns the pitch over. It's the look intent's sign, so the host and prediction see an ordinary look; nothing deterministic changes.
    - **CAMERA SHAKE** scales the boiler's shake and the judder, off to all of it in quarters. Only the eyes are spared: the gauges, the safety valve, the squeal and the sparks still say it.
    - **Not here:** VR takes its lenses and comfort from the headset (vr.json and its own settings), so none of these reach it.
    - **Verified:** `ComfortSettingsTests` (4); the app headless at 60° and 90° (`--settings` with the field of view set, `--capture`) looked at.

298. **The yard's fun: emotes and outfits (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #36).** GDD §9, the director's decision of 6 Oct: until the gate the yard is a safe space where "the crew wait for friends, hang out, dance, try on outfits". Nobody could do either: there were no emotes, and a crewmate's look (cap or helmet, scarf, colour) was fixed by their player id.
    - **Emotes.** Hold EMOTE (J, rebindable) and the wheel is round the crosshair in the prompts' fine print: DANCE up, WAVE left, POINT right (`EmoteWheel`). While it's held the mouse leans toward one instead of looking; let go, and that one is sent. A tap without a lean sends the last again. It's intent like any key: two bits on the intent's hotbar byte, sent once. The host turns it into an `EmoteEvent` (who, which, when) and sends it as a `RecordKind.Emote` record, kept for its length (player.json `emotes`: the dance 8 s, the wave and the point 2.5 s). A new one replaces the last, but not within the 0.5 s cooldown. The crew draw it while the emoter stands with nothing else to do (`CrewActs.EmoteOf`); walking ends it. Nothing in the sim reads an emote, so it moves no player or train state, and works in a night as well as the yard (`EmoteAndOutfitTests.AnEmoteMovesNothing`).
    - **The poses are placeholders.** crew_clips has no dance, wave or point, and the clips are art's. Until they come (`CrewPose.Dance`/`Wave`/`Point` play clips of those names the moment crew_clips has them), `CreatureArt.EmoteArms` poses the arms by IK over a clip: the dance steps on the spot (the walk) with the hips swaying and both fists pumped in turn, the wave is a hand up high rocking side to side, and the point is an arm straight out ahead. `dt screenshot --view crew --act dance,wave,point`.
    - **Outfits.** OUTFIT in the settings picks one of the crew's eight looks (look.json `crewColours`, named in `crewColourNames`, each with the cap or helmet and scarf that go with it), or THE CREW'S PICK (your id's, as before). It goes in your Hello. The host keeps everyone's in `World.Outfits` and sends them to the crew (`MessageType.Outfits`) as it does names. In the yard the in-night menu (note 292) has OUTFIT too: changed there, it's tried on at once (`MessageType.Wear`), and the crew see it. Past the gate the host keeps what you wore out; a change then is saved for the next night. A Passenger wearing your face wears your outfit.
    - **Also fixed on the way:** the settings' PLAYER NAME only reached the Hello from the second night on (it was set after the first was joined). The name and the outfit are now set before a night starts.
    - **Protocol 33** (31 is #201's, 32 #202's): the intent's emote bits, `RecordKind.Emote`, the Hello's outfit byte, `Outfits` and `Wear`.
    - **Not yet:** no mirror in the yard to see yourself (the crew see you); bots don't emote; the dance's clip is art's (asked on C1's and E1's PRs).
    - **Verified:** `EmoteAndOutfitTests` (Sim, 6: the wire both ways, seen by the crew for its length, replaced but not on top, moves nothing, the outfit in the Hello, tried on in the yard and not past the gate), `YardFunTests` (Game, 7), `RejoinTests` (the Hello's outfit, protocol 33); `dt screenshot --view crew --act dance,wave,point` and `--hud --emote-wheel` looked at.

299. **The bot gunner takes its gun (queue #37, D1).** Found while verifying #28 (note 290): in an 8-bot night with enemies (`dt harness --route frontier:7 --bots 8 --enemies --seconds 600`), the gunner fired no rounds, on main as on #212. A hound pack boarded and three of the crew were mauled with the guard gun standing empty. The harness's `posts` gave the gunner −1: it never reached its gun. `--trace` showed why. Six seconds out of the yard, it went into car 1 to catch the mail cranes' bags (its legs are a roof-walker's, `RoofWalkerBot.Look`'s drops: the next crane ahead whose board it's read, gone in for 45 s short of it). There was always another ahead, so it stood at car 1's side door all night. Bots crew a solo player's train in the app too, so this was a gunner that never fired for anyone.
    - **The fix.** The bags are the walkers' to catch. The gunner leaves them alone (`Look(..., catches)`) unless it's the only hand aboard besides the driver, as in a crew of two (note 222's look-out, the same reading). It still goes in for trouble in a car (a fire, Fire Flies on a lit lamp) while there's nothing at the back to shoot, as before.
    - **Verified:** `BotGunnerTests.FromTheYardTheGunnerWalksBackToItsGunPastTheMailCranes` (frontier:7, 8 bots, 10 cars, walked aboard from the yard: at the gun by 54 s; with the old behaviour forced on, the test fails with "the gunner never reached its gun"). The Sim suite. Harness, frontier:7, 8 bots, enemies, 600 s: 3 deaths to hounds before, 0 after, the train 5.8 km out before and 7.5 km after, 7 bags caught by the walkers where 5 were; no hounds came on the after night. With the hounds insisted on (`--insist cinderhound`, 400 s): before, 1 round fired, the gunner at its gun only at 262 s, 6 deaths; after, 24 rounds (its whole stock), 28 packs sent and driven off, 0 deaths, the gunner at its gun at 54 s.

300. **Solo, a few runs then friends: tested (queue #38, D1; GDD App. F.1, the director, 6 Oct 2026: "a solo player can finish one to three runs before it gets seriously hard and they realise they need friends ... The solo finish target will be tested later").** `dt balance --crews 1` over Local and Frontier at 3 and 6 cars, three seeds each, 24 km nights (on main with A1's run length, #207). First run: Local delivered 6/6 and Frontier 2/6, every loss to the cold. That looked like the target, but every loss was the bot standing still:
    - **Stranded on a landing.** The last door it shut at a stop left the lone driver on that car's landing, and `StopHand.SetBackAlone`'s walk to the cab is on the ground: from a car's deck it went nowhere, and it stood there "to the cab" until the fire died (frontier:2, 3 cars, from 1020 s). It now gets off the car first, by the side it's on (`OffTheCar`, or `GetDown` from a roof).
    - **Stood on the points.** A stop's hold is 2 m short of the points, and the driver took a stand up to 3 m past it as there. Frontier:2 with six cars stood 0.4 m over, its front on the points; they wouldn't go over, and the driver stood at the lever till the cold took it. `StopDriver.HoldOver` (1.5 m) is now the most it stands past a hold, everywhere a hold is judged (the stop, a switch set wrong, back together after). And once the stop gives the spur up (its Held give-up), a driver out throwing it alone goes back up into the cab rather than waiting at the lever all night.
    - **Judged.** `balance.json` `solo`: the first runs' cell (Systems Spec F.4 "Early": Local, 3 cars) delivered at least 66 % alone; the cell a crew advances to (F.4 "Establishing": Frontier, 6 cars) at most 34 %. Only judged where a sweep has crew-of-one nights there. The nightly soak runs the solo sweep, reported and not failing (a first pass, for the director to read).
    - **Found: solo isn't hard, for a bot.** With the two fixes, every solo night delivers: Local 3 and 6 cars, Frontier 3 and 6, and Frontier and Dead Lines at 10 cars (24/24, none lost, nobody hurt). "Solo is hard on frontier at 6 cars" fails. What a crew of one does pay is income. Mean net: Local 3 cars 420 (the spec's crew 765), Frontier 6 cars 996 (2,975), Frontier 10 cars 1,570 (5,355), Dead Lines 10 cars 2,716. A solo crew progresses at about a third of the spec's pace, and never stops progressing. Four creatures never come at a crew of one (`minCrew`: the Tippy Toesie, Soot Children and the Gaunt at 2, the Passenger at 3); the rest landed 3 punishes a night at 3 cars and 6 at 6.
    - **Caveat.** The bot is a diligent solo player: it never forgets the fire, misreads a board or falls off a roof, and it reads the line perfectly. People alone will find it harder, by an amount no sweep measures. The target is the director's to set against a person's solo night, not the bot's.
    - **DESIGN-TODO (the director): what makes solo "seriously hard"?** Untuned, for the director's call: (a) leave it, and let income be the wall (a third of the pace, roughly as the spec's car costs and progression shape stand); (b) the director's pressure scaled up when the crew is one (a `director` weight for crew size, the B.8 shape); (c) the four held back from a crew of one let in (lower `minCrew`), each with its counter checked alone; (d) the work itself: a lone driver stops for nothing it can't do from the cab at the higher tiers (a stop's loading needs a second pair of hands). Each is a tuning change; (b) and (c) touch every solo night, people's too.
    - **Verified:** `StopCrewTests.ADriverAloneOnACarsLandingGetsDownAndBackUpIntoTheCab` (left and right landings; the left fails without the fix), `ATrainStoodAsFarPastItsHoldAsItMayLeavesThePointsFree` (fails at the old 3 m), `BalanceTests.SoloFinishesItsFirstRunsAndNoMore`. Sim suite 951/951. The two failing nights traced again: frontier:2 at 3 cars drives on to 16 km, at 6 cars works its stop and runs 24 km.
281. **Fortress towns, first pass: a custom each, people who talk, papers to read, a square that's solid (the director's direction of 6 Oct 2026, GDD App. F.1 T133; GDD §3.1).** The direction: "fortress towns are where the world is built ... procedural, with people in them. Each town has its own odd culture, different from the last. Learn by inference, as in Lethal Company. Little notes, and text-only lines from the townspeople ... Much more in the towns is interactable." Before this, the town was art (note 107): houses you walked through, idle drab folk, nothing to read; the plan's fortress `Identity` was unused.
    - **The writing** (`content/world/towns.json`, `Sim/Towns/TownContent.cs`). Fourteen customs, each the human answer to one creature's rule (its `creature` by enemies.json `costs` names, "choir" always about), with a law, a hall, a centrepiece, six lines and three notes; eleven habits (`quirks`); three trades (`industries`: pit, growing, foundry, the linegen fortress identities) with their hands' lines and stalls; twelve jobs (`roles`) and an `anyone` pool; six threads of mystery (the fall, the lost trains, the dead lines, the penal cars, Dispatch, the fees); generic notices; knocks at the three doors; the gatekeeper's `welcome` with `{law}`. Placeholders `{town}`, `{other}`, `{hall}`, `{law}`, `{n}`, `{name}`, `{name2}` (a person in the same town, so papers and lines point at each other). Written in sentence case, drawn in the HUD's capitals.
    - **The numbers** (`content/tuning/towns.json`): the square (left of the way out, the platform's other side; 100 m to 28 m inside the outer gate, its far wall 30 m out, inside the yard's 70 m pad), how many stand round the centrepiece (3–5), one house in four with somebody out front, 2–3 lines a person, a scrap for 35%, 1–2 habits, 3–4 notices, 1–2 loose notes, reach (talk 2.6 m, read 2.0 m, 28°, closing at 4 m), typing 45 characters a second and 6 s left on screen. None is in the spec; each a first reading, fitted to the yard linegen lays.
    - **Generation** (`TownGenerator`). Deterministic from the route's seed and the fortress's name, each part on its own `Streams` stream (custom, habits, ring, names, roles, lines, papers...). The custom is drawn from those whose creature the edition fields (enemies.json `director.roster`; the demo gets six of the fourteen), never the last town's (`TownSite.Last`). People: the gatekeeper and a wall guard inside the gate, the clerk, the keeper and the storekeeper at their doors, a reader at the board, the fitter by the engine, the lampman by the cars, a porter on the platform, the ring round the centrepiece, and the street's folk down the yard (16–20 in all). Lines are dealt from shuffled decks without repeats in a town; the custom's six go first to the keeper and the ring, then the board's reader and the gate (`Precedence`), the street gets the habits and the trade, and anyone short is topped up from the trade, their job, a thread, and last `anyone`. The gatekeeper's first line is always the law. The board posts the custom's first note, then the trade's, the habits', the generic and the threads'; loose notes lie on a bench, by the hall's door, on a crate by the engine.
    - **In the world** (`Town`, `World.EnableTown`). The plan in world space, its walls (the square's far and end walls, the three buildings, the solid fixtures, a body-sized box for each person) added to the stops' `StopWalls` (now `Add`able), so `PlayerMotor` stops at them exactly as a client predicts. `Target` look-picks the person, board, paper, fixture or door within reach and the cone, for someone on the ground (up on a car, nobody in the town is in reach). Enabled after the run, on the host and every client (`SessionSetup.Build`, `PrototypeSession`), from the route and content alone.
    - **Not replicated, no protocol change.** Talking and reading change nothing in the night. The card is the app's (`Game/TownTalk.cs`): a Use press at the town's prompt (`Hud.TownTarget`: the prompt shown is the town's) opens it, Use again hears the next line or turns the next notice, walking 4 m off or a line said and left 6 s closes it, and the app keeps that press from the host while the key's held (so a lamp at somebody's feet isn't picked up). `Hud.Prompt` asks the town after the train's own controls and before what's lying in reach. Whoever you're talking to turns to you (`GreyboxScene.TownFacing`). What's needed alike is content: `world/*.json` is hashed into the Welcome as `world`, and a joiner who differs is told `world/*.json`. The last town's custom crosses in `SessionSetup.LastTown`, which the campaign keeps (`CampaignState.LastTown`, set when a night settles).
    - **Art** (`Art/SquareKit.cs`, `Art/WorldArt.Towns.cs`): the fortress's walls on the square's side run up to it and on from it on their ten-metre grid, the square's own walls step out to 30 m with a tower at each far corner, the lineside keeps its rocks and fences out of it (`WorldArt.TownSquare`), and no house of note 107's stands in it. The hall (brick, two storeys) and the office and stores (weatherboard), each with a name board, a door lamp and lit windows; a centrepiece for each kind (bell, post, tally, lamps, horn, mirror, shelf, lectern, brazier, line, pegs, bench, carriage, cannon); the board with a paper per notice; the plaque, stalls, benches, fire barrels, a crate; papers lying about; five lamp posts. The people are the crew's model in a lighter drab than note 107's (0.72). L1: kit boxes, readable at night; the director's review decides what's next.
    - **Headless:** `dt town [--route r] [--last culture]` (the town as made: custom, people and their lines, papers, fixtures, doors), `dt town sweep [--seeds n]` (customs' spread, repeats of the last, the longest line and paper), `dt screenshot --route r --town square|board|hall|gate|street`, `dt screenshot --hud --route r --talk person|board|paper|fixture|door [--who i] [--again n]` (the card open as Use opens it).
    - **Verified:** `TownTests` (the same route makes the same town; every custom written in full for a creature that exists, the demo's six among them; everything said fits the cards and nothing's unfilled, nobody says what another says; a gatekeeper with the law, a keeper on the custom, a full board; an edition keeps only its creatures' customs; never the last town's custom; everybody clear of the train, the walls and each other on frontier:7, local:3 and deadLines:3; walking at the hall stops at its front; what you look at is what you talk to or read; nobody's in reach from a car), `TownTalkTests` (a night starts in a town with its walls standing; lines heard in turn and the card typing out and closing; the board read notice by notice and put down; a lamp at somebody's feet doesn't take the press; looking away a press isn't the town's and closes the card; every word in the font). Screenshots: `town-square`, `town-over` (the square from above), `town-board`, `town-hall`, `town-talk`, `town-board-card` in out/shots.
    - **Not yet / the director's call:** the fortress's services in the town (the board of contracts, the stores, the upgrades and the clerk's counter are still the front end's menus); the terminus as a town of its own (it's note 107's) and the town you arrive at being the one you leave from; townspeople who move about, and models of their own (the crew's, with its mask's eyepieces, for now); interactions the whole crew sees (ringing the bell, lighting a lamp), which would need replicating; notes out along the line (villages, Holdouts, the wreck yard): "world building" past the towns; the harness doesn't build towns (its bots board on the platform side, clear of the square); the fortress walls along the rest of the yard are T124's to make solid; the greybox look has no square.
    - **Second pass: Maritime towns of 20 to 350, their houses and households (the director's notes of 7 Oct 2026, App. F.1 T133).** "These are maritime Canada towns, the buildings must look like Maritimes buildings. They must be fully interior modeled and explorable for some of them with residents. Lore is through NPC dialogue ... creepy things, sometimes hints of how to deal with monsters they've heard about but never the full rule. Cultures should all be traumatized somewhat ... between 20 to 350 people." The pieces:
        - **The writing** was rewritten for it. Maritime names, Acadian places among them (the card's font draws the accents as their plain letters), and every custom marked by loss. A plaque says how many live here and how many did. Households (`households`: the empty chair, the sleepwalker, the window, the one who came back, the letters, the cradle and more) have lines by part (elder, parent, child, lodger) and a thing of their own.
