A knock at a shut door is answered from behind it (`houseKnocks`); the lost houses (`emptyHouses`) have what's left to see.
        - **Anyone can hint at another town's creature, never the whole rule.** "In {other} they won't sing", "Go out four, come back four", "Never ride the last car". The hints are the customs' own, so nothing invented reaches a player as a rule.
        - **Enough lines for a 350-person town.** Every job has five lines, "anyone" has 47 and every thread three. A town of fifty speakers then never repeats a line and never leaves anyone mute.
        - **Population and the houses** (`TownGenerator.Houses`, `Sim/Towns/TownHouses.cs`; towns.json `population`, `household`, `former`, `houses`, `explorable`). The population (20–350), and how many lived here before (1.3–3.5 times as many), are drawn from the night. The households (2–6 each) take the lots down the yard's street on both sides, nearest the square first, every 15 m at 10.9 m out (note 107's village spacing, which the fortress's walls already allow for), off the platform. The first few, one per 70 people (2–5), stand open (`HouseKind.Open`), the rest shut (`Lived`). The houses of the people lost (the former population's households less the present's) follow: boarded, burnt or left open (`Boarded`, `Burnt`, `Empty`).
        - **An open house's ground floor is the Sim's** (`HouseLayout`): kitchen and parlour either side of a partition, the front door into the kitchen, a doorway through, the boxed stair, the range, table, dresser, cabinet, armchair and the parlour's lamp stand, each with a size and whether it's solid. `Town.Walls` stands the house's walls from it with the door and the doorway left open, plus the solid furniture, so a crewmate walks in, round the table and through to the parlour exactly as the art has it. A shut house is one box, a burnt one knee-high.
        - **The household** stands where the layout says somebody would be: at the range crouched, at the table or in the chair seated, at the window, by the stair. The parent always, then whoever else the household's story has a part for, up to four. Their own lines come first, then the custom.
        - **Nobody talks through a wall.** `Town.Seen` tests the line of sight against the town's walls (skipping the box the target stands in), so a resident can't be picked from outside the back wall.
        - **With T124's solid fortress** (#199, note 274): `Fort.Square` steps the fortress's walls and towers back round the square, and a town's fort stands no village houses (`Fortresses.Solids`). The town's houses are its own.
        - **Art.** `Art/MaritimeKit.cs` is the first pass, before the director's references:
            - four forms: a storey and a half with the Island's centre gable, the saltbox, the gambrel, and two storeys with a Lunenburg bump;
            - horizontal clapboard (`Clap` turns the siding texture's boards across) in seven faded paints, white trim and corner boards, a fieldstone foundation, two-over-two windows (lamplit, dark or boarded), a brick chimney, and a lamp by every lived-in door;
            - an open house built inside to the Sim's layout: floor boards, painted plaster over wainscot, the windows' insides, the partition and its doorway, the door swung in, the furniture, the household's thing, its lamps and the range lit while you're near (`MaritimeKit.Lights`);
            - the custom's building in its `hallStyle` (`SquareKit.Building`): a white church with a steeple over its door and pointed windows, a schoolhouse with its belfry, a car shed, a hall.

            Residents use the crew's model in their pose (`gunner` seated, `crouch_idle`, `lantern` with the hand lamp hung and lit, `idle`).
        - **Prompts in #206's style** (GDD §32 there): `NAME   TALK : [E]`, `READ`, `KNOCK`, `LOOK`; nothing foretold.
        - **Headless:**
            - `dt town` gives the population (now and before) and the houses by kind, with the open ones' households and things;
            - `dt town sweep` gives the population range and the most houses;
            - `dt screenshot --route r --town houses|house|kitchen|parlour` shows the street, an open house, and its kitchen and parlour.
        - **Verified:**
            - `TownTests.ATownIsTwentyToThreeHundredAndFiftyPeopleInHousesAndHasLostSome`;
            - `YouWalkInAtAnOpenHousesDoorAndThroughToTheParlour` (frontier:7, local:3);
            - `AShutHousesWallsKeepYouOutAndNobodyTalksThroughAWall`;
            - the first pass's tests over the bigger towns: nobody repeats a line, nobody is mute, everyone stands clear;
            - `TownTalkTests.EveryWordInATownIsInTheFont`, now covering the houses and the law too.
        - **Third pass: the houses to the director's references (7 Oct, photographs of Cape Breton, Peggy's Cove, Lunenburg, Shelburne and Blue Rocks: "lots of variations so it doesn't feel like the same 10 assets recycled across towns").**
            - **A design per house, drawn in the Sim** (`Sim/Towns/HouseDesign.cs`): gable-front or eave-front; 1, 1½, 2 or 2½ storeys; a gable, saltbox, gambrel or hip roof and its pitch; gable dormers, a shed dormer, a Lunenburg bump or the Island's centre gable; a lower side wing; a hood over the step or an enclosed porch; cedar shingle (silver, stained or painted) or clapboard; paint, trim, door, shutter, roof and accent colours; sash; chimneys; Victorian trim. What stands of it (the wing, the enclosed porch) is in `TownHouse.Parts` and walled by `Town`, so it's solid where it's drawn.
            - **A character per town** (content/world/houses.json `characters`, weighted by the fortress's identity, `byTrade`):
                - a fishing cove of shingled gable-fronts;
                - an old town of painted houses with bumps and brackets;
                - a loyalist waterfront row;
                - a farm town of capes with ells;
                - a company town of one double house in many paints (a coal row: identical on purpose);
                - a town of all sorts.

              Each character weights the odds and has its own palette, so one town isn't the next.
            - **The palettes are content**: houses.json's paints, stains, trims, doors, roofs, accents (sRGB hex, weighted). The Sim keeps indices; `Town.Looks` carries the colours to the art.
            - **Textures** (`tools/art/texgen/mat_maritime.py`, procedural so they rebuild without the scans): `shingle_cedar` (courses of silver cedar, butt shadows, lichen) and `clapboard` (lapped boards in near-white paint, faint wear). The kit tints both to the house's colour.
            - **The kit** (`Art/MaritimeKit.cs`) builds any design: the walls and roof in either orientation, gable ends fanned from the roof's profile, windows floor by floor and face by face (clear of the door, the wing and, inside an open house, the partition and furniture), shutters with their Z brace, the dormers, bump and centre gable, the wing with its roof and sometimes its own door, the hood or enclosed porch, chimneys or a stovepipe, brackets and window heads. Lived houses are lit; boarded, empty and burnt ones faded, boarded, dark, or charred to the sills with the chimney standing.
            - **Headless:** `dt art houses --character cove|lunenburg|shelburne|farm|company|mixed [--kind lived|boarded|empty|burnt] [--count n]` renders a lineup to out/shots/art.
            - **Verified:** `TownTests.HousesVaryWithinATownAndTownsDifferInCharacter`:
                - across 80 towns every character turns up;
                - in each town at least 80% of the standing houses round the square (the first 40: a big town's streets go on past them, note 335) differ in form, siding, paint, wing and porch (a company town shares one form);
                - nothing stands out of its lot or within 3 m of the line.

              Lineups and town streets looked at.
        - **Not yet:**
            - upstairs;
            - empty lots as cellar holes;
            - residents with faces of their own.

301. **Wrenches are the repair tool, Sea of Thieves style (queue #39, D1.3 for D1 at the director's call, the number C1's; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "When it comes to damages on the train, people running into things, anything like that, the wrench doesn't seem to be repairing things in the Sea of Thieves style ... I want to see that as soon as possible").** The first slice, behind `train.json` `repair.wrench` (on):
    - **Everyone carries a wrench** (`player.json` `kit`: crowbar, wrench; slot 2). The cab's rack wrench stays, for anyone who's lost theirs.
    - **The wrench in hand, Use at the break, mends it** (`Repairs`, `CrewActions.Apply`). The breaks: the burst boiler at its fire door (`boiler.json` `repairSeconds`, 25 s, the campaign's faster repair upgrade still divides it; the repair kit no longer mends it); a breach at its hole, from inside (`breach.boardSeconds`; bare hands no longer board it up, and Use at the hole without the wrench does nothing, not even the end door beside it); and, new, a car battered by what it ran into or what ran into it (couplings, hazards, the bend's strain), mended at its dent on the left wall three quarters back (`Repairs.DentAt`, clear of the end doors, the side doors, the crew lockers and the cargo), `integrityPerSecond` (0.04) back while it's worked, never past what a Car Hugger ate (`1 − Eaten`).
    - **A few presses do it as well as a hold.** A mend half done is kept with Use let go while you're still at the break with the wrench in hand (`Repairs.Keeps`; it's the player's own `ActionProgress`, so nothing new is replicated and a client predicts it as before: `NetcodeTests.AClientBoardingUpABreachIsPredictedExactly`, `...MendingADentIsPredictedExactly`). Walk off or put the wrench away, and it's started over. A dent's progress is the car's own `Integrity`, kept anyway.
    - **Every break is called out** (`RepairCallouts.Of`, drawn by `Effects.Repairs`): one language for all of them, an amber glow beating about once a second at the break, a halo and a ring swelling out of it, and torn metal spitting sparks; a shower off each strike while someone's wrench is at it (`GreyboxScene.Mending`); a small hot light so the wall round it reads. A dent is called out below `dentedBelow` (0.9) of what the car can come back to; above it, it's still mended at the dent, but nothing calls you to it. `dt screenshot --view mend --integrity 1,0.5 --breached 2` (`--mending` for the strikes), and `--view firebox --ruptured`.
    - **The HUD** (`Hud.RepairPrompt`): at a break with the wrench, `BOARD IT UP` / `MEND THE BOILER` / `MEND THE CAR : HOLD [E] (n%)`; without it, the break and the key that puts the wrench in hand (`BOILER RUPTURED   WRENCH : [2]`).
    - **The bots mend with it.** The fireman (or the driver alone in the cab) takes its wrench into hand and works the fire door; nobody goes back down the train for the kit (`KitCarry` stands down). A walker boards a breach with its wrench.
    - **Stranded (§23.2) is the kit's rule,** so with the wrench a lost kit strands nobody (`Run`: `StrandedTests.WhereTheWrenchMendsTheBoilerALostKitStrandsNobody`). Whether a night can still be stranded (a rupture with no wrench left aboard?) is the director's call for the next slice. **Answered (the director, 8 Oct 2026):** "If every crew member drops their wrench off the train then leaves them behind and then the train breaks down they could be stranded." So the next slice strands a ruptured night with no wrench left: every wrench (the crew's and the cab rack's) gone the ways §23.2 loses a kit, or dropped off the train and left behind (GDD §23.2).
    - **Slice 2 (D1.3, on the director's go): the kit's jobs go to the wrench, and the kit goes.** All behind `repair.wrench`, so `false` is still the T109/D.7 rule entire.
        - **A Holdout's lock** (D.7): the wrench in empty hands opens it quietly in `holdouts.json` `open` (6 s, no noise), as the kit did (`World.CrewAct` passes it to `Holdouts.CrewAct` as `kit`; the HUD offers `OPEN THE LOCK : HOLD [E]`). The crowbar or the shovel still smashes it, quicker and loud; a barricade's still pried. `HoldoutTests.TheWrenchOpensALockSilentlyAndTheCrowbarSmashesIt`.
        - **A broken radio** (note 200): the wrench in empty hands, Use held still for `kit.radioMendSeconds` (`Bodies.Mends`, `Bodies.Mend`); a tap puts nothing down. `HazardTests.TheWrenchHeldAtABrokenRadioMendsItAndATapDoesNothing`.
        - **The kit's gone:** none stowed in the fitter's locker, spares or not (`World.StowRepairKits`), none rolled at the stops (`loot.json` `repairKitChance` forced to 0 by `World.EnableLoot`; kits are their own stream, so the rest of a stop's loot is unchanged), and `campaign.json` sells no spare kits (its `spareKit` is gone, so the store's row is too). A save's spares stay in its file and aren't stowed. The repair upgrade (id `repairKit`, kept for saves) is now "Fitter's wrenches": it still divides `repairSeconds`, so the wrench's boiler mend is the quicker.
        - **The HUD:** no supplies row for the kit, no "where the kit is" under BOILER RUPTURED (the fire door's callout shows where), the radio's prompt without "PUT DOWN". The clerk's "kit lost" line can't come: nothing's stocked, so nothing's lost (`Run.Kit`).
        - **Still the kit's code, for `repair.wrench: false`:** `BodyKind.RepairKit`, `KitCarry` and `KitRun`, `EngineeringKit` and §23.2's Stranded, the cascade audit's rupture chain, the stranded outro's empty shelf. The tests that pin the kit's rule run with the flag off.
        - **The engine's shell** (the director's "people running into things": the Sleepers' and the line's debris hit the front vehicle, the engine; `Hazards`, `TrackRules`): its dent is on the boiler's left flank, waist high, `repair.engineDentBehind` (2.5 m) behind the left running board's sandbox (`Repairs.DentAt(train, car)`), worked from the board, never from the cab. `RepairTests.TheEngineBatteredByWhatItRanIntoIsMendedFromItsRunningBoard`; `dt screenshot --view mendengine --integrity 0.5,1`.
        - **The smashed headlamp** (the director, 8 Oct: the wrench mends "burst boiler, breach, car damaged in collision, engine damaged, broken radio, locked holdout door, smashed headlamp; the rest stay as they are"): a Climber's smash no longer times out by itself (note 266's relight waited on `climbers.lampOutSeconds`). With the wrench in hand in the cab within `dentReach` of its front windows, each second worked takes `repair.lampMendRate` (6) off what's left (45 s of glass is 7.5 s; lamp armour halves it), then it's lit again as the driver had it (`Repairs.Lamp`, `TrainOnLine.LampOut`/`MendLamp`, lent by the `World`). Called out twice, on the cab's nose and on the windows' sill inside, where the mender stands. The bot driver steps forward to the windows and mends it, but never while the Climber that smashed it is still in the cab: it takes whoever comes within reach, so the driver keeps to its corner (`KeepClear`) and the glass waits. Before, a harness night's driver crossed the cab to mend it, was taken at km 3, and the train stood the rest of the night (D1's regression call, 8 Oct; `FiremanTests.TheHeadlampTheClimberSmashedWaitsTillItsGone`). And it mends from the floor behind the fire and the coal, where Use with the wrench is the lamp's: the corner it keeps to is by the vent, where Use is the vent's, and the same night's driver, the Climber gone, held the vent open from there with the wrench; the lamp was never mended, and the boiler drained to nothing and the train stood (`FiremanTests.TheHeadlampsMendedFromTheFloorNotTheVentsCorner`). `RepairTests.ASmashedHeadlampStaysOutTillTheWrenchMendsItFromTheCabsFrontWindows`, `...TheBotDriverMendsASmashedHeadlampFromTheControls`, `UpgradeTests.ArmouredTheSmashedLampIsMendedSooner`; `dt screenshot --view cab --smashed --headlamp-out` (and `trackside`).
        - **Stranded is the last wrench's** (the director's answer above; GDD §23.2): `EngineeringKit.Wrench` reads §23.2's rules for the wrenches. One's aboard in a living crewmate's kit, on the cab's rack, or on a fallen crewmate's body in a reachable car or on the line within `stranded.kitLostBeyond` of someone alive; in a car taken or cut loose and left behind, on a body left that far back, or carried off with one, it's lost. A ruptured boiler with no wrench aboard ends the night once she stops (`Run`, `RunEnd.Stranded`, "THE LAST WRENCH WENT WITH THE CAR"). Every respawn brings a wrench, and a wrench can't be dropped yet, so in play it takes the crew hanging theirs on the rack and losing the rest with the fallen. The clerk's "kit lost" line isn't said for the last wrench (AU1 has no recording for it). `StrandedTests.WithNoWrenchLeftAboardARupturedNightIsStranded`, `...AWrenchOnTheRackOrInAnyLivingHandKeepsARupturedNightGoing`.
        - **Stays as it is** (the director's call): a fouled gun is cleared by hand, a hot box greased (note 331), a car fire put out with the extinguisher; a charred cell (note 267), a car's spoiled cargo and what a Car Hugger ate aren't mended. Left: the swing at a break (mending is Use).

302. **A dead town's railway side: its station, and a goods yard of derelict stock (B4, queue #40; linegen plan §11.3 "Dead town: platforms, station building, goods shed, sidings with derelict stock (reusing the consist kit in damaged states), road crossings, house shells").** A main-line dead town was a village halt like any other (note 154): the plan's two platforms, its name board, houses. The railway it was a town for wasn't there.
    - **The layout** (`StopGenerator.RailwaySide`, its own seed `StopSeed.DeadTown`, after the village and before the Holdouts and lairs, so they're placed round it; `StopContext.DeadTown`, which `PlanStops` sets for a "town" landmark): stops.json `deadTown`.
        - **The station** (`BuildingKind.Station`, 16 × 7 m) stands `gap` (1.5 m) behind the halt's platform on its side, 4–12 m along from the lane up to the village, whichever end fits.
        - **The goods yard** is out past the tier's rail buffer by `beyond` (2–12 m), on the far side from the village if it fits, else the village's: a goods siding 70–110 m long, its middle within `reach` (60 m) of the halt along the line, with its points long lifted (`StopLayout.Sidings`: derelict track, not a branch, so nothing runs onto it); 1–3 derelict vans (`BuildingKind.Derelict`, 14 × 3.2 m, 1.2 m apart) standing on it from its buffer stop up the line; and the goods shed (`BuildingKind.GoodsShed`, 20 × 9 m) beyond the siding, its workbench a find at `find` (0.6, a `Bench`, so loot.json's bench items).
        - A new Z.5 check, "A dead town has its railway side" (a station, derelicts, one siding), applies to dead towns alone: one that can't be laid is rerolled (P15).
        - "Nothing overlaps" lets a derelict stand on its own siding (it still mayn't touch the main line).
    - **Solid** (`StopWalls.Walled`): the station, the goods shed and every derelict stand as walls, like a village's houses, and a find in the goods shed is put out on its doorstep as a house's is.
    - **The measure:** a dead town is a village halt to P15 and its band. Laid anywhere along the town, the goods yard's find made the village's round trip long (local's 95th percentile went from 22 to 30); within `reach` of the halt, `dt site sweep --seeds 60`'s new `DeadTown` rows score as the halts do (first-attempt quantiles identical), in band 100% from frontier on and 59/60 at local (its halts' 100% on 2.2 attempts is near the band's top already).
    - **Art** (`WorldArt.Stops`): the station a brick booking hall (or timber, variant 1), its door and an iron canopy to the line; the goods shed a tall timber shed, its doors to the siding; each derelict a box van gone to rust on two bogies, its door openings dark (a leaf slid off its runner on variant 2), drawn as the prison car is; the siding's sleepers and rusted rails, and a timber buffer stop at its far end (`GoodsSiding`). `StopMap` draws them (the station in brick red, the shed in timber, the derelicts in rust, the siding dashed).
    - **Headless:** `dt site --route frontier:7 --stop 1` (Maddox: `railwaySide` and `sidings`, and the plan); `dt site --tier deadLines --seed 3 --kind village --town` (any seed as a dead town); `dt site sweep`'s `DeadTown` rows. Seen: `dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 9850 --cam 10218,-2,4 --target 10255,11.8,3` (the station behind the platform, from the line, the halt's lockup beside it) and `--cam 10150,-8,4 --target 10215,-30,2` (the goods shed and its siding's derelicts).
    - **Not yet:** towns on settlement-line alternates still have no stop at all (note 154; features are main-line only). The derelicts are buildings, not vehicles: nothing couples to them (their siding's points are lifted). Nothing lives in the goods yard's sheds yet (level-design H.2's sites are the village's and yard's).
    - **Verified:** `StopGeneratorTests.ADeadTownHasItsStationAndAGoodsYardOfDerelictStock` (each tier, 25 seeds: the station behind the platform, the siding past the buffer with its derelicts on it, the shed beyond with its find out of the buffer, all walled, none at a halt), `TheLinesDeadTownsAreStopsWithTheirRailwaySide` (frontier:7, deepTerritory:2 and :5: every main-line dead town a village with its railway side; no other village has a siding).
304. **The voice booth (AU1, queue #42; the director, 7 Oct 2026: "Make an artifact for this where I can put my recordings for lines and then listen to them after you've done work modulating and editing them so they don't sound like me").**
    - **The page** (the Dark Territory Voice Booth, claude.ai/artifact/3VvuCkMwP3hJ6iDb1PZaoe; its source `tools/audio/booth/voice-booth.html`): the script as lines by group (the Holdout prisoners, the Soot Children's call, the yard clerk, the crew's breath, creature sources), each with what to say and how. The director adds a take per line from a file (a phone voice memo is the expected form); the page keeps it in the artifact's asset store and its `takes` collection. The disguised versions come back under the take, each played on the page and marked Keep or Redo.
    - **Why files, not a record button:** an artifact can't open the microphone, so takes come from the director's phone or desk. The asset store takes only images, video, PDF, fonts and text: a voice memo (.m4a, MPEG-4 audio) goes in as video/mp4, and anything else is wrapped in a JSON envelope (base64) that `booth.py` unwraps.
    - **The disguise** (`tools/audio/booth.py make LINE TAKE --out DIR`): each version moves the voice's size (its formants) as well as its pitch, so it's another throat and not a sped-up recording of the director. A listener knows a voice by its formants and how it moves, which pitch alone doesn't hide.
        - The prisoners: deep, old, thin, a woman, and behind a wall.
        - The Soot Children: through `recipes/children.py`'s child (a girl, a boy, a small one).
        - The clerk: flat and deep, plus a preview through the radio as the game plays it.
        - The crew: within a semitone, so a breath stays a breath.
        - Creatures: per cue.

      Tails are cut at −50 dB. Each version is a .wav for the game and an .mp4 preview for the page.
    - **What's kept** becomes a candidate on the audio checklist, like any recipe's, and goes into the game through `install.py`.
    - **Not yet:**
        - The director's first 11 takes (7 Oct: prisoners, the Soot Children's call, the clerk's lists, the Track Doll) are on the page. Their versions, and installing what's kept, are #42's next PR.
        - The director's own script wasn't found (not in the repo, Drive or the artifacts), so the page holds a 31-line draft (`tools/audio/booth/script.json`) and takes lines pasted in.

305. **Crew 2 and the group creatures: GDD Part Eleven, open question 12 swept (queue #43, D1: "At crew 2, which group-based enemies are still fair? Needs a harness sweep, especially Ribbits and Tippy Toesie").** Each creature whose rule counts the crew, alone (`dt balance --pairs --only <kind>`), on frontier:7 and deadLines:2, at crews 2 and 4, three seeds a cell, the clear hazard set, on the line and at stops (168 short nights). And each grab rigged at crew 2 (`dt audit grabs --crews 2`).
    - **Every grab breaks at crew 2.** The one other crewmate frees each: a Ribbit pack of two broken off in 0.2 s (of 8), Tippy Toesie in 1.3 s (of 20), Soot Children killed in 3.9 s (of 14), a woken Gaunt broken off in 1.9 s (of 8), the Car Hugger in 0.3 s (of 10), the Choir fled in 0.8 s (of 12). The Passenger never comes at fewer than three (`minCrew`).
    - **Ribbits, Tippy Toesie, Soot Children, the Gaunt and Followers: fair, and never landed.** No grab, punish or death in any night at either crew. The bots keep together and never stand idle alone, which is each one's opening. People who split up will meet them; the grabs above say the other one can get them out.
    - **The Choir: unwinnable at 2, from how the bots played it.** One crewmate seized and killed every night at both sizes; at crew 2 that's half the crew, and the sweep calls a night lost at half. The gunner had gone into car 1 to catch the mail and was working with the side door open: App. A.7 seizes anyone outside or behind no shut door, and with the driver at the controls nobody could break it. Now, the Choir gathered past halfway (`ChoirShelterAt` 0.5, about 20 s off) or here, out of the yard and the forts, the crew bots go indoors (`WarmUp.Shelter`), shut the doors before any work in there (`ShutFirst`), and leave the bags (the hook goes out through an open door). After: fair at both sizes, 24 seizes, all broken, nobody dead.
    - **The Car Hugger: crew 2 lost 2 of 3 Dead Lines nights, from how the bots played it.** The gunner saved the gun, then went down to the guard van's platform to club it with nobody but the driver aboard: swallowed, and nobody to pull it free (A.3: "swallowSeconds for friends to pull them free", and one player can barely out-hit it). The walkers' legs now club it only with a crewmate out of the cab within `PullReach` (10 m); otherwise they keep clear, up the train, and it may take the car. After: crew 2, no deaths, the same cargo lost (15.6 % on deadLines:2).
    - **Open: the Car Hugger at crew 4 (not crew 2's).** On deadLines:2 at crew 4 it still eats a clubber most nights (3 dead in 3 nights, none pulled free; 4 before the reach rule): a friend is near, but the bots never pull a swallowed crewmate out. It's the crew-4 bots' answer, not the rule; left for a later item. *Done (note 310): from the roof, a friend goes to the end ladder's top and hauls.*
    - **The answer to question 12:** all of them are fair at crew 2, played right. The Choir and the Car Hugger ask a crew of two to play them differently from a big crew (shut in rather than out, and let a car go rather than club it), which is the GDD's intent for small crews.
    - **Verified:** `CrewOfTwoTests.TheChoirFindsACrewOfTwosGunnerBehindAShutDoor` and `ACrewOfTwosGunnerKeepsClearOfTheCarHuggersMouthAndLetsItTakeTheCar` (each fails without the change: Seized 1, Eaten 1). The Sim suite. The Choir and Car Hugger sweeps re-run after (above); the Car Hugger at crews 2, 4 and 8 on the line: 0, 3 and 0 dead.

308. **The kit lost, on the radio (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #47; GDD App. E.12 question 5).** The question was whether the fitter's empty shelf is enough of a tell that the engineering kit is gone, or whether the clerk needs a radio line. The director, 7 Oct 2026: a radio line.
    - **What's said:** once the run has held the kit lost for `stranded.lostForSeconds` (the same second the Stranded check waits), each machine puts the yard on the air once: "Yard to consist. Engineering kit reported lost. Yard out." When the kit went with a car (`KitLoss.CarTaken`, `LeftBehind`), the car's number goes in: "…lost with car 3." It says what's known, never what follows from it (GDD §32 on prompts). It's a reading like the tally's: the radio card typed at the clerk's pace and said in his voice (`NetPlaySession`'s bulletin, between the tally and the manifest). It's said once a night, however long the kit stays lost.
    - **A flag:** run.json `radio.kitLost` (true); false puts back the shelf alone.
    - **The voice:** the clerk's bank has no "engineering kit reported lost" or "with car" yet. `tools/audio/clerk.py` lists them now, and until the audio chat rebuilds the bank the set breaks up over them (the card still says it), as it does over a typed name.
    - **Verified:** `RadioCardTests.TheYardSaysOnceWhenTheLastKitIsLost` (a hosted frontier:7 night, every kit carried off: said once, then not again) and `AKitLostWithACarSaysWhichCar`.

309. **The outside creatures start where the stops say they live (B4, queue #48; level-design H.2; GDD B.6).** The stop generator has placed each outside creature's site since the generated stops did (level-design Part H, "Holdouts and creature lairs as generated level content": Ribbits' warrens, the Gaunt's roost, a Soot Child's call, Followers' ground, the Grumbler's perches, the Whistler's nest), "the layout says where; the director will say when". Nothing read them: every spawn put its creature at `SpawnContext.Out`, an offset from the ground crew's middle, and the wiki told players they wait in warrens and sleep in the furthest building.
    - **Where** (`SpawnContext.Sites`, `NearestSite`; enemies.json `sites`): the sites of the generated stops within `around` (300 m) of the train, in the world on the ground there, the nearest to the ground crew within a kind's reach and no closer than `minOut` (12 m, nothing comes out from under their feet).
        - **Ribbits** come out of the warren nearest the ground crew within `warrenReach` (70 m). A stop with warrens and none that near has none to send: the spawn fails, and the director spends elsewhere. They lose interest past 45 m (`giveUpBeyond`), so a pack at a warren 45–70 m off waits there until someone comes near.
        - **The Gaunt** sleeps in its roost (the building furthest from the train on foot) within `roostReach` (400 m): you go to it.
        - **A child** calls from its call, beyond the stop's built edge where the train can see it, within `callReach` (160 m).
        - **A Follower** takes only a crewmate standing in one of its grounds (its radius and `groundMargin`, 4 m); off them, nobody's free for it (its weight and its spawn both).
    - **When** is the director's, unchanged: the same gates and weights, the same budget. What's changed is only where: a stop where the crew keeps away from the warrens and the roost meets fewer Ribbits and no Gaunt, which is B.6's "you go to it".
    - **A hand-laid route** has no layouts and no sites: there they come from out in the dark round the ground crew, as before (`Sites` empty).
    - **Not yet:** the Grumbler's perches (it comes to a facility's crane on its own rule, which already is a gantry) aren't read (the Whistler's nest is, since note 314); the abandoned crewmate's packs (note 273) still come from round them, on purpose (they're hunted wherever they are).
    - **Verified:** `SpawnSiteTests`: Ribbits out of the warren nearest the crew, and none from a stop whose warrens are all far; the Gaunt at its roost and a child at its call; a Follower only for someone on its ground; a hand-laid route's Ribbits as before.

310. **The crew pull a swallowed crewmate from the Car Hugger's mouth; harness nights started on the line keep their walkers (queue #49, D1; found in #43, note 305).**
    - **The rescue.** On deadLines:2 at crew 4, the Car Hugger ate a walker most nights: it went down the end ladder to club it, was swallowed on the ladder, and the friend on the roof above stood there the ten seconds A.3 gives friends to pull them free. `Heed.Rescue` steered a rescuer at the one held on its own level, and from the roof that got no nearer: the one held is on the ladder or the platform under the roof's edge, past `grab.pullReach` (1.6 m) from anywhere on the roof but its end. A rescuer on the Car Hugger's car's roof now goes to the top of the end ladder over the one held (where `Beat` takes hold of the ladder) and hauls from there. Traced (`dt harness --route deadLines:2 --bots 4 --cars 6 --enemies --insist carhugger --start 7700`): seeds 1 and 3 had lost two walkers each, one after the other; now every grab (20 a night) is pulled free and nobody's eaten.
    - **The harness's walkers.** `dt harness --start` past the gate put every crewmate after the driver in the respawn queue (App. D.1: past the gate nobody spawns aboard; `HostSession.Lobbying`, with Holdouts on). The gunner and fireman were posted at 1 s; the walkers never were, and stood "waiting in the queue" all night. Every mid-line harness night with four or more ran with the driver and the gunner only. Anyone still waiting at 1 s is now put on the roofs, spread down the train as boarding does (`Harness.PostWaiting`). The combination sweep (`dt balance --pairs`) wasn't affected: it doesn't enable Holdouts, so nobody queues.
    - **Verified:** `CarHuggerRescueTests.AHarnessNightStartedOnTheLineHasItsWholeCrewAboard` and `AFriendOnTheRoofHaulsASwallowedCrewmateOutOfTheCarHuggersMouth` (seeds 1 and 3; each fails without its change: "roof-walker never came aboard", "nobody was pulled out"). The Sim suite.

313. **Fog that fills the low ground first (B4, queue #52; linegen plan §14 "Fog density ×1.3 in `low_ground` and `marsh`, ×0.8 on crests"; maritime-rules §4 "fog filling the coves first").** The plan has carried a fog factor per stretch since §14 landed (`PlanExposure.Fog`), and nothing read it: the renderer's fog was the route's one density for the night, the same in a marsh hollow as on a summit.
    - **The factor reaches the eye.** `ITrackConditions.Fog(path, distance)` (1 by default; `PlanConditions` reads the plan) is the stretch's factor averaged over `weather.fogBlendM` (150 m) either side (the runs' exact mean; it was nine samples until note 278 found two run edges 300 m apart stepping it twice over), so a hollow's fog comes up round the train over a few hundred metres and drains away again; at cruise that's about 20 s, never a step. `Views.FogDensity(route, train)` is the route's density times the factor where the engine is, and the app, `dt screenshot`, `dt film`, `dt trailer` and `dt playthrough` all set the frame's fog with it. The drifting fog cards (`Effects.Fog`) each take the factor where they lie, so the low ground ahead is seen filling before the train's in it.
    - **Water is foggy like low ground.** A stretch along a shore (`LinePlan.Shores`: sea, Fundy, dyke, river), or within `weather.fogWaterM` (40 m) of a lake's edge or across one, takes `weather.fogWater` (×1.3); in low ground too it's the larger of the two, not both (`why` "water"). frontier:7's Fundy shore (km 15.6–18.7) and dyke (km 22–24.3) are its foggiest stretches now.
    - **For the eye only.** Nothing the sim decides reads it: §14's fairness plans sightlines at the night's minimum fog distance and leaves that alone, boards stand where they stood, and the lamp still reveals along the track (§22.6). The caveat: at ×1.3 the 20 % contrast distance (density is 1.6 over the fog distance) falls to about 0.77 of the night's mean fog distance, so in a hollow the eye sees a little less than authority planned for; the boards already stand well beyond the fog (§9.5's worked example: 251 m), and restricted speed carries the rest. `weather.fogAlongLine` false keeps the night's one density everywhere; a plan saved before this note reads as false.
    - **Verified:** `FogTests.TheFogThickensInTheLowGroundAndByWaterAndNeverSteps` (frontier:7, deadLines:3: deep in any stretch longer than the blend the fog is that stretch's own; every shore's middle at ×1.3 or more; along the whole line, 10 m at a time, no change bigger than one sample's share of crest-to-hollow) and `FogIsTheSameOnEveryMachineAndOffThePlanItsTheNights`. Seen in `dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 17000 --view ahead` against main's: on the Fundy shore the buildings across the flats go into the fog and the near ground still reads.

314. **The Whistler's nest at its site (B4, queue #53; level-design H.2 "out on the side of the stop with the least built on it"; note 309's "not yet").** The stop generator placed a Whistler's nest at every stop, and the Whistler never went there: it ran its victim to note 273's spot, 30 m straight out from its gap.
    - **Where it runs** (`Whistler.NestSite`'s `sites`, read through `CreatureSites.Of`, the lookup note 309's spawns now share). At a generated stop it goes to the layout's nest: the nearest within `whistler.nestSiteReach` (110 m) of its gap, at least `nestMinDistance` out. The way there has to pass note 273's checks: no 2 m steeper than `nestMaxSlope`, never more than `nestMaxRise` from the rail, no water. A stop's ground is laid level for the stop, so a nest past the line's 40 m corridor is still walkable there. Off a stop, or when the way fails, it runs as before.
    - **Through no wall.** Every run, to a stop's nest or note 273's spot, now fails the check where it would cross a stop's or a fort's walls (`StopWalls`, within half a metre). It goes the other side, shorter, or to the formation's edge, as note 273 has it.
    - **Where the nest is.** The layout put the nest anywhere from 15 % to 85 % of the zone's length, often 150 to 450 m along the line from where the train stands, and no Whistler at a gap could reach it. Now it's within `lairs.whistlerNestAlong` (50 m, stops.json) along the line of the stop point, 40 to 90 m out on the emptiest side as before. With that, the gap behind car one runs to the stop's own nest at 156 of 166 stops (Frontier, Dead Lines and Deep Territory, seeds 1 to 12). The rest are blocked by water, a slope or a house.
    - **The rescue.** At its 4.5 m/s, 100 m is about 22 s of running, and the 20 s at the nest come after. A friend at 5.5 m/s still closes on it, as the GDD's "every rescue is a chase on foot" asks, just further from the train.
    - **Verified:** `SpawnSiteTests.TheWhistlerCarriesItsVictimToTheStopsNestAndThroughNoWall`: every generated stop with a nest on three tiers and twelve seeds. The run goes to the stop's own nest at 90 % or more of them (156 of 166), never through a wall, and when it doesn't use the stop's nest, no further than note 273's 30 m. `GrabDestinationTests` (note 273's mountainside, bank and cutting) are unchanged.

315. **Each player skips their own film (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #54; GDD App. E.12 question 2, E.5, E.9).** The question was whether a player's first derailment should be unskippable for them. The director, 7 Oct 2026: "players should be able to skip whenever they want. It's up to EACH player if they want to skip their film." That replaces note 177's vote (a majority of the session, or the host, after the first player's shot) as well as answering the question.
    - **Each player's own:** the film is already each machine's own playback of the same recording (`WreckSeconds` is the client's), so skipping is the client's alone and nothing goes on the wire. `NetPlaySession` keeps the held Skip bit and never sends it. Held for wreck.json `skip.holdSeconds` (0.5 s), it jumps this screen to the cause card. The cause card is never skipped. Nobody else's film changes, and the host counts no votes (`World.FilmSkipped` stays false).
    - **Whenever:** from the first frame: the first person, the replay and the cut. A skip taken while the film's still being shot (off the frame loop) waits for it, then lands on its cause card. **Reading:** a held half second, not a press, because Jump is the skip key and a player mashing it as the train comes off shouldn't lose their own death by accident. The prompt fills a line under "HOLD [SPACE] TO SKIP" as it's held.
    - **The Stranded outro (E.9) the same way,** from its 3 s skip delay (E.10's number, kept). **Reading:** the director spoke of the film; one rule for the one key reads better than a vote on one screen and your own on the other. E.9 now says so.
    - **A flag:** wreck.json `skip.own` (true); false puts back the crew's vote, which `HostSession` still counts and `FilmTests` still pins.
    - **Bookmarks are untouched:** a derailment's stills come from the film's peaks (note 203), not from how far a screen has played it, so skipping doesn't lose them.
    - **Verified:** `WreckSessionTests.TheFilmIsTheCrewsAndEachPlayerSkipsTheirOwnToTheCauseCard` (skippable in the first person; a tap skips nothing; held, it lands on the cause card once the film's in; the crew's film isn't voted off) and `FilmTests.EachPlayersOwnSkipIsNeverTheCrewsVote` (the whole crew holding it, the host's player too: no vote, nothing skipped). The vote tests run with `skip.own` false. `dt screenshot --film 1 --skip-hold 0.3` shows the prompt part-filled (looked at, beside one with nothing held).

316. **The panels you open, in note 285's form (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #55; GDD §32; note 285's "not yet").** The roster (held Q) and the supplies (I) were the last riveted plates in a night: the HUD's full-size text on iron with brass trim and four rivets, 260 px of a 480 px screen for the roster. Note 285 kept the panels you open on plates ("you asked for them") and listed them as not yet done; the director's word on the overhaul was that there's too much UI on screen.
    - **The form is the ballot's** (note 285): fine print (`Hud.Fine`) on a dark backing, lit along its top in the title's colour, no rivets, no trim, a fifth of the way down the middle (`Hud.Panel`). The roster's title is in ink and the supplies' in amber, as before.
    - **What they say is unchanged:** the roster's names and SPEAKING; the supplies' rows (`SuppliesLines`, which C1's #39 rewrites for the wrenches; untouched here). The close key reads in the prompts' form, "CLOSE : [I]".
    - **Verified:** `QuietHudTests.ThePanelsYouOpenAreFinePrintWithNoRivets` (no rivet, brass or bevel; the roster under 200 px wide, the supplies under 60% of the screen; SPEAKING still green). `dt screenshot --hud --supplies` and `--roster`, before and after, looked at.

317. **A trestle across a lake's neck (B4, queue #56; maritime-rules §4's "not yet": "a crossed lake is always a fill").** Some crossed lakes are now taken on a low timber trestle, the water running on under it.
    - **Which** (`LineBuilder.TrestleAcross`). `terrain.lakes.trestleChance` (0.4) of crossed lakes, each from its own dice (`Rng("lakeTrestle", lake id)`), so a line whose lakes all stay fills is laid exactly as before. The span is where the main line is over the water, plus `trestleAbutmentM` (6 m) each end. It's not laid when that's over `trestleMaxM` (240 m), or within `trestleClearM` (50 m) of another structure.
    - **What** it is: a `Trestle` in timber, no weak limit, its height the rail over the lake's floor. It's named like any bridge ("Bramwell Trestle") and is a landmark. It's laid before the tags, the exposure, the authority and the signage, so it's tagged a bridge (×1.5 wind, §14) and boarded as any bridge. The terrain already leaves a span's ground open, so the lake's basin runs under the deck. The art draws the timber trestle that the ravines' weak trestles use, its bents standing in the water.
    - **A terrain bug it found.** `TerrainField.Nearby` clamps a point behind a branch's toe (or past a spur's end) onto the edge's first (or last) point, and measured the point's lateral across the tangent there, so it came out about 0. frontier:5's alternate toes 230 m past a lake, and its "formation" ran back along main's centreline and filled the lake under the trestle at its own rail height. A `Near` now says when it's `Past` an edge's end (more than 1 m beyond it along the tangent). Such a near stands no formation and no lake fill. Its share of the land's blend is as before, so the land beside a toe is unchanged. Under a fill it never showed (main's formation is the same height). It would also have filled the ground under any main-line bridge within about 300 m before a junction, and laid a strip at rail height on past every spur's buffer stop.
    - **How many:** frontier 1–12, dead lines 1–12 and deep territory 1–12 have 21 crossed lakes, and 8 of them are trestles (frontier:5 two, deadLines:9 three, deadLines:12, deepTerritory:1 and :3 one each). Every one of those lines validates first time.
    - **Verified:** `WatersideTests.SomeCrossedLakesAreTakenOnATrestleWithTheWaterOnUnderIt` (frontier:5, deadLines:9, deadLines:12):
        - timber, no weak limit, named "… Trestle", a landmark;
        - the span covers the water and is no longer than `trestleMaxM`;
        - the lake is wet under the deck, the ground below its level;
        - the stretch is exposed.
      The other waterside tests are unchanged (the formation-at-rail check already skips bridge spans). Seen in `dt screenshot --route deadLines:12 --structure trestle --view trackside`: Bramwell Trestle's bents stand in the black water, the train on the deck. In `--at 6000 --view ahead` the deck runs out across the lake between its riprap banks.

318. **The run map's and the route card's markers where the stops are (B4, queue #57; the director, 7 Oct 2026: "markers on the map in the train dont seem to align properly with stops on the route").** Measured on frontier:7, there were three causes:
    - **The cab map marked each stop at its zone's start** (`RouteFeature.Start`). Where the train stands is the stop point, 150 to 445 m on (Maddox's halt 445 m, the Grain Elevator's yard 345 m). With the train standing at a halt, its red mark sat a marker's width or two past the halt's. `GreyboxScene.MapStop` marks the layout's stop point (`Run.StopWorld`): the platform, or the yard's working track off to its side. On a hand-laid route, whose stops have no layouts, it marks the zone's middle.
    - **The train's red mark sampled the main line at the engine's distance**, which is along its own path. On a spur or an alternate that's a point on main somewhere else. It's now the engine's own place (`CarFrame.Origin`), so in a yard it sits off the line by the yard, where the train is.
    - **The route card's profile** ticked each timetable place at its kilometre (`CardLine.Km`, counted from the outer gate, kilometre post zero, linegen plan §9.7) as if counted from the line's start. That's the same axis as the train's pencil, so every tick was a gate's length (about 1.2 km on frontier:7) early against the train. `PlanHud.ProfileAt` puts a kilometre post where it is on the profile. The 5 km ticks are the posts' too now.
    - **Verified:** `MapMarkerTests`:
        - `TheRunMapMarksEachStopWhereTheTrainStandsAtIt`: every stop on frontier:7 is marked within its stop point's offset of where the train stands, and never at its zone's start.
        - `TheRouteCardTicksEachPlaceWhereTheTrainsPencilWillBeThere`: every main-line landmark's tick is within 60 m of the pencil for a train standing there.
      Both fail without this. `dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 10243 --view cab`, standing at Maddox's halt: the red mark covers the halt's.

319. **An engine short of steam holds the train back (queue #58, D1; the director's test build, 7 Oct 2026: "both heat and pressure are going down, something is wrong with the boiler, and I'm maintaining top speed").** Not a merge fault: main did it too. With steam driving (T97) the pressure sets the speed the engine can make, and the engine pulls only up to it; nothing held the train back above it. With nobody firing at full regulator (a 4-car train on the flat), the fire was out by 90 s and the pressure gone by 240 s, and the train was still at 17 m/s then, 10.6 m/s at 15 minutes: train.json's resistance (not in the spec) is "about 0.019 m/s² at max speed, so a dead boiler coasts for kilometres". T97's own reading ("pressure sets the speed ... the vent (or the brake) for less") wants it both ways.
    - **The rule.** Going faster than its steam can make, the engine holds the train back at `boiler.json` `starvedDecel` (0.12 m/s²) × (1 − the boiler's power factor): none from `workingBandMin` (60) up, all of it at `powerFloor` (20). A ruptured engine keeps its own `ruptureDecel`. 0 puts the old coast back. In the working band nothing changes, so the spec's acceleration and braking tables, the bots' driving and every steady night are as they were.
    - **After:** the same run holds 19 m/s while the pressure's in the band, then falls with it: 17.6 m/s at 120 s (pressure 40), 11.1 at 180 s, stopped by 270 s. GDD §23's "Fire dies: coasting on grade and momentum, brakes only" still holds on a grade; on the flat the coast is now a few minutes, not a quarter of an hour.
    - **Verified:** `BoilerTests.AnEngineWhoseFireDiesSlowsWithItsSteam` (unchanged in the band; under 6 m/s at 240 s where the old coast was still over 16; stopped by 300 s). A 4-bot frontier:7 night with enemies runs exactly as before (4,031 m in 240 s, nobody lost). The Sim suite.

320. **A crew renamed, and deleted, from the fortress (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #59; GDD §9 "each host has three campaign slots"; note 33's "not yet").** A slot's crew was "Crew 1" for good, and a slot once used was used for good: renaming a crew or emptying a slot was `dt campaign`'s alone.
    - **The name is a field on the fortress** (`TextField.CrewName`), as the lobby's is (note 267): chosen, it takes no typing; Enter starts it, Enter or Esc ends it. Each key is kept to the slot at once, as every fortress change is. Up to 24 characters (`FrontEnd.MaxCrewName`, the lobby's). Erased to nothing and left, it's the slot's name again ("Crew 2"); the slot list and the fortress's heading say the slot's name for a blank one either way.
    - **DELETE THIS CREW asks first,** as leaving a night does (note 292): a screen of its own (`Screen.DeleteCrew`, "DELETE NIGHTJARS?"), KEEP IT first so a second Enter keeps it, and what goes said under both: the cars, the scrip, the nights, and a night under way. Confirmed, the slot's file goes (`SaveSlots.Delete`) and the slot list says "Slot 2 is empty."
    - **Verified:** `FrontEndTests.TheFortressRenamesTheCrewAndDeletesItOnlyOnceAskedTwice`; `dt screenshot --menu fortress` and `--menu deletecrew`, looked at.

321. **Audio upkeep: the kit lost in the clerk's voice, and the bot crew's network audio test steady (AU1, queue #60).**
    - **The kit lost, said.** Note 308 added "engineering kit reported lost" and "with car" to `tools/audio/clerk.py`'s phrases, but the bank wasn't rebuilt, so the set broke up over them on the air. `clerk.py` has now read them in the bank's voice (speaker 385; the bank is 215 takes and nothing else was re-read). `ClerkVoiceTests.EveryCauseCardTheStrandedLineAndTheKitLostAreSaidWithNothingBreakingUp` says both shapes of `Radio.KitLost` with nothing breaking up, and it fails on the old bank. The voice booth's Clerk 04 asks the director for both phrases too (note 304).
    - **The flake, found.** `CrewAudioTests.ABotCrewIsHeardOverTheNetworkAsTheAppHearsIt` hosted the night, then built `new GameAudio(Content)`, which loads and decodes every sample in the bank. Nobody stepped the session meanwhile. Under a full suite's load that took 13 s, past the transport's 8 s silence timeout (`DatagramOptions.TimeoutSeconds`), so the host dropped all three bots and the test saw 1 of 4 aboard. Reproduced with 12 busy loops on 4 cores (1 of 4, as A1.2, A1.4 and A1.7 logged), with the session's state logged each second: all four aboard when hosted, then three dropped.
    - **Fixed** by loading the bank before hosting, as the app does. The test was flaky, not the netcode: a real host steps every frame. Under the same load it passed 3 of 3.

322. **Main's new features heard (AU1, queue #61).** An audit of what landed since 7 Oct found sixteen things a player would expect to hear with no sound of their own. Each hook reads only replicated state (GameAudio's rule), and each cue is a line on the audio checklist (`tools/audio/cues.py`).
    - **Healing finds** (note 272), `crew-heal`:
        - while Use is held on one, `apply` per find (`bandages`, `medicine`, `morphine`; the client names a find as the HUD does, `Run.FindOf`);
        - once it's used up (its body gone mid-dose), `done`, a breath let out.
    - **Emotes and outfits** (note 298), `crew-emotes`:
        - `dance`, `wave` and `point` once each where the player stands (a dance moves nobody, so it has no footsteps of its own);
        - `outfit` when a player's outfit changes in the yard.

      What's already on the wire when the client first looks is old news.
    - **The Car Hugger lets go** (note 310), `cs-car-hugger.spit-out`. Eaten or pulled free, its grab ends the same way on the wire, so the spit-out plays only when the crewmate it held is still alive.
    - **A ball lands as what it struck** (note 290), `crew-cannon-impact.flesh`, `.structure` and `.train`. The Track Doll keeps her porcelain, and a surface with no take installed is the boom it was.
    - **Per-creature hurts** (note 290 handed them over), `.hit` for the Gaunt, the Switchman, the Soot Children, the Followers and the Grumbler:
        - a health drop on a record still there (a killing blow takes the record, and that's its death);
        - a Follower's blow on its nest stays the nest's;
        - the blow that turns the Grumbler feral is heard as it turning.
    - **The shovel's rack** (note 275), `crew-melee.shovel-rack-off` and `-on`, at the cab's tool rack as `ShovelOut` changes.
    - **An engine short of steam** (note 319), `state-starved.labour`: a loop under the chuff, as loud as `StarvedDrag` is near its worst (`BedStarved`).
    - **Derelicts shunted out** (note 294), `place-derelict.roll`: a car's seized axles, while a derelict near the ears is moving.
    - **The interface:**
        - `ui-menus.type`, a key for each typing that took into a name (`FrontEnd.Type`, `Erase`);
        - `ui-menus.delete`, the stamp for a crew deleted (the entry's own `Sound`, in place of select);
        - `ui-panels.open`, `close` and `page` for the route card, the supplies and the roster (App);
        - `ui-film.skip`, this player's own film skipped (the session's `SkipHold` reaching its end; `Choices`).
    - **The sounds:** 46 candidates, two per cue where the approach was open, uploaded to the audio checklist and installed first-choice (L1 until kept):
        - foley built from the CC0 packs, the real thing where they have it (`recipes/heard_foley.py`);
        - each creature's hurt from its own established voice and body (`recipes/heard_creatures_ui.py`);
        - the interface matched to the existing paperwork set (ledger, card, typewriter, rubber stamp, the projector's shutter).
    - **Tuning in install.py:**
        - the starved engine's first choice is the beatless one (`FIRST_CHOICE`), since the chuff already beats;
        - a derelict's flats thump once a turn, built at 2.4 m/s, so its loop's rate follows the car's speed (`LAYER_EXTRAS`, the "speed" param `BedWheels` sets).
    - **Not yet:**
        - The mail crane's catch and miss: host-only today, so it needs a replicated field first.
        - D1.1's `sign.<creature>` hook (note 327: a sign shown a crewmate afoot, something moving out there, never its tell) plays each creature's own movement until its sign has a sound of its own.
        - The jig is on wood only; a dance on the ballast or a roof wants its own surfaces.
        - Breaths, swallows, the cork, the syrette's tube, the Switchman's lamp chain and the projector are stand-ins until the Sonniss library.
    - **Verified:**
        - `FeatureSoundTests` (the healing find on a generated night, emotes and outfits, the shovel's rack, the starved engine's level, a derelict shunted, a ball by surface);
        - `CreatureSoundTests.TheCarHuggerIsHeardSpittingOutACrewmatePulledFreeButNotOneEaten` and `ABallOrABlowThatDoesntKillACreatureIsItsOwnHurt`;
        - `UiSoundTests.ANameIsTypedAKeyAtATimeAndACrewDeletedIsStamped`;
        - `ChoiceSoundTests.YourOwnFilmSkippedIsTheCutAndALetGoHoldIsNothing`.

323. **The MODS screen (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #62; note 53's "not yet": "an in-game mods screen"; the wiki's "Playing modded").** What was laid over the game, and what couldn't be, was only on the console (`mods: …`) and in `dt mods`: a player couldn't see from the game which mods they had, though a refused joiner is told which differ.
    - **MODS on the title** (before CREDITS) when anything's installed or couldn't load; with none, there's no MODS. Its line says how many are laid over and how many problems ("2 laid over the game, 1 problem.").
    - **The screen** lists the mods in load order, a row each: its name as it reads (Thunderstore's "LateDispatch" or "Late_Dispatch" as LATE DISPATCH) and version, its description under it. Then each problem from `ContentMods.Scan` ("… isn't loaded: it needs …", "… is installed 2 times …") as a row of its own, the sentence under it. It changes nothing: mods are laid over as the game starts, from its folders or a manager's profile, and BACK's line says so.
    - **`--no-mods`:** the mods are still listed and the heading says they're off. `Mods.Mount` now scans what's installed either way (`Mods.Installed`) and keeps `Mods.Off`; only the enabled scan is laid over, as before.
    - **Verified:** `FrontEndTests.TheModsScreenListsWhatsInstalledInOrderAndWhatCouldntLoad`; `dt screenshot --menu mods` (the example mod from `tools/mods`, and a made-up one missing its dependency), looked at.

324. **A full car says so (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #63; note 37's "not yet": "a human-facing prompt for which car has room"; GDD §32 "a short state only when it stops you").** A crate set down inside a cargo car that's full (`Run`: it loads only while the car's `Load` is under 1) lies there and never loads, and nothing said why: the crew learnt it by watching a crate not go.
    - **The corner says it** while you carry freight (a crate, or a heavy one) inside a full cargo car: "CAR 3 IS FULL" under the crate's name, over its keys (`Hud.Hints`). The car by its stencilled number, so it can be shouted ("car three's full, take it to four").
    - **Only what stops you** (§32): not which car has room, how much is left, or what a crate is worth. Empty-handed, or carrying what isn't freight, a full car says nothing.
    - **Verified:** `HudTests.ACrateCarriedIntoAFullCarSaysTheCarsFull` (half full: nothing; full: the line; empty-handed: nothing); `dt screenshot --hud --full-car --route frontier:7`, looked at.

326. **Explorable village interiors, a first slice (B4, queue #65; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "right now the villages don't have explorable interiors, so we want to see those be things that we can search through in order to find things. This is going to be a big part of the game ... do we split up and try and get more loot that way, or do we focus on just the yard together, or do we focus on just the village together?").** The village houses were solid boxes since T114 ("collisions"), and a find in one was put out on its step.
    - **Which stand open** (`StopBuilding.Open`; stops.json `village.openHouses`). The plain houses, a rectangle or a square, are about half of every village. The L, cross and paired houses stay shut: their parts overlap, and a hollow one needs a plan of its own. No dice decide it, so every stop is laid exactly as before.
    - **The walls** (`StopWalls.OpenWalls`). An open house stands as four walls (`WallThickness` 0.2 m), the one in its `Front` split either side of a door (`DoorWidth` 1.2 m). `Front` is the face that looks most toward the line, the face a shut house's finds are put out on. A crewmate, a cannon ball and a charging creature meet the walls as they met the box, and go in at the door.
    - **The finds** (`StopWalls.FindAt`, `InsideLocal`). A find in an open house lies inside, `FindOut` (0.65 m) out from the wall it was kept against, by kind:
        - at the foot of a cupboard on the back wall, or of a cabinet on a side wall;
        - on the cellar's hatch, or on a run of prised-up boards, out on the floor;
        - a second of a kind across the room from the first.
      A shut house's finds and repair kits go on its step as before.
    - **The art** (`TownKit.OpenHouse`). The sim's walls in plaster with a lintel over the door, a boarded floor, gables and a slate roof, and the cupboard, cabinet, hatch or boards where each find lies. Shut houses keep their modelled props. An open house is drawn from the kit's boxes, so it reads plainer from outside than its modelled neighbours (the art checklist's to take further).
    - **The search, a second slice** (`Run.SpotInReach`, `SearchAct`, `Reveal`; loot.json `search`). Level-design P14 already said village loot sits in "hiding spots ... that take time to search", and the first slice left every find in plain sight in the lamplight. Now each spot in an open house (the cupboard, the cabinet, the cellar's hatch, the boards; `Run.HidingSpots`) keeps its find, and a toy with it, until it's been searched:
        - a crewmate on foot, empty-handed and within `reach` (1 m) of the spot, holds Use for the kind's `seconds`: a cabinet 2, a cupboard 2.5, the cellar 4, the boards 5. Letting go starts it again. Something in hand, Use is that thing's (put down, used), so it's no search;
        - then the find and the toy come out where they'd have lain, the spot is searched, and it's never searched again. Crewmates at one spot don't add up: the furthest through is the spot's progress;
        - the repair kit at a spot still lies out beside it: the bots go for a kit wherever it is (E.12 question 4), and they don't search;
        - shut houses' finds stay on the step, and a barn's hayloft and a shed's bench as they were;
        - with `search` unset, nothing's hidden, as in the first slice. Not in the spec's numbers: a house's few spots take a crewmate about ten seconds, a village a few minutes alone, which is what splitting up buys back.
      The host searches, in `World.CrewAct` after the hands have had their go (a press that picks something up isn't a search). A `Search` record per stop with its loot out carries the containers searched and each spot under way with its progress, so every crewmate's HUD reads "SEARCH THE CUPBOARD : HOLD [E]", then "SEARCHING THE CUPBOARD (40%)". Nothing a client predicts: the player and the train are unchanged by it, and the finds are bodies the host puts out. A spot's searched where it stands, never through a wall: nowhere a crewmate can stand outside a house is within reach of what's kept in it. `Run.Stock(bodies, stop, searched: true)` puts every find out, for tools and tests.
    - **Searched, and it shows** (`StopWalls.Kept`, `GreyboxScene.SearchedSpots`). Where the art stands what a find is kept in, and which way it faces into the room, is the sim's (`StopWalls.Kept`: the cupboard's and cabinet's middles, the hatch and the boards under the find), so `TownKit.OpenHouse` and the hiding spots (`HidingSpot.Kept`, `Facing`) agree. A searched spot is drawn opened over the house's own furniture, from what's searched, so a client sees what the host has:
        - a cupboard's doors swung back past square, its inside dark;
        - a cabinet's drawer out;
        - the cellar's hatch stood up on its hinge over a black hole;
        - the boards laid by the gap they came from.
      `dt screenshot --searched` searches every open house with its finds out on the floor: `--route frontier:7 --at 10200 --cam 10152.2,101.2,1.6 --target 10148.9,104.9,0.7 --lantern --fov 75 --dawn 0.6` is Maddox's house 20's cupboard (`--cam 10152.0,101.5,1.6 --target 10155.4,104.6,0.5` its cabinet); `--at 10350 --cam 10311.6,48.5,1.7 --target 10313.5,51.4,0` house 15's cellar; `--at 19300 --cam 19258.2,-84.3,1.7 --target 19260,-86.3,0` a floor at stop 4. `SearchTests.WhatsKeptStandsInTheHouseFacingTheRoomWithItsFindInFront` pins `Kept`.
    - **Solid furniture** (`StopWalls.Furniture`). An open house's cupboards (1 m by 0.5) and cabinets (0.84 by 0.44) stand in `StopWalls` as boxes like its walls, so a crewmate goes round one rather than through it. The art draws them from the same boxes. A find lies just out from the face, and a crewmate stands within the search's reach of it. `OpenHouseTests` walks from the step to just in front of every find, round the furniture, and finds nobody can stand in a cupboard.
    - **Every house, a third slice** (`StopWalls.Rooms`: `Outline`, `CompositeWalls`, `Doorways`). The L, cross and paired houses stand open too, so `Open` is now every village house (stops.json `village.openHouses`, still with no dice). A house of more than one part is laid out from its outline, the parts' rectangles together:
        - the walls follow the outline's runs. At a corner, a run along x carries on over an inside corner's notch and a run along y stops short of an outside one, so no two walls overlap and no corner is left open;
        - each unit has a door in its longest run facing the line, with open ground outside it. An L or a cross is one unit, its parts open into each other; a pair is two cottages, so two doors. A pair's facing sides, 0.4 m apart, never get a door;
        - what's kept stands against a run's inside face, or out on the floor in front of one. The runs are chosen by the container's index, never the door's run, and the furniture is kept clear of the corners;
        - the art lays the floor by the outline's cells (they don't overlap where a cross's bars do), puts a lintel over each door and a gabled roof over each part, its ridge along the part's longer side.
      A plain house keeps its own four walls, unchanged. The walk-in test now flood-fills from outside each house on a 10 cm grid instead of walking straight lines (an L's corner is in the way): every door reaches in, every find is got to, nothing crosses into a house except at a door, and nobody stands in a cupboard. `PlayerMotor` now pushes a crewmate out of the walls near them until they settle (up to four passes, in the walls' fixed order). Pushed out of one wall, they could end up in the next, in an inside corner or against a door's jamb. Seen at frontier:7: `dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 10250 --cam 10258,78,3 --target 10253.3,92.3,1.5 --dawn 0.6 --fov 60` is an L at Maddox (`--cam 10254.5,88.6,1.6 --target 10252,95,0.8 --lantern --fov 85 --searched` is inside it); `--at 10300 --cam 10297,64,3 --target 10291.8,77.5,1.5` is a cross; `--at 12050 --cam 12002,-56,3 --target 12010.8,-67.1,1.5` is a pair.
    - **The director's notes of 8 Oct: the light and the finds** (GDD App. F.3: "some lighting inside, dim to keep it scary ... loot needs to be discoverable in there ... a bit of a brighter more unique look ... good texture work, not VFX").
        - *Dim inside* (`GreyboxScene.HouseInteriors`, `TownKit.HouseLight`). Each part of an open house is an enclosed space for the renderer (`Room`), so the moon and the sky stay outside it. Its one light is a candle stub guttering on a saucer in a corner, the first corner clear of the furniture and the finds; one house in three (or one with no clear corner) has a tin oil lamp turned right down, hung from the middle of its ceiling. Both are dim and warm, the candle flickering more than the lamp, with a small halo at the flame so the light reads as coming from it. A crewmate's lamp is the light to search by. Only the houses within 40 m of the eye are lit.
        - *Finds that stand out* (`FindKit`; `tools/art/texgen/mat_finds.py`, the `finds_atlas` texture). Each kind of find is its own model, wearing its own cell of a new 4×4 atlas of clean, bright stock: a red tin label, striped toffee paper, blue candle wrapping, a chemist's label, a white bandage packet with a red cross, a white enamel tin, gingham over a jar of plum, a chrome-yellow paraffin tin, a red oilcloth tool roll, green baize with a brass plate, a white watch face in gilt, polished brass, manila. It's the brightest, most saturated thing in a worn grey room, with a paper sheen and a metal glint in its spec, so a lamp picks the finds out by their surfaces. Nothing glows: the medicine bottle and the jam jar are brown and plum glass, not the emissive lamp lens. The models are drawn at 1.35 times life about their base (the body is still a 0.15 m ball), to read across a dark room.
      `HouseInteriorArtTests` pins both: the atlas's cells (index.json) match `FindKit`'s order, every loot.json item has its own model, and every house's light stands inside it, out of its walls and clear of its furniture. Seen without a lamp (`--route frontier:7 --at 10250 --cam 10254.5,88.6,1.6 --target 10252,95,0.8 --fov 85`: the L's candle on its far wall) and with one, searched (`--at 10200 --cam 10153.6,102.4,1.5 --target 10155.0,104.3,0.2 --fov 60 --lantern --searched`: the bandage packet at the cabinet's foot).
    - **The director's notes of 8 Oct: ransacked, and a monster nesting** (GDD App. F.3: "procedurally generated furniture scattered about, like the place has been ransacked many times before ... sometimes a monster should be nesting in there").
        - *Ransacked* (`StopWalls.ClutterOf`, `RansackKit.Piece`). Each open house's clutter is dealt from the stop's seed and the house's index, on a stream of its own (`ClutterStream`), so the stop is laid exactly as before and every machine has the same mess. It has two or three heavy pieces, each against a run of wall with no door: a table (stood with a leg kicked out, or overturned with its legs into the room), an iron bed with its mattress slashed and the stuffing out, a dresser pulled over on its face with its drawers under it. These are solid, part of `StopWalls` like the cupboards. It also has eight to fourteen things underfoot that aren't solid: chairs (mostly knocked over), crates (some stove in), drawers turned out and dropped, a shelf's planks, heaps of rags, letters and forms, smashed crockery, a picture face down, a bucket kicked over. None of it stands on a find, on the spot in front of one where a crewmate searches, in a doorway, or on the nest. A candle never stands under a heavy piece. The walk-in test flood-fills round all of it.
        - *A monster nesting.* The Gaunt has roosted in the village house furthest from the train since note 309, and it starts asleep there when the director sends it. Now the house shows it (`StopWalls.Nest`, `RansackKit.Nest`): a hollow of trodden filth ringed with bedding and stuffing matted into heaps, gnawed bones pale against it, and no light at all. Every other house has its candle or lamp, so a dark doorway in a lit village is the tell. In a house of parts the roost was its building's middle, which can be in a wall; now it's the middle of its biggest stretch of floor. Nothing else about where or when the Gaunt spawns changes (D1's #66 holds what's met off the train).
      `OpenHouseTests.EveryOpenHouseIsRansackedTheSameOnEveryMachine` and `HouseInteriorArtTests` pin it: the same clutter twice from the same seed, inside the house, heavy pieces clear of the nest, the nest's house dark. Seen from the ceiling by lantern (`--route frontier:7 --at 10200 --cam 10152,101.9,2.8 --target 10152.05,101.9,0 --fov 110 --lantern --dawn 0.6`: Maddox's house 20, the Gaunt's) and from its door.
    - **A bot crew splits up for the village** (`StopHand.Village`, `FootPath`; facilities.json `crew.village*`). GDD App. F.3's choice, made by the bots too. Once the yard's crates are in, up to `villageShare` (half) of the crate hands go to the village's open houses, while the rest shut the doors. Each one:
        - takes the nearest hiding spot nobody else has claimed, within `villageReach` (150 m), and says so on the crew's calls (`CrewCalls.ClaimSpot`), so the next hand goes elsewhere;
        - walks there by `FootPath`, an A* over a 25 cm grid kept clear of the stops' walls (the houses, their furniture, the heavy clutter) and of the train. The train is one wall: its steps stand out past its sides, and the coupling gaps aren't a way through;
        - holds Use at the spot until it's searched, as anyone does, and picks up what comes out;
        - carries it back by a way round the houses to a cargo car's steps, where the crate hand's own way takes it up and in. A shut door makes it put the find down on the landing, open up, and take it up again.

      The driver doesn't call the loading done while any hand alive is out (`CrewCalls.Scavenging`), within its give-ups as before. A hand called back (the dawn, a give-up) comes home by a planned way, not straight at the train through the houses. Nobody goes with less than `villageDawnSpare` (15 min) of the night left. A bot crew without loot (the stop-crew tests) never goes. `StopCrewTests.WithTheCratesInHalfTheHandsSearchTheVillageAndBringTheFindsAboard` pins it: the crates in, at most half the hands out at once, spots searched, finds stowed, everyone back and the train whole.
    - **Rooms** (`StopWalls.Partition`, `InnerWall`, `InnerDoorways`). The bigger houses are cut into rooms, so a house is somewhere to go through, not one glance from the door (GDD App. F.3's "explorable interiors"). From the house alone, with no dice, so every machine has the same walls and the stop is laid as before:
        - an L's wing is walled off along its seam with the main part, with a doorway (`DoorWidth`) in the middle of the wall;
        - a plain house (a rectangle or a square) `RoomsFrom` (9 m) or longer has a back room, `BackRoom` (0.38) of its length, across the end away from its door. With the door in a side, the back room's end is the house's variant's. Its doorway is a fifth of the house's width off the middle, toward a side. A cross's arms and a pair's cottages stay as they were;
        - such a house is laid from its outline like an L (`Composite` is true for it): the floor's cells are cut at the inner wall, and the outside's runs end where it meets them, so each room has its own walls and corners. The inner wall's two faces are runs too (`WallRun.Inner`), either side of the doorway. What's kept stands against them as against any wall, and the heavy clutter as well. No door goes in them, and the walls stand from them as the inner wall itself, between the outside walls' inner faces;
        - the clutter keeps a metre clear either side of the inner doorway, and the light's corners are the outside's, so the back room is often the dark one;
        - the art puts a lintel over the inner doorway, and across a plain house the wall goes on up into the gable under the ridge;
        - the Gaunt's roost in such a house is in the middle of its biggest room, as it already was for an L.
      `OpenHouseTests.TheBiggerHousesHaveABackRoomThroughADoorway` (frontier:7, deadLines:2, local:3, deepTerritory:2) pins it, with the walk-in flood fill:
        - only a long plain house or an L has rooms;
        - the inner doorway is walkable from both sides, and the wall is solid away from it;
        - some floor in every room is got to;
        - no two pieces of furniture stand in each other.
      `YouWalkInAtTheDoorAndTheFindsAreInside` still has every find got to. Seen by lantern in `dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 10190 --lantern --fov 80`: `--cam 10208.4,72.6,1.6 --target 10212.0,75.0,1.3` is Maddox's house 1, from its door to the back room's doorway, and `--cam 10211.1,74.2,1.6 --target 10213.5,76.5,1.0` is in its doorway.
    - **Boarded windows** (`TownKit.BoardedWindows`). Every village house is open now, and an open house was a plaster box with a doorway, where the modelled shut houses had windows (GDD §30's dead settlements; the Wiki's "windows boarded over with raw planks"). Each run of its outside wall with no door has one or two windows, as fit with about a metre of wall either side, spread along it. Each is a pale trim frame and sill round a black pane, three raw planks nailed across it, ragged and off level by the house's variant, and the planks' backs on the inside face. Art only: the wall is as solid behind them as anywhere. Seen at Maddox from the street (`dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 10190 --lantern --cam 10196,40,2.5 --target 10222,62,1.5 --fov 75`) against the same view on main, which has blank walls.
    - **Not yet:**
        - A stair: ground floor only.
        - Doors that shut: done (note 401).
        - B2's walk-in town houses (#194) are a fortress's, built separately; when they land, the two can share a kit.
    - **Verified:** `OpenHouseTests.YouWalkInAtTheDoorAndTheFindsAreInside` (frontier:7, deadLines:2):
        - every plain house is open and no other kind is;
        - from the step to the middle is walkable for a crewmate's width, and from behind the back wall it isn't;
        - every find in an open house is inside it and walkable to from the step;
        - a shut house's finds are outside it.
      `SearchTests` (frontier:7): an open house's spots keep their finds through a held search that's let go short and starts again, and give them up held through, once; a crewmate carrying something doesn't search; nowhere a crewmate can stand outside a house reaches a spot in it; a client sees the search under way and then done.
      Seen in `dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 10200 --cam 10156,88,2.2 --target 10152,101.9,1.4 --dawn 0.6` (Maddox's house 20 from the street: the doorway dark in its front wall) and `--cam 10154.5,99.5,1.7 --target 10151,104.5,0.6 --lantern --fov 80` (inside: the boards, the cupboard against the back wall, the cabinet against the side).

327. **A presence of threat off the train (queue #66, D1 (D1.1); GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "ideally, we want people to be feeling like when they leave, there is this presence of threat at all times. ... Or at least up the perceived threat factor").** Off the train, exploring a village, nothing much happened: the director spends on the train's night, and only a crewmate the train had left (note 273) had a pressure of their own. Now the crew afoot are watched, and draw the night on. `enemies.json` `director.afoot`; not in the spec.
    - **Afoot:** alive on the ground, further than `fromTrainM` (20 m) from every car's footprint (`Director.FromTrain`), outside the forts. Worked out once a second by the host's director (`Director.Watch`), out of the safe yard, as the draws are.
    - **Perceived threat: signs.** `firstSign` (6 s) after someone first steps off, then every `signEvery` (12–24 s, the director's own dice) while anyone's out, one of them in turn is shown a sign (`World.Watcher`, replicated on the world record like the draw's answer, note 287): a pair of eyes for `signSeconds` (3.5) at `signOut` (14–22 m: the hand lamp's edge), within `signSpread` (35°) of the bearing of a creature that lives at this stop (one kind drawn from those with a site within `signReach` 160 m, note 309's lairs; that kind's nearest site, so a village with a warren, a roost and a child's call shows all three in time), at its eye height (`signHeight`: a Ribbit's 0.35 m off the ground, the Gaunt's 2.3), and its sound from there.
