Not through a wall: the bearing drawn, then others across the spread, the first with a clear line that far past the stop's walls (`Train.Walls`) and every building's footprint (an open house's door gap is no way through, note 326; and the art draws buildings the sim doesn't wall); with none, short of the first wall (something at a house's corner), and none at all if that's nearer than half the lamp's edge. **Honest** (App. F.1's rule: a tell the rules can back): only a creature whose site is here and that the night could send; with no site in reach, a Ribbit's (they come for whoever's on the ground anywhere, App. A.6), from away from the train. A sign is never a spawn: nothing's there when you walk up to it; what lives there is.
    - **Its sound** (`GameAudio.Watched`): a hook for the audio chat (`sign.<kind>`: `sign.ribbits`, `sign.gaunt`, …); until it's made, the creature's own movement, at 0.7, never its tell (a tell means it's coming; a sign only that it's there): a Ribbit landing a hop, the Grumbler's scuttle, a Soot Child's turn, the Whistler running. The Gaunt and the Followers make no sound of their own until they're on you: theirs is the eyes alone.
    - **Real pressure.** While anyone's afoot the night's pressure builds by + `perSecond` (0.08) × the share of the living afoot, inside the pressure model's other factors (tier, conditions, relief, busy, escalation; note 266): with half the crew out, 0.04 on top of the base (0.03) and the quiet ramp at its full (0.1): about a third faster, and more than twice the base before the quiet has built. And what it sends then is more often met out there: the outside zone's creatures and whatever lives at the stops' sites (`Director.Outdoors`) weigh × (1 + (`outsideWeight` 2.5 − 1) × that share). The caps, the budget, the gates (a solo night still meets no Ribbits, Soot Children or Gaunt: their rules want a crew of two or more), the sites they start from (note 309) and the left-behind's own hunts (note 273) are as they were. `on: false` is the night as it was (`AfootTests` pins it to the rate).
    - **`dt afoot --route frontier:7 [--seconds 300]`:** the director's walk, headless. The train stands at the line's first stop with a village, under way past the grace; one crewmate walks doorstep to doorstep through it, and the night runs as the host runs it, twice: `after` (afoot on) and `before` (off). Signs by kind, the director's spawns and the threats that telegraphed, with their times from arrival. The bots never get 20 m from the train (a 4-bot `dt harness` night: 0 crew-seconds afoot; a 4-bot playthrough: 10), so they can't show it.
    - **Seeing one:** `dt afoot` lists every sign shown (`shown`: when, whose, and where the walker's eyes and the sign's were, in line coordinates), and `dt screenshot --route frontier:7 --at 5450 --cam <eye> --target <sign> --watcher <sign>` draws it from there. Looked at on frontier:7's village: a Ribbit's eyes low in the gap between two houses, a Soot Child's out past the end of an alley, a Gaunt's half behind a porch post (a glimpse, and fair).
    - **Before and after** (`dt afoot`, 300 s, solo): frontier:7, first spawn at 78 s → 45 s, 4 spawns → 6, and 9 signs (Soot Child 5, Ribbit 3, Gaunt 1; 17 once B4's open houses (note 326) stopped blocking the sightlines: Gaunt 9, Soot Child 5, Ribbit 3); frontier:3, 49 s → 25 s, 6 → 7, the Whistler on them 2 times → 3, 16 signs; frontier:11, 62 s → 34 s, Whistler 2 → 3, 13 signs; deepTerritory:2, 27 s → 13 s, Whistler 2 → 3, 17 signs; deadLines:5 (a Ribbit hunt took the walker at 79 s either way), 2 signs. The first sign 5 s after stepping off, every time.
    - **Verified:** `AfootTests` (signs from the warren at a stop: first at `firstSign`, one every `signEvery`, toward the site within the spread, at the lamp's edge, at a Ribbit's height, all of what lives there, none a spawn; aboard, nothing, and the rate exactly as `on: false`'s; the afoot term is `perSecond` × the share; what's outdoors and what isn't; the sign on the world record for every machine). `dt playthrough --route frontier:7 --bots 4` photographs every sign from the watched crewmate's eyes (`sign-<kind>` shots; frontier:7's one, a Follower's eyes by a yard wall, looked at) and reports `afoot`, as `dt harness` does. AudioTests, NetcodeTests and the Sim suite.

328. **The threat orchestrator, and the run between stops (D1.2 for D1, queue #67; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "on the train, still relatively boring from point A to point B ... more threats that can board the train at speed ... tower defense style that gives our gunners things to do ... a threat orchestrator that takes into account how many players are on").** The design outline is [docs/design/orchestrator.md](design/orchestrator.md), linked from GDD App. B.1.
    - **Why a fast train is boring, by the numbers:** the train's top speed is 22 m/s, the Cinder Hounds can't board above 19 and the Climbers get a grip only under 14 (note 286); the rest come at stops. Kept hot and never stopped, only the Car Hugger (lying in wait on low ground) can land, which is the director's playtest. App. F.1's boarding-first decision made the hauling train safe on purpose and left "a fast, flying class" for later.
    - **The outline:** an orchestrator over the director (a census each second of who's active, at which post, and how long since each had something to answer; a live crew multiplier, per-player caps, and the post with the most slack favoured); upkeep jobs while the train runs (U1–U6, hot boxes, loose couplings, lamps, powder to the guns); threats that board at speed (S1–S5); waves at the guns (§5.3); pacing targets P1–P8; the director's changes D1–D7; and five questions for the director, the first being §15's "scaling by train length, not enemy count multipliers", which scaling by active players changes.
    - **Built, the first piece: the hound run** (orchestrator.md §5.3, §6.1; enemies.json `director.run`; `Director.Runs`, `CinderHound.Runner`). A train that has run 2.4 km at 19 m/s or more since it last slowed under 2 m/s (×0.75 with the boiler over its working band) draws a stream of Cinder Hounds: round(1.4 + 0.6 × the crew alive), 2 to 6 (2 at crew 1, 3 at 2, 4 at 4, 6 at 8), in pairs 6 s apart on alternating flanks, 200 m behind the rear car. A runner howls (the pack's 4 s telegraph), then closes at the train's speed + 5 m/s whatever that is, and leaps aboard the rear car from 30 m as the director's hounds do, at any speed (the director's packs can't board above 19 m/s; the train makes 22). About 38 s a pair from howl to leap. **Why 19:** it's the director's packs' own top speed: under it they board, and outrunning them stays their counter (App. F.1, Decided: "outrunning them means going fast, which risks derailing"; note 286's table). The run is what answers going faster than that, the top-speed strategy App. F.1 left for later, so running hot is a choice between the bends and the guns.
    - **Answered one at a time:** a ball landing within 5 m of a runner scatters it (break off), and one on it kills it (note 290), so a ball between a pair (4 m apart across, 3 m along) takes both. A round fired near but not at it doesn't: the director's packs keep `suppressRounds` (one round anywhere within 220 m sends a pack off). `EnemyContext.Landed` is the tick's ball landings (not one stopped by the train's own body). Missed, a runner is the pack fight aboard the rear car (App. A.3, staying aboard: note 269).
    - **Where it sits:** outside the budget and the caps, like the left-behind's hunts (note 273): the fast train's own. Nothing in the grace, a fort, the final approach or the terminus' safe stretch, at a stop or with the run not under way; one run at a time (the count starts again once its last runner is dealt with), and a train that slows mid-run sends no more of its pairs. Its own dice (stream 0x4A11), so the night's other draws are untouched. Host only: `Runner` isn't replicated; a client draws a runner as any hound.
    - **Headless:** `dt harness ... --enemies` reports `threats.houndRuns` (each run's time, km, size, crew, hot, and its runners scattered, killed and aboard). Seen: `dt screenshot --run --view run` (three pairs closing on the rear car and its gun, off the line's left; the fog hides a hound past about 40 m, so the staged pairs are closer than a real run's).
    - **Verified:** `HoundRunTests`: a 21 m/s train with four aboard draws a run of four after the grace, both flanks, every runner boarding at 21 m/s when nobody shoots, and no second run while they're aboard; the size at crews 1, 2, 4 and 8; a ball landing between a pair scatters both, one landing 150 m off doesn't; no run at 18 m/s (under the packs' 19), 12 m/s or at a stand; slowing starts the count again. `TheGunnerAtTheGuardGunAnswersTheRun`: the gunner bot at the guard van's gun, a run of two behind a 21 m/s train: 7 rounds, both killed on the line, none aboard. A 4-bot harness night (frontier:7, 900 s) drew no run: the bots haul at cruise (14 m/s) and stop, which is the point; the harness has no top-speed driver yet. The Sim suite, NetcodeTests included.

329. **The cannon's traverse sound, low and slow (queue #68, D1; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "there's a weird sound that is happening when the cannon turns. I think we just get rid of that altogether, or make it something that's a lot more low and slow. Right now it just feels like this weird high repeated sound").** It was `gun-lay`'s "gear's teeth": an impulse train at 6–28 Hz band-passed at 1.8 kHz with a 6 dB peak at 3.1 kHz, over a steam hiss band-passed at 2.6 kHz. Now the gear is a clunk 2–5 times a second under a 420 Hz low-pass with a 180 Hz peak, the steam a breath under 500 Hz, and the motor's hum (32–44 Hz, under 220 Hz) carries it; its reach is 60 m, not 90. The traverse-stop clunk (a recorded take) is unchanged. AU1 owns audio and has recorded candidates for the gun's lay on #205; whichever lands, this is the synth fallback. Verified: `dt audio render --sound gun-lay --param speed=1` (the spectrogram's top half silent), `CrewAudioTests` and `AudioTests` 49/49.
330. **A derailment that commits (queue #69, D1; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "derailments are feeling quite underwhelming ... took a curve going into a yard at 30 kilometers an hour ... glided off the rails ... add a little bit of impulse there ... more drama").** Every launch in the wreck was a share of the speed (the first car thrown sideways at 0.3 of it, the rest jostled at 0.35), so at 8.3 m/s the first car came off at 2.5 m/s, nothing rolled past 9°, and the train slid to a stop on its wheels. Now there's a floor, whatever the speed (wreck.json): the first car's thrown at least `kickMin` 4 m/s sideways and, when that floor's what threw it, popped up `kickUp` 3 m/s as its flange climbs the rail (at 80 km/h the pop made the wreck grind over the opera, `AudioTests`); each car after is thrown at least `jostleMin` 2.5 m/s, hops `jostleUp` 2 m/s and tips `jostleRoll` 1.4 rad/s the way it's thrown. At 30 km/h (and at 18) every car goes over now, one after another down the train; at 80 km/h it's much as it was (the shares there are mostly over the floors). Not in the GDD's numbers (App. E covers the crew's fling, not the cars'); by eye on `dt screenshot --wreck 2 --speed 8.3`. Pinned by `WreckTests.AThirtyKilometreDerailGoesOverRatherThanGlidingOff`. The crew's own fling already had a floor (E.10's `minKickSpeed`), so whoever's aboard is thrown with it.
331. **The hot box, the first upkeep job while the train runs (queue #71, D1; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "on the train, still relatively boring from point A to point B ... things players do to maintain the train while it runs"; [orchestrator.md](design/orchestrator.md) §5.1 U1).**
    - **What it is.** Every `everyMetres` (2.5 km ± half) of the train's running, more above 18 m/s, a car drawn from those running cool has its rear axle box run dry: `Vehicle.HotBox`, the seconds it's been hot. None in the first 2 km, none in the yard or a fort, never more open than there are crewmates alive (at least one). The engine's own never does. All in the new `content/tuning/upkeep.json`.
    - **The tell.** A dry squeal at the box (`hotbox`, a synth loop: 1.25–1.65 kHz wavering, harsher as it heats), and from about 15 s smoke off the bogie, thick and dark by the end, the box glowing dull red from about 40 s (`Effects.HotBoxSmoke`; `dt screenshot --view hotbox --hotbox 100`).
    - **The fix.** Use held 3 s with the hands within 3 m of the box, on the rear bogie outside the wheel: from the coupling gap behind the car, its end ladder, or the ground beside it (`HotBoxes.Within`; never from the roof or inside). The prompt says GREASE THE HOT BOX. The outline's oil can from the lampman's locker is left out: the grease is at the box, until there's a can to carry.
    - **Left alone.** After 60 s it drags: each box takes 2 m/s off the top speed, held there as the Car Hugger holds its cap (1.1× what the engine can pull, over the cap; a flat 0.15 m/s² was out-pulled). After 120 s it catches: a car fire at the bogie (App. C.5), and the box is done.
    - **Readings.** The outline's "every 4 km of running per car" would be 29 boxes on a 23 km night of five cars; read as one somewhere in the train every 2.5 km, about eight a night. The cap is the outline's "one job open per active player".
    - **Netcode.** The host brings boxes on and sets the fires; the seconds count on every machine (prediction drags as the host does), and greasing is predicted like the hands' other work. The vehicle record carries `HotBox` (protocol 35).
    - **Bots.** A bot in reach of a hot box greases it (`Heed.HotBox`, before a rescue). And a roof walker goes to the nearest one nobody's at: along the roofs to its car, down the end ladder into the gap behind it, and Use held there (`RoofWalkerBot.Grease`; the box is in reach from the ladder's foot). On a 4-bot frontier:7 night with boxes made frequent (every 600 m), 6 of 10 were greased and 3 caught; the same night without the errand, 4 of 9 and 4 caught. The rest are boxes that come on while the walkers are at a stop's work, warming, or after the pack. The harness takes `--upkeep`; without it a harness night has none, so the soak, the balance sweep and the tests are as they were.
    - **Verified.** `HotBoxTests` (7; the walker's errand: one walker greases a box set 20 s in, before it drags, and never does without it): one comes on by the train's running, one at a time with nobody aboard; left alone it holds the train 2 m/s under its top speed; left too long the car's alight; greased from the gap behind and from the ground beside; not from the roof. The screenshot, looked at.
291. **The Look Review's open creature notes (the director, 6 Oct 2026; queue #29, E1).** Six notes on the creatures had no reply. Each was looked at in the reel and the turntables, and is answered in the model or its clips.
    - **The Ribbit's geometry "that doesn't seem quite attached."** Seen from four sides, the hind feet were flat planks laid by the legs. The ears were boards stood up off the skull. The hands were a disc on a stick with a brush of fingers. The jaw was a thin tray under rings of lip, and there was a crease all round the neck. Now the skull is fused into the body's skin (`kit.fuse("body", ["body", "legs", "skull"])`). The hind feet are a hare's, with a heel, a thick sole and four toes grown into the leg. The forearm runs on into the hand's heel, and the fingers have knuckles and a thumb. The jaw is a heavy, rolled scoop of its own fused skin. The ears are lop ears, rooted deep in the skull, hanging down past the neck.
    - **"The swell needs to be much bigger, the tongue has no actual tongue."** The sac's pivot is now its top, under the chin. Swelling, it balloons to a pale, veined ball bigger than the head, out in front of the chest. The head stays level for it, as a calling toad's does; before, the swell pose tipped the head back 56°. The tongue is modelled: broad, flat and wet, with a groove, lying in the mouth's floor, and a sticky club at its end. `tongue_01` scaled along itself shoots it out; `tongue_02`, the club, is scaled back so it stays round. In the `tongue` clip it's 7× its length. In the game `CreatureArt.Lash` aims it at the catch's chest and stretches it until the club is on them. That replaces the cylinder the engine drew. With nobody to reach, it's drawn back to the length it lies in the mouth. `RibbitTests.OnItsCatchItsTongueIsOutToThem` holds it to the chest, as before.
    - **The Cinder Hounds' animations, "a full overhaul with much better quality."** The paws are placed by IK on footfall paths, not swung by angle tables. In each gait a paw is down for its duty, sliding back under the body, then picked up, folded and swung through. The pitch of the foot and toes (hind) or the hand and fingers (fore) is set through the stride, and the stifle is held forward of the hip-to-hock line, the elbow behind (`paw`, `stride`). On that, the gallop is a rotary one, hind left, hind right, fore right, fore left, in 14 frames. It has a gathered suspension (all four off the ground, the spine bowed) and an extended one, the body pitching over the forelegs. The head is steadied against all of it, and the tail streams out, each bone a beat behind. The prowl is a lateral walk: the shoulder blades roll over each step and the back sways. Its stop now holds a forepaw up off the ground while the head snaps round. The crouch, lunge, bite and hit are posed with planted paws. The lunge sinks before it goes, flies with the forelegs out past the head, and lands within 0.45 m of the sim's place, so the cut to the bite doesn't jump. The feet planter is gone. Every clip's paws now rest on the ground (lowest −0.002 m) and leave it only in a stride's flight. The checks are the stick figures of every frame and `CreatureArtTests`.
    - **The Switchman's "little shuffle flee: a bit more fluid, slow, and intentioned."** The flee was 20 frames on four linear keys. It is now two long strides over 2.1 s, keyed every four frames and eased. The weight rolls over each planted foot before the other is dragged through. The hips and shoulders turn against each other, the lantern swings behind the walk, and once a cycle the head turns round over its shoulder, unhurried, to look back at the train. (In the game the sim goes from BreakOff to Gone at once, so the flee is the reel's and the Look Review's.)
    - **The Tippy-toesie, "a general more creepiness."** Its hunch is curled tighter, the neck craned out and the head cocked over too far. The stalk is the checklist's exaggerated slow tiptoe: the knee drawn up to the chest and held, the head popping over to the other side, the foot let down slow. Waiting, its head lolls over much too far and goes further. Then it's upright all at once, turned full on you, and goes slowly back over while its fingers ripple, one after another. Fleeing, it scuttles low with its arms folded up like a mantis's and its head turned round, still on you. The shush finger is put to the face after the head is cocked, and the folded hands are placed by IK before their own shoulders, so `dt art clearance` stays clean (CreatureArtTests). The hunch is eased just enough that it still stands over a door's height on its points, so `TippyToesieTests` (its heights against the door and the roof) passes unchanged.
    - **The Choir, "more ethereal and ghostly."** The bell and the tendrils are ghost parts. A part named `ghost…` (`MeshPart.Ghost`) carries `Skinner.GhostWear` (−1, which no real wear is), and the scene shader draws it screen-door transparent by the view, as the era's games drew a ghost (`bayer4`). It is thin and see-through face on, dense at the rim where the eye looks through more membrane, and the rim gives off a faint cold of its own. The child's mouth and its teeth stay solid, hanging in a bell you can barely see. The drift's tendrils move in slower, wider waves, and the bell turns a little as it goes. The flag is on the part because the bake (tools/models overbake) merges a model's materials into one atlas, so a material name doesn't survive it.
    - **rig.fuse, two fixes.** Edges left with no face (a fold the dissolve closed up) are deleted first; on their own they made QuadriFlow call the whole skin not manifold, and the skin fell back to the collapse's uneven triangles. The Ribbit's body and jaw are QuadriFlow's now. `kit.fuse(..., lose=)` says how much of the union QuadriFlow may smooth over before the collapse is used instead; the default 1.5% is unchanged, and the Ribbit's body takes 3% for the groove under its lip.
    - **Found on the way:** a shader with more than one non-ASCII character in it fails to compile ("unexpected end of file"). The shader text seems to be handed to the compiler sized in characters, not UTF-8 bytes, so each multi-byte character drops a byte off the end; scene.frag's one ü fits in its trailing newline. Keep shader comments ASCII.
    - **Verified:** the full suite (1,660 tests; the one network-timing test that failed under load passes on its own), `CreatureArtTests`, `RibbitTests`, `TippyToesieTests`, `dt art clearance`, budgets (Ribbit 7,948 of 8,000 triangles; hound 4,746; Switchman 8,699 of 9,000; Choir 2,948 of 3,000; Tippy-toesie 8,484). Looked at: `dt art reel` for every changed clip, `dt art clip` turntables, `dt screenshot --view choir --threats`.

306. **The crew's emotes, the clips (queue #44, E1; F1's #217, note 298).** #217's emote wheel plays crew clips named `dance`, `wave` and `point` when crew_clips has them, and poses the arms by IK over the walk or the idle until then. They're in `tools/blender/crew_clips.py` now, so #217 picks them up with no code change. `CreatureArt.Crewmate` loops each from the crewmate's own beat (the variant's offset), so the wave and the point are holds that loop from anywhere, not a start and an end.
    - **wave** (1 s loop): the right hand up over the shoulder, open, waved from the elbow; the weight on one hip, the head tipped.
    - **point** (2 s loop): the right arm straight out ahead at the shoulder's height, the hand flat along it, the eyes down it (`look_at`); the left hand on the hip; a jab of emphasis once a second.
    - **dance** (4 s loop, twice over player.json's 8 s): a workman's jig in heavy boots (§31). For two bars it stamps knee-lifts on a two-a-second beat with the fists pumped up over the head on the beat. Then come two bars of a side-to-side shuffle, the hips swinging, the fists up before the chest and the elbows out flapping like a hen's, the head bobbing a beat behind.
    - **Verified:** `dt art clearance --only crew --clips dance,wave,point` is clean (the fists first sat in the coat at the armpits; now they're out before the chest). `CreatureArtTests`, `CrewActsTests`. `dt art clip crew wave|point|dance` looked at.

307. **The trailer, re-cut and heard (queue #46, E1; the art checklist's "trailer", GDD §36: Next Fest pulls trailers on 18 Jan 2027).** `dt trailer` was silent, and cut before most of the creatures had their art: its one creature shot was the Tippy-toesie in an aisle.
    - **The cut** (58 s at 24 fps):
      - title card; the train out of the fog; card; the crew on the roofs; card ("SOMETHING RUNS BESIDE IT");
      - the Cinder Hounds running the train down, from low behind the pack;
      - the Switchman at his lever, his hand on it (COMMIT), the lamp coming at him out of the fog until the engine goes by;
      - card ("SOMETHING IS ABOARD"); the Tippy-toesie in the aisle; a Car Hugger eating the rear car; the Choir's ghosts over the guard van; the cannon at the pack, from the gunner's seat;
      - card; the dawn; the end card.

      The creatures are staged as the screenshots stage them (`Staging.Threats` and its modes), staged afresh where the train is each frame, and that far into what they're doing. The Switchman's beat is the exception: it's staged once, with its camera, so he stays by the line while the train comes on. The pack is brought in close behind the guard van for the trailer only, in the hounds' beat and the cannon's (the screenshots' stand 14 to 26 m back).
    - **The sound is the game's own.** `GameAudio` runs offline, every take decoded on demand (as `dt audio render` and `dt film` run it). It's updated each sim tick from the shot's camera (under a card, from car 1's roof) and mixed on to keep time with the ticks.
      - The beat's creatures are mirrored into the world for the mixer to find, then taken out again before the next tick, so the night itself never meets them.
      - Only the beat's own creatures are heard (the hounds in theirs, the Switchman in his), so its tell isn't buried under every other creature's.
      - The Choir's beat has it gathering (`ChoirState.Build` 0.8: five voices of eight), not the full swarm. The swarm at the guard van hit full scale, 17 dB over the rest of the cut. The cannon's shots are heard where the muzzle is.
      - **The master** (`--level`, -18 dBFS RMS over the whole cut) brings the game's mix up to a trailer's loudness. The game's own mix sat about -21 dBFS, leaving headroom for its tells. A soft limiter over a knee at 0.8 then rounds a gunshot or a close tell off under full scale.
      - There's no score: what's heard is the night itself (the train, the tells, the guns). A score is the director's call. E.6's music is the derailment's, and a trailer that ends on a derailment (GDD open question 3) would bring the opera with it.
    - **Out:** out/trailer/frames, `trailer.wav` with its spectrogram, and `trailer.mp4` (H.264 and AAC) with a contact sheet, through FilmCommands' ffmpeg finder. `--beats i,j` renders only those beats, to look at a shot.
    - **Found on the way:** a steam-driven session starts with its brake on (`PrototypeSession`: `Brake = 1` under `SteamDrive`). The old trailer set the throttle but never let the brake off, and the train ended the cut standing (0 km/h). It now runs 45 to 66 km/h through the cut.

311. **The engine's front, a second pass (queue #50, E1; the director, 7 Oct 2026: "it just looks like we took the old classic boiler train and then flipped it around … a cooler post-apocalyptic redesign that still allows us to have that forward control … more lines to it, more curves to it. It didn't look like it was just like a box slapped onto a cylinder").** Note 276's cab-forward engine, redrawn as one shaped machine. Only the art changes: the sim's engine is note 276's (and #222's inside it), so the walls, the roof walk, the windows the driver sees down the line through, the doorways and the running boards, the bots' ways and every test are as they were.
    - **The prow** (`TrainKit.Prow`, `ProwRows`).
      - One lofted shell of armour (`Kit.Loft`, new), raked back from a plough at the rail up to the cab's window sills. It's curved across in plan, so its ends sweep back into the cab's sides.
      - The foot is rust-scabbed plough plate, ribbed with welded rail iron, with three ram spikes at the buffer's height.
      - Above it, riveted plate round **the headlamp's eye**: a round, hooded, caged lamp barrel out of the prow, where World puts the light.
      - A rolled rail caps it at the sills, carried on down both sides as the cab's waist.
    - **The cab** (`CabShell`).
      - Its sides under the windows belly out like a hull's. Their foot rises towards the nose into the prow's sweep.
      - Two strakes run along them, round the prow at the same heights and on along the boiler, the lines the director asked for.
      - Over the waist, armour plate leaves slits for side windows rather than an open frame of posts. Welded patches sit over old damage, and a shutter is propped out over the slits.
      - The windscreen's posts rake forward from the sill into the brow, as a ship's bridge leans out over its bow.
      - The driver's front windows are the same openings as before.
    - **The roof** (`Roof`).
      - A helmet: arched across, its front narrowing and drooping into a brow out over the windscreen, with spikes welded along its edge.
      - Its eaves come down over the sides, more towards the back (`EaveAt`), so the roof's line falls back along the cab.
      - Two shoulders carry it on down onto the boiler's flanks, head-high over the way beside the boiler.
      - Over the top it keeps the arch the coaling hatch sits on (Bunker's `RoofY`).
    - **The boiler.** A rounded casing (`Rounded`, a superellipse; it was an octagon) under the strakes and straps. The skirt over the wheels is bellied too, its foot swept up at both ends like a fender's.
    - **The way in** (the director, 7 Oct: "there actually has to be a way to get into the cab from the train"). It's the one note 276 made: off car 1's plate onto the footplate, forward along either running board beside the boiler, and in at the doorway at the back of the cab's side. The new shell keeps it all clear (the shoulders are head-high over it; the side armour stops at the doorway). Each doorway is framed in rolled iron, with a caged lamp on a bracket at the cab's back corner, lit back along the board.
    - **Views:** `prow` (low off the front quarter), `prowside` (square off the left), `wayin` (on the left running board, a crewmate's eye, looking forward to the door).
    - **Found on the way:** a tapered `Kit.Cylinder` (`radiusB`) with its caps drew a black square seen from the side (its cap's face). The pillars are plain cylinders now.
    - **The engine is out of its own headlamp's shadow.** The headlamp's shadow map starts 0.3 m out from the lens (`GreyboxRenderer.LampViewProjection`), and a piece whose bounds reach past that is drawn into it whole.
      - Main's plough already reached 0.4 m out, so the engine's 18k triangles were drawn into its own lamp's shadow (the frame's budget, `PerfBudgetTests` at 72 fps fireman, had 448 triangles to spare).
      - The new prow first reached 0.62 m out, and the frame went over the budget.
      - Now nothing of the prow stands more than `ProwReach` (0.28 m) ahead of the engine's front: the plough's foot rakes back from there, and the ram spikes are short and raked down.
      - The engine drops out of that pass: fireman 1,493,564 of 1,500,000 (main had 1,499,552).
    - **Verified:** `dt screenshot` prow, prowside, wayin, engine, trackside, gangway; `DarkTerritory.Game.Tests` 463 of 464 passed, none failed, one skipped (the runner itself reported a session error after the last test); `art show engine` 18,762 triangles of its 45,000.

312. **The Cinder Hound, remodelled and re-rigged to the director's concept sheet (queue #51, E1; the director, 7 Oct 2026: "I want to get a remodel done and a re-rigging done of this particular style of model … make sure that it still aligns with the look of the game, but try to base what you have for the Cinder Hound off of this look moving forward").** The sheet (front, side and top views) shows a hound burnt to its frame and grown over by what burnt it; `tools/blender/cinder_hound.py` is rebuilt to it and its docstring describes it.
    - **The frame (SK_Quad, re-rigged).**
      - The same 40 bones by the same names and hierarchy, so the game's code and every clip's IK drive it unchanged.
      - The proportions are the sheet's: stilt-legged, the withers 0.72 m (0.55 m before), the hocks high, the chest a deep narrow keel and the waist tucked up hard.
      - The skull is long and narrow and carried low, nose to rump 1.6 m; with the tail, 1.88 m all told (CreatureArtTests: 1.25 to 1.9).
      - The forelegs stand out past the keel (`FORE`, 0.115 m from the middle), so their elbows clear it.
    - **The hide.** Charred plates (`char`: the library's pine bark, burnt dark brown; the baked high copy crazes it into scales split by cracks, lifted at their edges). It's overrun by thorn ridges that branch over the flanks like roots (`thorn`: the library's slag), each with a thorn.
      - Between them the cracks glow, a branching network (`ember_core`, forked) over the ember faces of the flanks and haunches.
      - Black crystal shards rake back up the spine (`mineral_growth`), tallest over the withers, with flame streaming off the tallest five. Shards also stand on the skull and the haunches.
      - Singed fur in tufts: a ruff at the neck and shoulders, a beard under the chest, and the haunches and elbows (`fur`: the library's fleece, burnt brown).
    - **The head, legs and tail.**
      - The skull is its own flat-shaded piece (`skull`), its planes catching the light like a carved thing: a blade of a nasal ridge, the brow over sunk ember eyes, tall burnt-card ears, teeth long at the front.
      - The lower legs are cased in scutes, with a spur back off each elbow and hock.
      - The paws are big and splayed: four toes each, with long black hooked claws (`claw`).
      - The tail is a burnt thorn branch, its twigs and thorns off it and its tip split three ways.
    - **The clips** are the IK gaits and poses of note 291, re-fitted:
      - the strides are longer and the paws lift higher for the longer legs (`GAITS`);
      - the prowl, crouch and bite sink lower or higher to suit the body;
      - the bite's body sits higher so the forelegs stay clear of the keel.
    - **The bake** (`tools/models/recipes/cinder_hound.py`): dresses for the new materials; the high copy's charred plates replace the matted hair; the body, the skull, the thorn and the fur are baked; the cracks, the flame and the eyes keep their own layers.
    - **Verified:**
      - 7,852 triangles of 8,000, 40 bones, every clip present.
      - `dt art clearance --only cinder_hound` clean (the bite and the hit first put an upper arm into the keel by up to 7 cm).
      - `dt art clip` side, front quarter and front.
      - `dt art reel --only cinder_hound` (run, prowl, crouch, lunge, board, hit, bite).

333. **The gun's laying, recorded low and slow (AU1, queue #72; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "there's a weird sound that is happening when the cannon turns ... make it something that's a lot more low and slow").** D1's #252 (note 329) made `gun-lay`'s synth low and slow. The recorded candidates #205 swapped in were the same high repeated sound: ten exhaust chuffs and fifteen gear teeth a second, centred at 1.8 kHz with 40% of their energy over 1 kHz. #205 dropped them.
    - **Two new candidates** (`recipes/gunlay_low.py`, AU1.7), both from the packs' real recordings and each one seamless cycle:
        - `slow`: the worm wheel's clunk on each stroke of a double-acting motor at 1.2 turns a second (2.4 clunks a second, heavy and lighter), over the motor's hum and a soft breath of steam.
        - `deep`: the worm grinding round under load, a tooth giving with a deep thud twice a second, over a labouring motor.

      Both are centred at 135–150 Hz, with under 0.05% of their energy over 1 kHz. At the game's 0.8–1.2 rate they clunk 1.6–2.9 times a second.
    - **Held until kept:** install.py's `HELD` keeps a cue out of the game (no first-candidate install) until the director keeps one of its candidates. Meanwhile `gun-lay` falls back to its synth backup (`tools/audio/synth-defs/gun-lay.json`, D1's). A kept candidate is swapped in through `SWAPS` as before; then `swaplevel.py` matches it to the synth's loudness.
    - **Verified:** the install leaves `gun-lay.json` equal to D1's synth while nothing's kept; `CrewAudioTests.LayingTheSeatedGunRunsItsSteamMotorWhileItTurnsAndClunksAsItStops`.

337. **The Cinder Hounds' own light (queue #70, E1; first claimed as #62 and 323, then 331 and 335: F1's MODS screen, D1's hot box and B2's walled towns landed with them first; note 209's "not yet": "read at range in the rear lamp, and as a pack: more glow, and a light of their own").** At night a hound was its ember slashes and nothing else: climbing the rear car's end in shadow, or running behind the train past the rear lamp, a pack of three read as a few yellow specks.
    - **Now each hound carries its own light** (`CreatureArt`, `HoundEmber`, `HoundLightRange`): its cracks' heat, a point light a little under its keel (the `belly` bone), flickering, and scaled by the glow its phase already gives its cracks (brighter on the run in, on the bite).
      - It lights its legs, its underside and a pool of the ground it runs over orange, out to 4.2 m. Behind the train a pack reads first as pools moving over the ballast, one to a hound, then as the shapes in them.
      - It lights the car end it's climbing too, so a boarding hound is a black shape against its own glow.
      - Not its own hide: the light is inside the hide's normals, so the char stays black and the cracks are still what glows on it.
      - A pack is 3 to 5 (`enemies.json`), well inside the renderer's 32 lights (nearest first past that).
    - **Found by it: the staged pack ran in the air.** `Staging.Threats` put the three ground hounds at 0.6 m over the rail; the sim runs them at -0.3 (`Rear.cs`). Off the ballast's shoulder that was a metre over the ground, and their light's pools showed it: the pools sat on the ground 2 to 3 m nearer the camera than the hounds. The staging is at -0.3 now; the game was never wrong.
    - **Staging:** `dt screenshot --threats --view hounds` (new): from the rear car's roof at its end, a gunner's eye, back down the line at the pack. `--board s --view board` for the climb.

325. **More set dressing, the first slice: what the railway left beside its line (queue #64, E1; the director's notes of 7 Oct, GDD App. F.3: "Right now I'm seeing the same like three things over and over again, as set dressing, and it's getting kind of boring").** Between the stops, a generated line's lineside was its trees, tufts, rocks and poles, with a shrine now and then; nothing a railway leaves.
    - **Now, the railway's leavings** (`WorldArt.Leavings`, on generated and hand-laid lines alike): one thing to a stretch of 85 m (`LeavingsEvery`), about four in five stretches (`LeavingsChance`), 3 to 14 m out from the rails. Fifteen kinds, the most a scatter has:
      - new in `JunkKit`, each its own piece: a stack of old ties, rails racked on bearers (one bent), oil drums (one on its side, a tar stain), a cable reel, a milepost, a platelayers' hut (brick or board, its roof half off) with ties stacked by it, a wheelset off a wreck, a heap of spilt coal, a camp gone cold, a platelayers' trolley tipped on its side, a grave or two (a tie cross, a cap on one);
      - and props already made but never scattered: stores crates dumped in a heap, fallen freight (timber, sacks, carboys), a sandbagged post with drums behind, a dead signal (on a generated line for the first time).
    - **No kind comes round again soon.** The kinds are dealt from a deck shuffled per 15 stretches (about 1.3 km): within a deck no kind twice, and across a join a deck's first four cards are none of the last four before it (swapped only with its middle, so the deck before's tail is known without dealing every deck back to the start). No kind within four stretches (340 m) of itself, and nearly every kind in 5 km (`LinesideArtTests.TheLeavingsBesideTheLineAreDealtSoNoKindComesRoundAgainSoon`).
    - **Cheap.** 26 to 308 triangles a piece; every one is in `ArtCatalog` (`junk-*`, small props, the hut a medium one), so `dt art check` budgets them and `dt art show junk-hut-0` shows them. The stops, branches, tunnels and bridges clear them as they clear the trees.
    - **Not a mail crane:** a mail crane beside the line is the sim's (note 149), so one dressed in would read as a stop that isn't.
    - **The second slice, a stop's yard** (`WorldArt.YardPiles`, drawn by `YardLeavings` with each building): the yards had buildings and nothing small round them. Now the leavings that belong by a building (ties, rails, drums, a cable reel, a wheelset, spilt coal, stores, fallen freight, sandbags) lie about every works building (a shed, the hero, a goods shed, the powerhouse, a barn, an outbuilding, a station, a signal box, a lamp room, a water tower):
      - Spots at both corners of each gable end and every 7 m along both long walls (`YardSpacing`), 1.3 m out (`YardStandOff`); seven in ten have a pile (`YardChance`).
      - **Never on a track.** A spot within 3.2 m (`YardTrackClear`) of the main line or any of the yard's branches is left out, so the doors' side, where the served track runs, is mostly bare, and so is a shed's back wall when the next track runs by it (P5). A shed with a crane's runway through it has none (the castings lie there).
      - The kinds are dealt from one shuffled deck a stop, so the buildings of one yard don't wear the same pile.
      - The houses are the villages' (B4's and B2's), the wells and the Holdouts their own.
      - **Verified:** `StopArtTests.AYardsPilesLieAboutItsBuildingsAndOffItsTracks` (both nights: every pile 3.1 m or more from any track, the main line's 600 m about it and every branch whole, and close by its building; at least six piles a night); `PerfBudgetTests` green; shots from frontier:7's third stop (the gable of a goods shed by the main line, the powerhouse).
    - **Not yet (the next slices):** more kinds for the villages; the hand-laid line's pines and the generated line's biomes still repeat their own few trees.

336. **The orchestrator's live crew: the budget from the crew alive, and the engaged cap by it (D1.2 for D1, queue #75; [orchestrator.md](design/orchestrator.md) §3.2 1, 3, 5; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "orchestrates threats based on the number of active players in the game currently").** The first piece of the orchestrator itself (note 328 has the outline and the hound run). enemies.json `director.orchestrator`.
    - **The live crew** (`Director.Census`, once a second with the director's think; `Director.Active`): the crew alive in the night now. Until anyone's been seen it's the crew the night was planned for.
    - **The budget** (`liveCrew`): App. B.1's crew multiplier, `0.7 + 0.12 × crew` to 1.6, now takes `Active`, so `Director.Budget` is live. A crew of four that loses two spends from then like a crew of two (×0.94 of ×1.18), on top of the relief valve's alive share squared. Off: the crew the night started with, as App. B.1 had it.
    - **The engaged cap** (`on`; `Director.EngagedCap`): the least of App. B.1's flat cap (4, or 6 at crew 6+), `ceil(active × engagedPerActive)` (0.75) and `perPlayer × active` (1), and at least 1. That's 1 at crew 1, 2 at crew 2, 3 at crews 3–4, 4 at 5, 6 at 8. The director holds "at the cap" on it, and the hound run (note 328) waits while the crew's at it, its count banked, so a crew of one never meets the run and the director's threat at once. The left-behind's hunts (note 273) and the Stoker (App. B.5, uncapped by design) stay outside it.
    - **"One a player" is a count, for now.** The director doesn't know which crewmate a threat is on, so the per-player cap holds only as the total (`perPlayer × active`). A true per-target rule needs §3.1's census of posts, orchestrator.md §6.2 item 4.
    - **The harness** (frontier:7, 900 s, same seed, on against off). Solo: 8 spawns on, 4 off; spent 22 against 11; nobody died either way. In both, a hound pack that boarded and stayed (note 269), which the lone bot never fights, and the fires it set, filled the caps for much of the night. That isn't this change's (it fills App. B.1's flat 4 the same). Crew 4: 11 spawns against 12, spent 29 against 30, nobody died. No fairness violations in any of the four. One seed each: a sign it doesn't starve or flood, not a sweep.
    - **GDD:** App. B.1's crew multiplier and hard-caps table say so.
    - **Verified:** `LiveCrewTests`: two of four die and the budget is a crew of two's from the next second (and isn't with `liveCrew` off); the cap at crews 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8, and App. B.1's flat cap with it off; a 900 s solo night where every director spawn came with nothing else engaged; at the cap the hound run's count banks with a hound and its fire aboard, and the run comes within 2 s of them being dealt with. `HoundRunTests` now run with a director that spends nothing (`HoundRunTests.Quiet`), so they test the run alone. Sim 1103/1103, NetcodeTests included.

343. **A lone crew answers a boarded hound pack (D1.2 for D1, queue #80; found in note 336).** Cinder Hounds that board stay (note 269), and a crew of one bot never fought them: the lone driver never leaves the cab for them. A pack and the fires it set held the caps for much of a solo night. The crew's walkers and gunner already go at a pack aboard (`Heed.Hounds`; the gunner leaves its gun for it).
    - **The lone driver cuts the car loose** (`ConductorBot.CutAlone`, `StopHand.CutLoose`): v1.1 App. A.3's other counter, "they go only dead, or with their car cut loose". A pack fight alone is three to five hounds biting at once, which a lone player loses.
        - When: a pack aboard a car that isn't the first behind the engine (that gap is every car), and nobody else alive aboard (`ConductorBot.Crewmates`).
        - The driver brings the train to a stand and readies it to be left, as for a Holdout (note 259's `ReadyToLeave`: the firebox filled, its door shut, the gauge vented).
        - Then: down out of the cab; on foot round the train to the nearest side ladder that reaches a roof (`StopHand.ToARoofLadder` uses `WalkTo`, out past the side-door steps; a walk straight along the car's side goes up them); along the roofs to the gap ahead of the front hound's car, and Uncouple on its plate (the stops' cut, `CutAt`).
        - Then back up into the cab (`SetBackAlone`), and on without the car. The hounds go with it (App. A.3).
    - **Not a walker's judgement:** the first version borrowed a `RoofWalkerBot` for the climb. Hurt, a walker keeps clear of a pack aboard, so at 1 hp the driver went up car 1's landing steps and back down for the rest of the night. It now takes only the climb (`RoofWalkerBot.Board`, `roofOnly`).
    - **The solo harness night** (frontier:7, `--bots 1`, 900 s, same seed, main against this): seconds the caps were held by boarded hounds, 1112 → 296; by their fires, 399 → 74. The director spent 30 against 22. Over 1200 s: two packs boarded (601 s on car 10, 840 s on car 9), and each car was cut loose, at 692 s and 925 s, about 90 s from the boarding. The driver was back in the cab at 733 s and 962 s, and the night ran on to 11.6 km. Nobody died, and no commit came without its telegraph. What the driver lost on the way (100 → 13 hp) came from the Whistler, out of car 2's gap at each stand (App. B.1: "stopping is when it grabs"), and a Dragger: walking the train alone costs a lone player.
    - **Not yet:** along the roofs the driver drops into each gap and climbs the next car's ladder (the stops' cut does too), about 4.5 s a car. A pack on the first car behind the engine stays.
    - **Verified:** `BoardedPackTests`: a lone driver at 12 m/s with three hounds on its rear car stands, cuts the car loose, keeps the other three, and is back in the cab and away; with a crewmate aboard the driver leaves the pack to them and doesn't stop. Sim 1141/1141.

339. **The Moose: a hyper-aggressive, territorial moose, too big to get on the train (queue #77, G1; the director's decisions of 7 Oct 2026; design `docs/design/creatures/moose.md`).**
    - **What it is.** GDD §21's eighteenth enemy (Outside, Split, cost 3; App. A.6, B.6; spec B.12). `Moose` (src/DarkTerritory.Sim/Enemies/Moose.cs) is loose in the world: `Extra` its target, `Extra2` its aggro (0–100), `Lateral` its heading, `Height` its `MooseMode` (graze, home, hunt, search, ram, square up, charge, wheel, snag, pin) for the clips, so a client draws it from replicated state alone. Its home, who put what into its meter and its search are the host's.
    - **Its temper.** Grazing, its meter fills from anyone on the ground it can see within 20 m (much faster within 12 m), anyone talking within 15 m (by the Voice byte, over a whisper's floor), a train going by within 25 m (once a pass); a hit fills it. Listening at 20 and warning at 50 are its tells; given room and quiet it falls 15 a second. Full, it's after whoever put the most in (lowest id on a tie, never dictionary order: `SortedDictionary`), and whoever hits it after that. Crowding counts only what it can see (`Moose.Clear`: no stop wall or car on the line between), so hiding behind the train or round a building works; voices it hears through them.
    - **The bullfight.** In sight within 30 m it squares up 2.5 s (the telegraph; the spine refuses a commit any sooner) and charges a straight line at 11 m/s, its heading locked; anyone on the ground it runs through takes a 60 hit (`ctx.Bite`: can't kill), and someone at 40 or less is pinned for 12 s (the shared GRAB). A friend's blow (`Struck`) breaks the pin and makes them its target; nothing hurts it (`Struck` passes 0 damage), so it can't be killed, by the director's decision, an exception to queue #25. Its body is a disc the rack's 3.2 m across: it can't come within half that of a stop's wall (`StopWalls`) or a car's box, so the alleys between buildings, doorways and the coupling gaps are out of its reach by geometry, not a rule. Charging into a wall snags it 4 s; into a car, or the track's clearance, it pulls up; three such charges without reaching its target and it gives up. Trees aren't solid in the sim yet (queue #14), so for now only buildings and cars are cover.
    - **Out of sight, aboard, away.** Out of sight it searches where it last saw or heard them for 25 s, and anyone talking within 15 m is found (and is its target). Lost within 5 m of a car they're aboard, it rams that car every 3 s for 15 s: only a ram (`Rams` on the host; every client reads `RamCount`, carried in the replicated `Health` as 1 + the rams, since nothing hurts it: the audio lands a boom on each, AU1 on #247; nothing in or on the car is touched). It gives up past 80 m from its ground and when the train moves off; it's gone 600 m behind.
    - **Never on the rail.** No part of its path comes within 3.2 m of any track's centre (`RailLine.Nearest`, the main line or a branch), 6 m while the train moves and wherever it's put down, so the line is a boundary it never crosses: the train can never hit it, and it can never stop or derail the train. The first draft let it cross a track at a run during a chase; this is the simplest rule that can't put it in the train's way.
    - **Where it comes from.** The director's spawn rule (`Spawns`, B.6): stopped at a facility or a dead settlement, one about at a time, every tier weighted 1/1.5/2/2.5 and by the line's biome (`moose.biomeWeights`, the plan's main-line biome), 30–60 m out from the consist's middle wherever `Moose.Place` finds ground it can stand on (dry, clear, outside the forts). A grazing moose isn't engaged (`Director.Engaged`), so it holds no cap and isn't dismissed for want of company. Beside the line on the run, `World.LinesideMoose` puts one down 300 m ahead, 8–22 m out, 2–5 per 10 km by tier times the biome's weight, on its own dice from the route's seed (so the director's draws, and every seeded test, are untouched) and costing the director nothing. Conflict pairs: the Gaunt, Ribbits, Whistler and facility loading. Its primary sense is movement (App. A.1 allows one), keeping it out of the Ribbits' (sight) and the Gaunt's (sound) one-tell-type cap so the pairs can happen. `minCrew` is 1: at a crew of one the solo rule (`grab.soloStruggle`) frees a pinned player, as from every grab.
    - **Its art** (`tools/blender/moose.py`, 39 bones; rebuilt on 8 Oct the Gannet's way, at the director's word that the first pass was "super low quality, very boxy and rigid, not organic"). The trunk, hump, neck, head and lower jaw (the mouth the gap left between the drooping lip and the jaw), legs, bell, tail and the ridge's crest are one skin through `rig.fuse` (voxel union, six relax passes so the joins fillet, QuadriFlow, smooth-shaded); the rack is a second fused skin (beams, burrs, cupped and twisted palms turned forward like open hands, rim tines, slag lumps), collapsed rather than QuadriFlowed (`quads=False`) and shaded hard only at its plates' edges; the tick sacs are rebound to the skin's weights so they ride it. A second pass the same day (the coordinator: it read as a deer or a llama) made it a heavy, front-loaded bull: the barrel about twice the girth, massive shoulders under a hump that is the back's high point, the back sloping to smaller hips and a tucked flank, a short very thick neck, a bigger head and muzzle, a heavy dewlap, thick legs with big knees and hocks, flattened engorged ticks in place of popcorn clusters, and palms that spread out to the sides in a broad flat span. 14,219 triangles (LOD 5,955), 3.23 m across the rack, 3.37 m to its top. Its colour is baked into one 2048 texture by `tools/models/recipes/moose.py` (a mottled, bald-patched ghost-moose hide crusted with painted ticks, darker legs and muzzle, slag rack with bloody velvet), so `tools/blender/build.sh` leaves it out; built with Blender as a Python module, bpy 4.5 (bpy 5 drops `Action.fcurves`, which `rig.bake` uses). The rack is its own bone a side (so `dt art clearance` measures it apart); a ridge of sacs on three spine bones swells when it warns; the charge is a rotary gallop with the head held at a fixed world rotation, so the rack stays level on the line. `CreatureArt` picks its clip from the replicated `MooseMode`, aggro and pace (graze, listen, warn, walk, trot, squareUp, charge, overrun, snag, search, ram, pin, strut; trainPass when a moving train is within `trainPassAt`, decided on the presentation side since the sim has no mode for it); the one it pins lies under its rack in `HeldPinned`. Views: `dt screenshot --view moose|moosecharge|moosepin` and `--moose <mode>`; stills in docs/design/creatures/. `CreatureArtTests` and `CreatureBodyTests` pin its budget, clips, size, clearance and gun body.
    - **Not yet.** Its sounds are the audio chat's (requested on the Audio Checklist; spec A.4's row is "pending"). The bots don't give it room or hush near it: they walk past it to the loading and rescue a pinned crewmate with a blow (`Heed.Rescue`), which the grab audit uses. Queue #48 may move its ground to a laid-out site.
    - **Verified:** `MooseTests` (14: left be it never charges; crowded it listens, squares up 2.5 s and charges a 60 hit; backed off at its warning it settles; a talker is its target; it pins the hurt and a friend's blow takes it off them; pinned with nobody coming, trampled; nothing kills it; out of sight and quiet it gives up; lost at a car it rams it and touches nothing; the train leaving ends it; it never comes within the track's clearance chasing someone along the line; a passing train makes it listen, never warn; every tier, more the harder; its charge is a hit, not chip). `SpecTableTests.TheMooseMatchesB12`. `dt audit grabs --only moose`: freed at every crew from 2 to 8 (1.2 of 12 s). A harness night (`dt harness --route frontier:7 --bots 4 --enemies --insist moose,ribbit --start 5090 --seconds 200 --trace`): placed at the stop, the look-out walks up (`LookErrand`, balance.json `look.mooseM`), it listens, squares up and charges twice, and the bot, gone back to its post, is missed both times. The combination sweep (`dt balance --pairs --only moose,... --at-stops`) still reads it "dormant" against the Ribbits and the Whistler: its one look-out goes to the Ribbits first and is busy for the night, so the sweep under-exercises it. The Sim suite.

340. **The Gannet: one enormous corrupted seabird that rides a fast train (queue #78, G1; the director's decisions of 7 Oct 2026; design `docs/design/creatures/gannet.md`; the orchestrator's S3, App. F.1's "fast, flying class").**
    - **What it is.** GDD §21's nineteenth enemy (Flank, Kill, cost 4; App. A.4, B.4; spec B.13). `Gannet` (src/DarkTerritory.Sim/Enemies/Gannet.cs) rides in a car's frame (`Attached`, `Local`): flying over the train is flying in the train's moving air, so the frame carries it with no frame change inside a tick (the moving-frames rule). It changes frame only between ticks (`Rehome`), to the car its prey or its mark is on. Pinning someone on the ground it's loose in the world. `Extra` is its prey on a dive, `Extra2` its mark, `Lateral` its heading in its frame, `Height` its `GannetMode` (Away, Soar, Hang, Fold, Stuck, Climb, Bank, Pin), so a client draws it from replicated state; its pecks come from the spine's own clock (`PecksLanded`).
    - **The dive.** Prey is a walker on a roof, over `preyAbove` on it and not seated. The roof's walk moves a player without a velocity, so it measures each crewmate's pace from their position tick to tick (`Pace`, by id in a `SortedDictionary`). It hangs over them 2 s (the calls stop), then folds: its line locks on where they'll be at the strike (position + pace × 1.6 s), and it strikes there. Breaking stride misses by geometry (a stop leaves them a walk's 1.6 s short; a step aside, off its 0.9 m), not by a rule. A strike within reach is a 35 stab (`ctx.Bite`, can't kill); nobody there on the roof and its beak's stuck 4 s, the only time a blow lands outside a pin.
    - **The mark and the pin.** A blow or a ball (`Struck`) hurts it and makes the hitter its mark. Its next pass is for them: a 2.5 s bank (the telegraph; the spine refuses a commit sooner), then, if they're still out (not in a car's room or the cab), down on them: the shared GRAB for 4 pecks × 3 s. Three blows from friends in the pin (`DriveOffBlows`) break it, and the last of them is its mark. The fourth peck is `DeathCause.Pecked`. 12 health; under 4 it leaves for the run (gone); killed, its head drops (`Bodies.SpawnCrate` in its car's frame, or `SpawnLoot` on the ground) as a find owned `Run.TrophyOwner(EnemyKind.Gannet)`. `RunLoot.FindOf` reads a trophy's owner (stop 0xFFF, container the kind) from loot.json `trophies.gannet`: 1.5 of the tier's car-loads, stowed in any car, the same on every machine.
    - **Coming and going.** `World.FastSeconds` counts the train's run at 18 m/s or more. The spawn rule (B.4) wants 30 s of it out of a tunnel, a train of two or more, once a run, every tier weighted 1/1.5/2/2.5, by the plan's biome and per walker on the roofs. Under 12 m/s for 6 s, in a tunnel, or 60 s with nobody walking the roofs and its mark inside, it goes Away (not exposed, not engaged: `Director.Engaged` leaves it out of the caps) and comes back after 180 s once the train's run fast again. It's never dismissed for want of company (`StaysAboard`). Its passes' waits come from its own id and the tick, never the director's dice.
    - **Its art** (from the director's reference, `docs/design/creatures/gannet-reference.webp`; rebuilt at the director's word that the first pass was "super low quality ... very boxy and rigid, not organic"). `tools/blender/gannet.py`: the body, the S of the neck, the head, the sacs and the legs one skin through `rig.fuse` (the union voxel-remeshed, then QuadriFlow, smooth-shaded); the wings bone-curved, their feathers layered, cupped and twisted cards, each riding two bones so the wing bends and the primaries splay; 15,712 triangles (its LOD 6,578), a 7.04 m span, 2.28 m tall. Its colour is baked into one 2048 texture by `tools/models/recipes/gannet.py` (sooted, flecked white, black primaries, a sulphur head, veined sacs glowing from inside), so `tools/blender/build.sh` leaves it out. `CreatureArt` picks its clip from the replicated `GannetMode` and lands each peck on the Sim's 3 s beat; the one it pins lies on their back under its foot (`HeldPinned`). Views `gannet`, `gannetfold`, `gannetstuck`, `gannetpin` and `--gannet <mode>`; stills in docs/design/creatures/. `CreatureArtTests` and `CreatureBodyTests` pin its budget, size, clips, clearance and gun body.
    - **Not yet.** Its sounds are made (note 384, spec A.4's row). The bots don't stop on a fold, or keep from hitting it (both since: note 454, and D1.3's #183); they do beat it off a pinned crewmate (`Heed.Rescue`), which the grab audit uses.
    - **Verified:** `GannetTests` (10: holding the line is a stab; breaking stride a miss and stuck; whoever's still is never prey; hit it and it banks and pins and pecks to the fourth; friends' three blows drive it off and the last is its mark; inside a car it can't come down; a slow train and it peels off, unengaged; killed, its head is a trophy in its car; under a third it leaves for the run; its numbers keep the fairness contract). `SpecTableTests.TheGannetMatchesB13`. `dt audit grabs --only gannet`: freed at every crew from 2 to 8 (2.4 s at crew 2, 1.0 s from 4). The Sim suite.

344. **Hold prompts in one form (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #81; GDD §32 "the action and its key ... and a hold's progress"; note 285).** Two forms had grown up. The search, the generator and the rigging said the action and its key ("SEARCH THE CUPBOARD : HOLD [E]") and their progress only once under way; the repairs (note 301), the boiler, the fouled gun, the breach and the hot box (note 331) said "(0%)" before anyone had touched them.
    - **One form** (`Hud.Hold`): the action and its key, and the percentage only once there's progress. A mend kept half done with Use let go (note 301, "a few presses") still says how far it got, and a battered car still says how whole its shell is.
    - **Verified:** `HudTests.AFouledGunAndABreachedCarSayHowToPutThemRight` (nothing done: no percentage; a quarter done: 25%; the battered car's 50% unchanged).
335. **Walled towns: up to 3000 people, the fortress round the town, streets to walk (queue #74, B2; the director, 7 Oct 2026: "lets make it so towns can go up to 3000 and that fortresses aren't just some straight line around the railroad, they should surround towns, towns should be explorable in a sense. this is our big worldbuilding work that makes it feel interesting and exciting to go around").** Before this, the departure fortress (T124, note 274) was a corridor along the yard: two walls 14.8 m out, towers every 120 m, note 107's houses between the line and the walls, the town's square stepping one wall back (note 281). A town of 350 filled the yard's street; nothing bigger fitted.
    - **How many** (tuning/towns.json): `population` 20–3000, drawn as min + (max − min)·u^`populationPower` (2, by multiplying: no `Math.Pow` in the Sim). About one town in three is 350 or fewer, half under ~770, one in ten over 2400. Households of 2–6 as before. The lost families' houses are at most `lostShare` (0.6) of the households; past that a big town's lost leave nothing standing. Out of doors at night, one in 22 but never more than `outdoorsMax` (16), and open houses one per 70 but never more than 6: every household at home also takes one of the custom's lines, and at 8 the street runs out of words (TownTests: nobody mute, nobody repeats). A town of thousands is shut in at night; its lit windows say so.
    - **Ten more households' stories** (world/towns.json `households`, twenty now), so a big town's six aren't the next big town's six: the dory that went out into the fog and the foghorn answered; the house where nobody goes out without the rope; the toys given to the gate; the miner who came up two hours late; the singing house gone quiet; the mother who counts her family every hour; the brakeman on a cut telephone line; the stones on the sill; the bride's place laid; the lighthouse still turning. Each tells its own loss and, sideways, how another town lives with something (don't whistle, don't go alone, don't leave a toy lying, never sing back, count them before they count you), never the whole rule. They reuse the ten object kinds the house already draws and places.
    - **The ground plan** (`TownGenerator.Houses`, the `houses.lots` stream; towns.json `walled`). The line's own street first (note 107's lots, every 15 m, 10.9 m out). A town that needs more lots than that is walled:
        - **lanes** across every 90–130 m (8 m wide), the ways from the line to the streets: never through the square (one that would be moves to just past it), and the line's own row leaves them clear;
        - **streets** beside the line, a pair at a time (one each side), their middles 34.5 m out and every 30 m past that, 6 m wide, up to 5 a side, as many as the households need;
        - **a row of houses either side of each street**, fronts 3.5 m back from it on lots of 13–17 m frontage (a house no wider than its lot less 2 m, its wing in what's left): the line-side row faces out, the far row back toward the line, so both front the street;
        - the lots sorted by distance from the square's heart: the lived-in houses round it, the open ones nearest, the lost at the town's edges.
    - **The wall** (`TownPlan.Bounds`, `TownBounds`): from `rear` (−8 m, behind the yard's start, the line's way out the back shut) to the gate, out past the last row's backs by `margin` (7 m) on both sides. `Run.Fortresses.Round` stands it in the train's walls: the sides a 10 m bay at a time, a tower at each corner and every 120 m, the front wall from the gatehouse to each corner, the rear across the line. A walled town's fort builds none of the corridor's walls, towers or houses, and its square has no walls of its own: it opens between its buildings onto the first street. A town whose houses fit the line's street keeps the corridor and its stepped-back square, unchanged: under about 165 people, one town in four (`dt town sweep`, 200 towns: 153 walled, the smallest 164 people, the biggest unwalled 169, five streets a side at most, up to 1181 houses).
    - **The safe zone** (`World.InFort`, note 273): inside the yard, a walled town's fort reaches its wall (its widest side plus 5 m), past the 80 m every other fort keeps, so nothing comes in over the streets and nobody out at the far one is left behind.
    - **The ground** (linegen tiers.json fortress `padM`, 70 → 200, `FortressTemplate.PadM`): level either side of the yard across the widest town (five streets reach ~177 m) and its wall, blended over 30 m past that. Lakes and shore keep their distance from pads, so on some lines the water near the gate moves back. **Overlaps:** B1's and B4's level design (the pad, the lakes and shore by the gate; B4's #239 trestle); every line's terrain within 230 m of the yard is level now, and no test pinned the old.
    - **The art:**
        - `WorldArt.TownWall`: the wall's pieces down each side, across the front from the gatehouse and across the rear, the towers with their lamps.
        - `Streets`: each street's beaten surface in 20 m pieces, lamp posts every 45 m lit within 120 m of you, the lanes in mud.
        - `Houses` by distance, so a town of hundreds of houses draws: a street's block (60 m of a row) is one mesh of its houses' far forms (`MaritimeKit.Street`) beyond 120 m, each house its far piece out to 75 m, its full design within. Those meshes are kept only while drawn (`HousePiece`: at most 600, the least recently drawn let go, a town's all let go when the town changes), not for the Look's life as kit pieces are. The square's walls aren't drawn in a walled town (as the Sim).
        - `Staging`: `dt screenshot --route r --town over|lane|outside` (over the gate looking back over the roofs; down the first street; outside the gate as the train leaves).
    - **Headless:** `dt town` reports a walled town's reach either side, its streets and lanes, and its houses' character; `dt town sweep` how many towns are walled, the smallest walled and the biggest not.
    - **Measured** (local:5, 2958 people, the biggest town on the test routes; the container's software Vulkan): the street 803K triangles and 605 draws, the square 841K and 621, over the roofs 736K and 557, outside the gate 414K and 398 (budget 1.5M and 1500). The scene build is ~31 ms against ~26 ms for frontier:7's 97 people (CPU, this container).
    - **Verified:**
        - `WalledTownTests` (Sim):
            - `ABigTownHasStreetsInsideAWallRoundItAndASmallOneIsTheYard` (3000: four streets or more, lanes, every household housed; 40: no bounds);
            - `EveryHouseStandsInsideTheWallOffTheStreetsAndClearOfTheNext` (frontier:7 at 3000, local:3 at 1200, deadLines:3 at 600: every part of every house inside the wall, off the line, out of every street, lane and the square, and no two houses' parts overlapping);
            - `YouWalkFromTheLineDownALaneToTheOutermostStreetAndTheWallStopsYou` (running from beside the line down the middle lane, past the outermost street, stopped short of the wall);
            - `TheWholeTownIsTheFortAndItsWallIsSolid` (every street in the fort; the wall down both sides and across the back in the train's walls; no corridor wall left in the yard).
        - `TownTests` over towns to 3000: everybody inside a walled town's wall; houses within it and apart in their rows; the house-variety test round the square.
        - The views above looked at: the square opening onto the first street, the street's painted houses, the town from over the gate and from outside it.
    - **The yards** (a second pass; the director's references: Lunenburg's picket fences, the woodpiles, sheds, traps and dories behind Peggy's Cove's and Blue Rocks' houses). Each house has its `TownHouse.Yard` (`TownGenerator.Yard`, on its own `houses.yards` stream so the houses are as they were):
        - on a street, a picket fence along the street's edge, its gate in front of the door (the house's trim colour; grey, gapped and short where nobody lives);
        - a board fence on the back line the line-side row shares with the row behind (one row owns it, so there's one fence, not two);
        - along the back, what the yard keeps, as much as there's room for, clear of the house by a step: a woodpile, a shed, a privy, lobster traps, a dory turned over on its blocks, the washing pegged out, a rain barrel. A row's back line is halfway to the row behind, or short of the wall; the line's own street in a town that's still the yard has no room behind its houses.
        - Each character weights them (houses.json `yard`): a cove's yards are traps and dories with few pickets, Lunenburg's are fenced and full of washing, a farm's has its woodpile and shed, a company row has the same picket and privy at every house.
        - All solid where drawn but the washing (`TownHouse.Solids`, `Town`'s walls); nothing of a yard stands in the square, a street or a lane.
        - Drawn into the house's own mesh (`MaritimeKit.Yard`), so a yard costs no draws; its far form keeps the shed, privy, dory and woodpile as blocks.
        - `dt screenshot --route r --town yard|yardtop|fence`, `dt art houses --character c --yard [--back]`.
        - Verified: `WalledTownTests.AYardIsFencedAtTheStreetWithItsGateAtTheDoorAndKeepsItsThingsBehindTheHouse` (most houses have a yard; pickets, board fences and things all turn up; everything in its lot, behind the house by a step but the fences; the gate clear in front of the door), and the house-overlap test over the yards too. The biggest town's street with its fences: 853K triangles, 614 draws.
    - **A town that's lived in** (App. F.3, the director: "the fortresses feel static and lame"). Presentation only (nothing in the Sim; every machine draws it from the clock, alike enough):
        - **Smoke from the chimneys** of the houses lived in, within 160 m of you (`WorldArt.Chimneys`, `MaritimeKit.ChimneyTops` as the kit builds the chimneys; `Effects.Chimney`: a puff a second or so, pale, rising slowly and leaning with the air).
        - **The watch on the wall**: a guard with a lantern walking each stretch of wall between two towers (three stretches in four), up and back at a walk with a pause at each end (`WorldArt.Watch`), a walled town's side walls or the yard's two. The crew's `lantern_walk` clip with the lamp hung and lit. The wall kit's merlons now stand on the wall's outer half (`StructureKit.Wall`, T124's) so the walk behind them is open and the watch shows over the parapet from inside; the Sim's wall is the same box as before.
        - `dt screenshot --route r --town watch` (from below the wall, up at the nearest of the watch).
    - **Not yet:**
        - granite, gardens, fish sheds on stilts by the water;
        - folk walking the streets (talking to someone who walks needs them to stop for you alone, and talk isn't replicated);
        - cross streets other than the lanes, and streets that bend with the land;
        - more lines for the street (`anyone`, the jobs, the threads), so a big town can open more houses and put more people out;
        - the roofs and steeple over the wall from outside;
        - the terrain past the line's start (seen from over the town, never from the ground: the rear wall hides it);
        - the harness and bots don't go into the streets.

345. **The orchestrator's census of posts and slack (D1.2 for D1, queue #82; [orchestrator.md](design/orchestrator.md) §3.1, §3.2 items 2–4; GDD App. F.3).** Note 336 gave the director the live crew and its caps; this gives it who's where and who's idle. enemies.json `director.orchestrator`; `Enemies/Census.cs`; `Director.Count`, `Director.Posts`, `Director.Next`, `Director.WhoseNext`.
    - **The census** (once a second, host only, players and threats by id): each crewmate alive and their `Post`:
        - cab: in it, or on the engine; the driver and the fireman share it;
        - gunner: seated at a gun;
        - walker: the roofs, a ladder, a gap or a landing;
        - rider: a car's floor inside its walls;
        - ground: off the train within `abandoned.behindM`;
        - left behind: further off; their own hunt answers them (note 273).

      Which engaged threats are on whom: the one it holds; else the nearest within `onRadius` (20 m); else the nearest crewmate at a post that `answers` it (a pack running behind is the gunner's).

      Their slack: seconds since they last had something to answer. Something to answer is a threat on them; an upkeep job on their car (an open hot box, note 331; a guttering lamp, D1's note 346, merged meanwhile); a hot box or a coupling working loose (D1's note 356) anywhere for a walker (greased from the landing, made fast in the gap; a loose coupling also for anyone on either car of its gap), or a guttering lamp anywhere for a rider (trimmed inside); or, in the cab, the train moving (the line and the fire are the driver's).
    - **Slack counts only on the run between stops:** the train moving faster than `drivingAbove` (0.5 m/s), past the grace, out of the forts and facilities, short of the final approach. A generated stop keeps the run `Underway` while the train stands to be worked. Counted then, the first crew-4 nights showed the driver at 530 s of slack with nothing wrong.
    - **It steers** (`census`, with the crew it counted at `minCrew`, 2, or more; a crew of one is App. B.1's as it was):
        - who's next: the free crewmate with the most slack, `minSlack` (30 s) or more. A kind answered at their post weighs ×`slackWeight` (2); a kind answered only at posts nobody holds, ×`emptyPostWeight` (0.5), except the Track Doll, whose rule is the empty cab.
        - slack presses: + `slackPerSecond` (0.05) a second for each crewmate at `slackPress` (150 s) or more.
        - one threat on any one player (`perTarget`): a kind whose every answering crewmate already has one on them weighs nothing; if that leaves nothing, it holds ("one on each"). It works on the pick, not as a hold on the crew: with the cap at ceil(0.75 × active), the whole crew is never taken before the cap holds.
    - **Two fixes found on the way:**
        - Steering went by the planned crew, so a night with nobody aboard yet discounted everything but the Track Doll (`CargoTests`' livestock night). It now goes by the crew the census saw.
        - The "one on each" hold also caught lists already weighing nothing for other reasons, which App. B.1 sends from anyway (its last pick). That changed solo nights. It now holds only when the census zeroed them.
    - **The harness** (frontier:7, 900 s, same seed; `threats.slack` reports each crewmate's most slack and seconds at 150 or more):
        - Crew 4, census off: max slack 120, 118 and 155 s, 6 s past 150; 10 sent; quiet share 0.31.
        - Crew 4, census on: max 155, 118 and 107 s, 6 s past 150 (a different crewmate); 8 sent; quiet share 0.22; nobody died; no fairness violations.
        - Over 1800 s, census on (before the two fixes): max 155 s, 6 s past.
        - A crew of four on this line is near the target either way: the bots work the train. What the census changes is who gets what.
        - Solo: identical to main (the same director trace, spawns and distance).
        - One seed each.
    - **Verified:** `CensusTests`: each post read from where a crewmate is; slack counts on the run (about 40 s past the grace), holds with the train standing, and a hound beside a walker clears it; an open hot box on their car clears it, and a guttering lamp anywhere clears a rider's (not a walker's on another car); slack presses the pressure by `slackPerSecond` a second past `slackPress`, and not with census off; who's next favours the slack walker's kinds ×2, discounts the ground's ×0.5, and with a hound on the walker weighs walker-only kinds to nothing; a crew of one steers nothing. a loose coupling far down the train clears a walker's and not a rider's on another car. Sim 1215/1215 and the Game suite (632, in slices: whole it runs out of memory; 1 skipped, VR) on main as of #333, NetcodeTests included.

346. **A lamp guttering, the second upkeep job while the train runs (queue #83, D1; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "on the train, still relatively boring from point A to point B"; [orchestrator.md](design/orchestrator.md) §5.1 U3).**
    - **What it is.** Every `everyMetres` (3 km ± half) of the train's running, a lit car with a room has its lamp start to gutter: `Vehicle.Gutter`, the seconds it's been at it. None in the first 3 km, none in the yard or a fort, never more guttering than there are crewmates alive. All in `upkeep.json` `lamp`; host only (`Gutters`), the vehicle record carries it (protocol 36).
    - **The tell.** The lamp flickers: drawn out for moments a few times a second, at random, more of the time the nearer it is to going out (a twelfth of the time at first, over half at the end; `GreyboxScene.Sputtered`, the car's lights and its lamps alike); and the wick sputters by the ceiling lamps (`lamp-gutter`, a synth loop: uneven crackles over a low flutter, quicker as it goes). The prompt in the car says TRIM THE LAMP.
    - **The fix.** The lamp key, in the car: guttering, the press trims it (it burns steady, and stays lit; a trim isn't a light seen in the dark, note 287, so it draws nothing). Burning steady, the key is the switch it always was.
    - **Left alone.** After 45 s it goes out: the car is dark, and Climbers make for an unlit car (App. A.4) until someone lights it again. The outline's ×1.15 on the pressure is the train's own lamp's dark, not a car's, so a car lamp out adds none.
    - **Bots.** One indoors in that car presses the lamp key every half second while it's guttering (`Heed.Gutter`): the host's trim reaches the client a snapshot later, and a second press on a lamp burning steady would put it out. Since 8 Oct (a 41-minute bot night with upkeep: 7 of 8 guttering lamps went out, nobody in their cars) a walker goes to one: with no trouble in a car to answer, the nearest car guttering with nobody inside is where its legs take it (along the roofs and in at its door, `RoofWalkerBot.GutterCar`), and in there `Heed.Gutter` trims it.
