Before a mail bag (the lamp's on a clock; a bag is pay); a gunner only with nobody else to send. `GutterTests.AWalkerGoesInToAGutteringLampNobodysWithAndTrimsIt`.
    - **Verified.** `GutterTests` (4): one starts by the train's running; left alone it goes out; the key trims it, then switches it as ever; a bot in the car trims it, and leaves a steady lamp alone. `dt screenshot --view inside --gutter 44 --scene-time 0.45` (out for that moment) against `--gutter 0` (lit), looked at; `dt audio render --sound lamp-gutter --param gutter=1`, the spectrogram looked at.
347. **TEXT SIZE (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #84; GDD §32 "Accessibility"; the director, 8 Oct 2026: "these are all quite important").** The HUD's print was one size: fine print two screen pixels a font pixel at 1080p, the rest four. Nothing made it bigger.
    - **The canvas, smaller** (`Settings.TextSize`, `Settings.Canvas`): 100%, 125% or 150% draws the overlay on 480x270, 384x216 or 320x180, stretched over the same window (the renderer's `OverlaySize`). Everything on it grows together and keeps its layout; at 1080p each canvas pixel is 4, 5 or 6 of the screen's, and the fine print (`Hud.PromptScaleAt`) 2, 2.5 or 3. It takes at once in the window (`ApplyDisplay`), in a night's menu too; a headset's panel keeps its own 480x270.
    - **What didn't fit, made to:** the incident report's settlement line wraps (it ran off the plate at 125%); a menu's heading, the credits' licence line and the profile's tally line wrap; a row too wide is cut short with "..." (the detail under the list says it whole); the key hints drop "OR MOUSE" and "OR CLICK" when they're wider than the frame; the profile's badges become a row of print each when the canvas is too short for them.
    - **Verified:** `TextSizeTests`: each size is the canvas above, a stray size is 100%; the HUD, the supplies, the roster and the derailed report lie inside the frame at every size; every menu screen, scrolled to its foot, does too; TEXT SIZE steps 100, 125, 150 and back, saved. `dt screenshot --menu settings|fortress --text-size 1.5` and `dt screenshot --hud --cord --text-size 1.5`, looked at.

348. **COLOURS: a colourblind-safe palette (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #85; GDD §32 "Accessibility"; the director, 8 Oct 2026).** The HUD's colours that mean something were green (heard, a good ping, a rescue), amber (a heading, a ping going bad, a bend to slow for) and red (dead, a grab, an alarm). To a protanope green and amber are 15 apart in CIELAB, where under 20 reads as one colour: SPEAKING beside a heading, a good ping beside a bad one.
    - **Two palettes in hud.json** (`standard`, `colourblind`; `HudTuning.Standard`, `.Colourblind`, `HudPalette`), chosen by the settings' **COLOURS** (`Settings.Colours`); `Hud`'s Green, Amber and Red are the chosen palette's good, warning and danger. Colourblind is sky blue, yellow and a deeper red: every pair 43 or more apart under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia (Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes 2009, full severity), and no closer than the standard's with full colour vision.
    - **What isn't in it:** the menus' amber (a selection, not a meaning), the hotbar's lit slot, and what's drawn in the world (the cab map's red limits, the callouts' amber glow). Those are shapes and places as much as colours; they're the polish pass's (#88) to look at.
    - **Verified:** `HudPaletteTests`: the simulation holds the standard palette under 20 for a protanope and the colourblind one at 40 or more for all three; COLOURS chooses what the roster's SPEAKING is drawn in. `dt screenshot --hud --colours colourblind` (`--roster`, `--spectating`, `--bend-warning`), looked at.
349. **CAPTIONS: the sounds worth hearing, written as they're heard (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #86; GDD §32 "Accessibility"; the director, 8 Oct 2026).** A player who can't hear the tiptoes on the roof can't learn that they mean something's there. With **CAPTIONS** on (off by default; `Settings.Captions`), what's heard is written in fine print at the foot of the frame on the left, where nothing else is: `[TIPTOEING, ABOVE]`, `[A CHILD CALLING, LEFT]`, the newest lowest.
    - **What a sound is, never what makes it** (content/ui/captions.json): a sound's name (or the name it's a variant of, a '.' at a time: `cs-ribbits.hop-land.ground` is `cs-ribbits.hop-land`'s) and the words someone hearing it would use. Neither a creature's name nor what to do: a reader learns what tiptoeing means as a listener does. The silent-by-design creatures (the Gaunt, the Passenger, the Followers) have nothing to caption. Covered: every creature's tell and sign that has a sound, the hot box, the boiler's strain and safety valve, the whistle (the Whistler's is the train's own) and the toys.
    - **Heard as the ear heard it:** fed each frame from the mixer's voices (not finished, not virtualised) at `SoundInstance.AudibleGain`, the gain the mixer last rendered each at, after distance and walls; under `threshold` (0.03) it isn't heard. Two of a kind are one caption, from the louder; a caption stays up `holdSeconds` (2.5) after its sound was last heard; at most `lines` (3) up, the oldest going first. Where is from the listener's head: AHEAD, BEHIND, LEFT, RIGHT, ABOVE, BELOW.
    - **Verified:** `CaptionsTests`: every caption is a sound that plays; none names a creature; variants, directions, threshold, hold and line count; end to end through the real mixer, a tiptoe 4 m behind is `[TIPTOEING, BEHIND]` and a call 2 km off isn't heard; the HUD writes them at the foot of the frame on the left at every TEXT SIZE; the setting starts off and saves. `dt screenshot --hud --captions` (with `--text-size`), looked at.
350. **FIRST NIGHTS: a tip while the night's built, the controls in the yard (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #87; GDD §32 "Accessibility"; the director, 8 Oct 2026).** A new player had the corner's keys and nothing else. With **FIRST NIGHTS** on (the default; `Settings.FirstNights`), the loading screen has a tip under BUILDING THE NIGHT, a new one each night, and for a player's first `firstNights` (3) nights a card in the yard: YOUR FIRST NIGHTS, the core controls in the prompts' form with the player's own keys (MOVE, RUN, JUMP; USE, SWING, LADDER; TALK, RADIO; CREW, ROUTE CARD, SUPPLIES; MENU), down the left a third of the way, no plate (note 285). It's gone once the train's through the gate.
    - **"Learned, not told" kept** (content/ui/tips.json): the tips are the shape of a night and the crew's habits, as a friend who's played would say them ("Roll call is shouted. Count the crew before the train moves."). None names a creature or says what to do when; what an action does is still the night's to teach, and the cab's controls, the gun's and the rest are said where you are, as ever.
    - **Counted by the profile:** `PlayerProfile.Data.Nights`, a night counted once its run is over (`CountNight`); `Onboarding.FirstNight` is FIRST NIGHTS on and fewer nights over than the file's count.
    - **Verified:** `FirstNightsTests`: no tip names a creature or says "if you" or "when you"; each night's tip and none with the setting off; the card for the first nights only, in the player's own keys (TALK rebound to B says [B]); the profile counts and keeps nights; the HUD draws the card in the yard inside the frame at every TEXT SIZE; the setting starts on and saves. `dt screenshot --hud --route frontier:7 --throttle 0 --first-night`, looked at.
351. **The polish pass in the real app window (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #88; the director, 8 Oct 2026).** Every menu screen, the yard, the in-night menu, the route card and the supplies walked in the app itself (xvfb, the real window path, 1280x720), at 100% and 150% TEXT SIZE and in the colourblind palette, beside the headless renders. What was off, fixed:
    - **TEXT SIZE shrank the fine print on a small window.** `Hud.PromptScaleAt` picked the half step wherever a font pixel got two of the screen's, but 150%'s smaller canvas gives a 720p window four screen pixels a canvas pixel, so it took the half step: the prompts, the corner and the panels came out smaller at 150% than at 100% (2 screen pixels a font pixel against 2.67). It now asks TEXT SIZE's scale more of the screen (`PromptScaleAt(pixels, textScale)`, `Keys.TextScale` by default), so the fine print only grows as the text does: 720p is 2.67, 3.33 and 4; 1080p 2, 2.5 and 3. `TextSizeTests.TheFinePrintNeverShrinksAsTheTextGrows` (540p to 1440p), and the HUD's fit test now runs at a 540p, 720p, 1080p and 1440p window (it had only 1080p's scale).
    - **The first nights' card ran off a small frame** (150% on a 540p window) and showed through the supplies panel. Its rows break between controls where one is wider than the frame, and it gives way to the roster, the supplies, the route card and the map.
    - **The supplies panel** steps down to the half step when the whole step won't fit the frame.
    - **A night from the command line** drew its first frame on the default canvas (no menu frame before it to take TEXT SIZE): the display settings are applied as the night starts.
    - **A long menu's "..."** on its first or last row read as part of that row's label ("TEXT SIZE: 100%  ..."): a small arrow on the plate's top or bottom edge says there's more.
    - **Not changed:** the HUD's "REPAIR KIT" against the wiki's "engineering kit" (moot: #299, note 301's second slice, took the kit and its HUD lines out); the in-night menu's heading and RESUME both say the night goes on (`NightMenuTests` holds RESUME's); paths on the profile screen print in capitals, the pixel font having no lower case.
    - **The app headless, for menus too:** `--screen name` opens a menu screen (`fortress` is slot 1's) and `--select n` moves down it, and `--capture` with no night writes the menu as last drawn.
383. **HOLD KEYS: holds as toggles (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #120; GDD §32 "Accessibility").** A player who can't keep a key down couldn't run, keep the brake on, talk, use the radio or read the roster. With **HOLD KEYS** on TOGGLE (`Settings.ToggleHolds`, off by default), a press of one of `Settings.Toggleable` (run, the brake, talk, the radio, the crew roster) latches it on and the next lets go (`HoldLatch`, read through the app's one `Held`).
    - **Client-side only:** what goes into the intent is the same held button, so the host, the sim and prediction can't tell. Turning it off lets go of everything latched.
    - **Use stays a hold:** a tap at a locker stows, a hold mends; latching it would turn every tap into a hold. The movement keys, the swing, the whistle and the emote wheel (held to aim, let go to do) stay as they are.
    - **What's said:** the first nights' card drops HOLD for those ("TALK : [V]"), and the VOICE setting says PUSH TO TALK (TAP V). The corner already said "BRAKE : [B]".
    - **Verified:** `HoldLatchTests`: hold is the key down; toggle presses on and off and the key down no longer counts; Use and the rest stay holds; off lets go; the card's wording; the setting saves.
386. **The settings in sections, and the loading screen looked at (F1, UI/UX 3; queue #123).** The settings had grown to thirty-odd rows in one list, the accessibility rows between the HUD's and the mouse's. They're now grouped under headings: YOU (the name, the outfit), SOUND AND VOICE, SCREEN (the HUD, the hints, the display), CONTROLS AND COMFORT (the mouse, the field of view, the shake, the headset's comfort, the key bindings) and ACCESSIBILITY (TEXT SIZE, COLOURS, CAPTIONS, HOLD KEYS, FIRST NIGHTS).
    - **A heading is a row** (`MenuItem.Heading`, built by `FrontEnd.Heading`): greyed so the keys pass over it as they pass over any greyed row, never clicked (no hit box), drawn dim and flush left with a rule out to the plate's edge. Nothing about the settings themselves changed.
    - **The loading screen** (note 350's tip under BUILDING THE NIGHT) had no headless shot: `dt screenshot --menu title --loading [n]` draws it with the n-th tip (and `--text-size`), looked at at 100% and 150%.
    - **The tests' own pickers skip headings:** the helpers that find a row by its label's start and step down to it (`Choose`, `Pick`, `Toggle` in eight test files) took "SOUND" for the SOUND AND VOICE heading and stepped forever; they match rows only now.
    - **Verified:** `SettingsSectionsTests`: every row under its section, in order, the headings greyed; the selection never rests on a heading, up or down; the night's settings keep the sections without the name and the headset's rows.

355. **Turning on the spot is silent (queue #92, D1; GDD App. F.1, build 1121: "turning on the spot shouldn't make a sound; only walking should").** The crew's feet scuffed once a turn standing still passed 1.2 rad (`GameAudio.Crew`'s `ScuffTurn`): a look round played a footstep. Gone; the scuff is now only for stopping short from a run, as before. `CrewAudioTests.FootstepsFallOncePerStrideAtTheFeetOnWhatsUnderThem` turns a full circle in a second standing still and hears nothing.
356. **A coupling working loose, the third upkeep job while the train runs (queue #93, D1; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "on the train, still relatively boring from point A to point B"; [orchestrator.md](design/orchestrator.md) §5.1 U2).**
    - **What it is.** Every `everyMetres` (6 km ± half) of the train's running, the pin in one of its gaps works loose: `Vehicle.Loose` on the car ahead of the gap, the seconds it's been at it. The metres count `roughFactor` (3) times over while the engine is on a bend tighter than `roughRadius` (800 m): the outline's "rough track". Never the engine's own coupling (that would be the whole train) and never behind the last car; none in the first 4 km, none in the yard or a fort, never more loose than there are crewmates alive. All in `upkeep.json` `coupling`; host only (`Couplings`), the vehicle record carries it (protocol 37).
    - **The tell.** The pin knocks in its knuckle (`coupling-loose`, a synth loop: a dull 340 Hz clank with a ring over it, 1.4 knocks a second at first, 5.5 at the end, louder as it goes), and the gap is called out as every break is (note 301's amber glow and sparks, `BreakKind.Coupling`, the sparks spitting up out of the gap). The prompt in the gap says TIGHTEN THE COUPLING, or the key that puts the wrench in hand.
    - **The fix.** The wrench in hand (bare hands where the wrench isn't the repair tool), Use held 4 s with the hands within 2.2 m of the pin: from the plate in the gap, an end ladder over it, or the ground beside. It comes before the plate's doors, so at a loose pin with the wrench in hand it's the pin that's worked; Uncouple is its own key and is untouched.
    - **Left alone.** After 90 s the pin drops and the rake parts behind it (`TrainOnLine.Uncouple`): §24's cut-car rules, what's behind rolls free at the speed it had, and the knuckle's release and the hoses parting are heard (`CrewCouplings`). The worst job, so the rarest: one a 24 km night on the flat, more on a night of bends.
    - **Bots.** A walker goes to it as to a hot box (`RoofWalkerBot.Grease`, now either job: along the roofs, down the end ladder into the gap), puts the wrench in hand and tightens it; any bot in reach does the same (`Heed.Coupling`).
    - **Verified.** `LooseCouplingTests` (7): one comes loose by the running, never the engine's nor behind the last car; a bend looses it a third as far on; left alone the rake parts behind it; the wrench tightens it in its time and the shovel doesn't; not from the roof nor inside; a bot in the gap puts the wrench in hand and tightens it; a three-bot crew's walker goes down into the gap and tightens one before it parts. `dt screenshot --view gapside --loose 60`, looked at; `dt audio render --sound coupling-loose --param loose=0.1` and `=0.9`, the spectrograms looked at (clean knocks, a peak near the hot box's).

352. **Loot on every yard line, and out before the train arrives (A1, queue #89; the director, 8 Oct 2026: "I really dont like that I spent all this work pulling into a yard switch line that had no loot and watched the loot spawn in the yard after I'd already stopped the train. Loot should spawn in all yard lines in early game and mid game").** Two things were wrong, and they were separate.
    - **A bare siding.** A yard's stock (level-design P14, stops.json `stock`) was dealt into shed bays picked at random across every shed until the tier's cars' worth ran out, so a siding could stand with nothing beside it: of 40 yards a tier, 3 local, 3 frontier and 3 dead-lines yards had a bare siding (about one yard in thirteen; deep territory's bigger stock left none bare). Now, where the tier's `everyTrack` is set, every yard track has something to load beside its loading face: a crane bay of its own, or a container in a shed it stands beside, on its side of the shed (nearer it than the shed's other track). A track the dice left bare gets a crate stack in the bay of such a shed nearest the middle of its face, on its side (`StopGenerator.StockEveryTrack`). No dice are drawn and the stack is the last container laid, so the rest of the stop (its track, its buildings, what the economy deals into its other containers, its kits and toys) is what it was; `dt site sweep --seeds 30` is unchanged on every tier, band and attempt count alike (the planner fills the empties from what's nearest, so more stock doesn't move the score).
    - **Reading:** "early game and mid game" is the first three tiers (local, frontier, dead lines; `everyTrack` true), and deep territory is left to its dice (false), though its bigger stock left no siding bare in 40 yards. One flag a tier to move.
    - **Pop-in.** A stop's loot (its crate stacks, strongroom, village finds, kits and toys) came out when the train first stopped there (`StepLoot`: under run.json `stopBelowSpeed`, inside its zone), and a facility's own crates when the train first stopped on its spur (`StepLoading`): in front of whoever was looking. Now both come out once the engine is on the main line within loot.json `stockAhead` (800 m) of the stop's zone, whatever its speed: further out than enemies.json `interestRadius` (520 m, the furthest a client is ever sent a body from), the lamp and the fog, so nobody sees them appear. 0 puts back the old rule. A stop passed at speed keeps its loot lying out; asleep and outside everyone's interest, it costs neither physics nor bandwidth.
    - **Verified:** `YardLootTests`: every yard track on local, frontier and dead lines has something beside it (40 seeds × yard and yard-and-village × no facility, a foundry and a switchyard); deep territory's flag is off; with the flag off and on, the same seed lays the same containers and only adds crate stacks (and on frontier some are added); a stop's loot is out with the train at speed 100 m inside `stockAhead` and not 300 m outside it, and `stockAhead` is beyond `interestRadius`; with no look-ahead it waits for the train to stop, as it did; a facility's crates are out as the train comes up to it. `dt site --tier frontier --seed 1 --kind yard`: the outermost siding, bare before, has its stack on its side of the long shed.

353. **Towns that are lived in: townsfolk with their own breathing gear, a round for everyone, a green and the things a walled-in people put up (queue #90, B2; the director, 8 Oct 2026, with two shots of an open house: "We need townsfolk models who wear some sort of respirator mask or oxygen mask or other breathing apparatuses to indicate the air is foul. Note some of the animation positions are off. Towns dont feel like they have a natural layout to them. There needs to be a behaviour loop for all the NPCs, its weird that so many of them are just standing around doing nothing. These towns need layouts, parks, signs of governance, signs of culture, statues, things that tell the story of a people walled in for fear of the outside world and what becomes of those who rarely leave the walls. They'd be trying to find ways of making the world feel tolerable.").** Renumbered from #89 and 352, which A1's #294 landed first.
    - **The poses were off.**
        - **In a short house the range's crouch was on the table's chair.** The layout put the chair 0.26 m from where the one at the range crouches: the director's shot had the seated one beside the chair and the crouched one on it. `HouseLayout.TableV`: the table (and its chair behind it) come forward in a house under ~6.3 m deep, so the range keeps 0.65 m.
        - **crouch_idle floated.** crew_clips.py plants most clips' feet (`rig.feet_planter`) but not crouch_idle's, so a crouched figure is drawn ~0.5 m up. A town's people are set down on their feet (`CreatureArt.FeetOver`, the lowest foot or ball joint at the clip's start over the idle's 0.03 m); a seated one sits on the gunner clip's pan (its pelvis over the chair, 0.08 m over its 0.48 m seat, `TownsfolkArtTests`). The crew's own crouch is C1/E1's (the clip): it still floats on the train.
        - **No swivelling off a chair.** Whoever's seated, crouched or mending stays as they are when talked to; only those standing turn to you.
    - **Their own breathing gear, never the crew's mask.** A town's people are the survivors' bare-headed figure (survivor_prisoner, the wildlander's patched coat on one in three), not the crew's masked one. `TownsfolkKit` makes the gear in the figure's bind pose and `CreatureArt.Wear` carries it on a bone (the head's skinning matrix for the face, spine_03's for the body); a hose runs between where the pose has put its two ends (`CreatureArt.Posed`):
        - a respirator: a rubber half-mask, a filter can either cheek, two straps;
        - oxygen: an amber cup on a hose over the shoulder to a green bottle slung on the back;
        - a rebreather: a mine-rescue set (the mouthpiece, the nose clip, two hoses to the breathing bag on the chest and its scrubber can);
        - a wrap: wool over the nose and mouth, a tin can sewn into it.

        The town's character weights the kinds (houses.json `gear`: a company issues its respirator and the pit's rebreather; a cove makes its own wraps). Each person's is drawn from their name (`Townsperson.Gear`, `TownGear.Pick`, in the kinds' order whatever the file's). At home half have the mask down on the chest. Hats out of doors: a sou'wester, a knitted toque, a flat cap, a headscarf. The survivors' chest lamp is dark on a townsperson. `dt art townsfolk [--full] [--pose ...]` lines them up.
    - **A round for everyone** (`TownRounds`, `Town.Now`; towns.json `rounds`). They go round on the night's clock: `World.Step` sets `Town.Clock` from the tick, so every machine has them in the same places.
        - **Out of doors**, a day is four slots of 45 s. The square's folk go out every other slot; the people at their doors (the clerk, the keeper, the store, the fitter) once, in the middle, when the rest are back at their posts, so there's always somebody to have a word with. Where they go: a bench to sit on, a fire barrel (hands out to it), the board or the laws to read, a stall's counter, a mend at the crate, a vigil at the centrepiece, the statue or the wall of names, a garden to tend, or a word with somebody at their post (one time in three first). A place holds one a slot, and nobody's put within 0.9 m of anyone else that slot. The way there is clear of what's solid: `Town.Clear` sweeps a body's width at the knees and the chest, `Town.Free` keeps the stop out of walls, and an 8 m wall index keeps a 3000-person town's planning under 0.1 s. The gate's people pace their post; a street's lamp-carriers walk to a neighbour's; the lampman walks the line.
        - **At home**, each of the household goes round the rooms' places (the range, the table, the parlour's chair, the window, the stair, the door) in turn, starting from their own, so no two share one. Each house has its own phase. The way between is the shortest over a 0.4 m grid of the places a body can stand, through the partition's doorway, pulled straight.
        - **They walk at the end of a slot** to arrive as the next begins, so everyone is at their post as the night starts. Acts play crew clips: sat (gunner), crouched (crouch_idle), mending (mend), hands to a fire (carry), at a counter (push), a lamp up (lantern), walking (walk, or lantern_walk with a lamp), and a word with somebody (now and then point).
        - **Whoever you talk to stops for you** (`Town.Hold`, from `TownTalk.Step`): their round waits on this machine and goes on from there after. Talking still changes nothing in the night.
        - **Townspeople aren't solid any more.** A wall of their own would stand in a different place on a machine that's stopped somebody, and prediction would diverge. App. F.1's solid world is the town's walls, houses and furniture.
    - **A walled town's green, its governance and its culture** (`TownPlan.Green`, `CivicKit`, `WorldArt.Civic`; towns.json `laws`, `civic`, `walled`). Every piece can be looked at and says something sideways:
        - **The green**, across the first street from the square, where the far row and the next street's near row would be: grass, gravel paths corner to corner, lamps. On it:
            - a statue: the survivors' figure cast in bronze or cut in stone on a plinth, frozen in its pose (the Founder's palm out; the Lamplighter's lamp lit; the Child looking up; the Railwayman turned from the gate);
            - the wall of names: slate, the names cut pale, iron rings by some, a row of blank slates already mounted;
            - the bandstand, a sky painted under its roof;
            - lamp gardens: cloches, or tin flowers in damp soil;
            - tin trees and the old elm hung with paper leaves and little lamps;
            - benches.
        - **Governance** (every town): four of the council's ordinances posted by the clerk's door, and the town's flag in the square.
        - **Culture:** the day painted on the inside of the back wall at the ends of the first streets: a sunrise over the sea, a window on a field, the day the wall's length.
        - **What becomes of those who rarely leave:** a walled town's folk have lines of their own ("My youngest was born inside. She asked me once if the train goes anywhere, or only comes.").
        - `dt screenshot --town green|statue|memorial|mural|garden`, `--clock s` for the rounds.
    - **Verified:**
        - `TownsfolkTests`:
            - gear of the town's kinds, the same every time;
            - everyone on a round, back at their post when it comes round;
            - every round clear of every wall (a bench's sitter aside), never two in one place, over two of its longest periods at three sizes up to 2000;
            - talking holds them and they go on;
            - the green and its pieces, the laws, the flag and the mural, each lookable.
        - `TownsfolkArtTests`: crouched set down, seated on the chair, every piece of gear built and cheap.
        - `TownTests` (people in no wall now, they've none of their own).
        - Looked at: the lineups, the sitter, the range, the armchair, the square over a round, the green, the statue, the names, the gardens, the mural.
    - **Not yet:**
        - natural layouts: streets that bend with the land, irregular setbacks, a crescent round the green;
        - the quiet house;
        - a council house of its own;
        - murals and a green for a small town (the yard's corridor);
        - a modelled townsfolk figure (tools/models needs Blender, not in this container: the gear is procedural on the survivors' figure).

357. **At a switch stand, Use is the lever's (A1, queue #94; found following up the switch audit, note 289).** `World.CrewAct` works a switch's lever (`SwitchStands.CrewAct`, Use held `junctions.throwSeconds`) before the hands (`Bodies.Handle`), and neither knew of the other: so the press that started a throw also put down what was carried (the lamp you'd carried out to the stand in the dark, dropped at your feet) or, empty-handed, picked up whatever lay by the stand, and the lever still went over. The cab's interactables were already spared the pick-up (`CrewActions.NearestInteractable` blocks it), but a stand isn't one of them, and nothing spared what was carried. The HUD offered the thing lying by the stand before the switch, and with something in hand offered nothing.
    - **Reading:** at a lever, the lever has Use, as at a Holdout's lock or a ruptured boiler with the kit in hand (`keep`): what's carried stays carried and nothing lying by it is picked up. Throw still lets go of what's carried (the same as everywhere). The alternative, "hands first" (put the lamp down to throw the switch), keeps one rule for the whole game, but it makes a lit lamp at a stand a thing you must set down in the dark, and a crate by a stand a thing you must move before you can throw it; the stand was always meant to be worked alone with a lamp (GDD §17).
    - **What changed:** `Bodies.Handle` takes `lever` (World passes `Switches.InReach`: a stand's lever or, with the powered thrower fitted, the cab's): carried, it's kept unless Throw; empty-handed, nothing is picked up. The HUD's switch prompt is one helper (`Hud.SwitchPrompt`, the cab's lever and a stand's) said before what's carried and before what's lying in reach, as the sim decides it. `Bots.Heal` doesn't hold Use for a healing find at a switch's lever, where it would throw the switch (its own rule: "never at a lever or a door").
    - **Verified:** `SwitchTests.AtAStandUseIsTheLeversNotTheHands`: Use held at a stand with a lamp in hand throws it and the lamp's still in hand; empty-handed with a crate by the stand it throws back and the crate stays down; Throw lets go there; a step away, Use picks up as it always did (it failed on main at the lamp). `HudTests.AtAStandThePromptIsTheLeversWhateversInYourHandsOrLyingByIt`: THROW TO with a crate by the stand and with a lamp in hand, and holding Use throws it with the lamp kept.

359. **S-bends (queue #96, B1; level-design B.4 and note 278's "Not yet"; the director, 6 Oct 2026: derailing on a bend is the core fear, and always the driver's mistake).** Note 278 gave every night its tier's hard bends, each one turn. Two hard turns close together couldn't be laid: each was its own curve limit and its own demand, and two lethal demands inside half a braking distance fail the lethal spacing check (§7.3), the rule that a driver who brakes for one can brake for the next. An S-bend is the one place that rule's reading is wrong: the driver should brake once and hold it.
    - **The piece** (`LineBuilder.SBend`, setpieces.json `hardBend` `sDeflectionDeg` 30–50 and `sGapM` 20–50): two turns at the hard bend's radius, either way, with a short straight between and its straights either side. Where room is short, shorter straights, then smaller turns; none under its least turn (one turn is laid instead). Realised as a reverse curve (`HShape.Reverse` with `gapM`: the straight between exactly as the piece says, the first turn the way the world band has room for; its heading comes out as it went in).
    - **How many** (tiers.json columns `sBends`): the chance a hard bend is laid as an S. Local 0 (its one or two teach the board, and a Local night lerping toward Frontier stays at none), Frontier 0.2, Dead Lines 0.3, Deep 0.4, Deep max 0.5. Rolled on a stream of its own keyed by where the bend is (`sBend`), so a night without one lays exactly as it did, and an S counts as one of the night's bends.
    - **Held as one** (`CurveLimits`, `HeldTo`): the first turn's limit runs on until the train's tail is round the second (the resume board a train's length past the S's last turn, not its first), so the second turn's limit starts under it at the same figure and is no demand of its own. One board, one demand, one resume; the lethal spacing check sees one lethal check. Form 19's line says "S-bend". The board pass already skips a curve under a lower-or-equal limit that a demand boarded (note 278), and the cab map already inks each curve limit of a board's figure in its reach (note 285, which found an S of ordinary curves on deepTerritory:2), so the second turn is red on the map with its figure.
    - **The land** (`IntentsFor`, `SBendMiddle`): the hill on each turn's inside, the fall on its outside, changing sides halfway along the straight between.
    - **By a branch** (`AwayFromBranches(…, s: true)`): an S comes out on the side it first turns to. Past a dead line's toe it first turns away from the dead line, as a single bend does. In an alternate's window it first turns away from the alternate, so it steps the main line away (a single bend turns toward the alternate's side, which keeps a one-way turn's line on the far side of its chord; an S has no chord to be the far side of).
    - **The metrics** report `sBends`. `hardBends` counts an S's turns as two, as it counts a reverse curve's halves (note 278).
    - **After** (`dt linegen sweep --cars 6 --seeds 30`, against the same code with `sBends` 0, which lays what main lays): S-bends on 11/30 Frontier nights (15 in all), 15/30 Dead Lines (16) and 28/30 Deep (35); none on Local. Demands a night unchanged (Frontier 14.2, Dead Lines 16.0 against 15.8, Deep 17.6 against 17.7): an S adds none. Every night passes with no fallback seed. First-attempt pass rates Frontier 0.87 (0.83), Dead Lines 0.83 (0.80), Deep 0.83 (0.77); within two 1.0 (0.97), 0.93 (0.97), 0.90 (0.87). Local is identical. The sweep's summary now reports `meanHardBends`, `sBends` and `nightsWithSBends`. The fallback seeds are re-proven (`--fallbacks`); Local's moved too, though Local lays as it did: they had gone stale on main since note 278. frontier:7 has two (8.8 km and 22.9 km along the main line): one board at 50 km/h 130 m before the first, one limit from 8975 to 9688 over both turns, one demand.
    - **Not yet:** hard bends (single or S) on alternates and dead lines (still the main line only); an S of three turns.
    - **Verified:** `HardBendTests.AnSBendIsHeldAsOneBendThroughBothItsTurns` (deepTerritory 1–3, deadLines 1, 2, 4: each S's two turns go opposite ways, one curve demand from before its first turn's tightest point to its second turn, its limit held past the second turn's tightest point, at a speed under what derails either, Form 19's "S-bend"; the lethal spacing check passes); `AHardBendIsBoardedAndGoesRoundAHill` now takes an S's two turns, each boarded (the second by the first's board) and each with its hill on the inside. The full Sim suite (1166) and Game suite (601, one skipped) pass with frontier:7's two S-bends in it.
370. **The art checklist's "not yet" lines, a second round (queue #107, C1; first claimed as #91 and note 354, then #96 and 359, renumbered each time another's claim landed first).** Three lines on the checklist said what was still missing; each is now drawn, and each is presentation only (nothing sent, nothing in the sim's state that a client predicts).
    - **The cars lean out on a bend taken too fast** (`overspeed-telegraph`: "not yet: the cars don't lean"; App. F.1's telegraph, "the cars straining and leaning").
        - `CarLean` rolls each car about its outer rail by its own strain (`BendStrain.PerCar`, note 265's stress): `stress^1.5` of train.json `overspeed.leanDegrees` (4°), so the inner wheels come up off the rail as it nears derailing.
        - It settles into the lean over `leanSeconds` (0.35 s). Past half way to derailing it rocks on its springs by `leanRock` (0.18) of it.
        - The sessions lean the frames they hand the renderer (`InterpolatedFrames`): the car, whoever's on it, the eye riding it and the replay that records them all lean together. The sim's frames never do. Once the train's off the rails the lean is gone, and the wreck's frames are drawn as they are (note 330).
        - `dt screenshot --strain x` leans the staged train, and the new `lean` view looks up the train from the line behind it.
    - **A ball from the train's own guns leaves its scorch on the train** (`cannon-impacts`: "a ball on the train's own body leaves no scorch (the car moves on)").
        - On first sight of an impact on the train (`ImpactSurface.Train`: a ball the train's body stopped, or a powder car going up, note 182), the scene finds the car it came down on and the face it struck: the side, end or roof nearest, carried on by the car's way since the impact's tick (`GreyboxScene.OnTheTrain`). The burn is then kept in that car's frame for the rest of the night (32 at most, oldest first out).
        - `Effects.TrainScorch` draws it lit, as a fire's char is (`Effects.Char`): a burnt ring, a black heart and blistered paint at its edge, kept within the face it's on. For its first seconds the iron glows with embers going out, and a thread of smoke comes off it a while longer. An unlit FX decal was tried first: it read lighter than the car at night, not darker.
        - `dt screenshot --impact train --impact-at -47,-1.55 --impact-age 30 --view side`.
    - **A crate being carried stays in the wreck's arms** (`wreck-task-poses`: "not yet: a carried crate isn't in the ragdoll's hands").
        - `FilmPlayer.Carried` says what was in someone's arms as the train came off (not a body or the child they were carrying). The film (`WreckFilm.Record`) gives it its own ball: held between the hands (`WreckFilm.InArms`) while they hold their work's pose (`taskHold`), then let go with the hands' way. It falls and strikes the cars and the ground as a body does, and tumbles on its own seeded spin (`Pcg32(seed, 0x10AD + doll)`, so the dolls' film is exactly what it was) until it comes to rest flat.
        - `FilmFrame.Loads` records it. `DerailSequence.FilmBodies` draws it as the body it was, turned by `Body.Tilt` (drawn only). `dt screenshot --wreck-poses` stages the carrier with a crate in their arms.
    - **Verified:**
        - `CarLeanTests`: the angle at the board and at the limit, the lean about the outer rail with the inner wheels lifting, settling in and out, and the sim's frames untouched.
        - `WreckDeathTests.ACarriedCrateGoesIntoTheWreckInTheirArmsAndIsThrownFree`: in the arms while held, the dolls' film identical with and without it, tumbling, and at rest flat on the ground.
        - Looked at: `lean` at strain 0 and 1, `flanges` and `gapside` straining, the scorch at 2 s and 30 s, and the poses with the crate.

369. **The HUD's last lines in note 285's form (B3, queue #106; GDD §32; note 285's rules, found re-reading `Hud.cs`).** Three lines had missed note 285's round two. The cold step still said what it does ("KILLING COLD: OUTSIDE, IT COMES ON 1.75X FASTER", note 201's line), where note 285 cut every (FASTER). The run end's commendation picker and the film's skip still put the key first ("COMMEND [LEFT/RIGHT] DAVE   [UP/DOWN] KEPT THE FIRE   [SPACE] GIVE", "HOLD [SPACE] TO SKIP").
    - **The cold step** (`Hud.ColdLine`) is its name alone: DEEP COLD, BITTER COLD, KILLING COLD. How much faster it comes on outside is learned out in it. The chilled countdown ("COLD: 40S") is an alarm and stays.
    - **The picker** (`Hud.CommendLine`): who and what, each with the key that changes it, then the action: "DAVE : [LEFT/RIGHT]   KEPT THE FIRE : [UP/DOWN]   COMMEND : [SPACE]" (the headset's stick and click the same way). It's what to do, so it's fine print with keycaps (note 285), at the foot under the commendations, as the alarms' how-to is.
        - **It fits.** At full size a name of twenty letters (`Messages.NameLength`) ran off both sides of the 480-wide canvas, and every TEXT SIZE (note 347) made it worse. `Hud.CommendLines` keeps it on one line, with a name too long for it cut short ("BARTHOLOMEW F. : [LEFT/RIGHT]   CAME BACK FOR ME : ..." at 720p): the name is the only part of the line of any length. Only where no name would go on one line (125% in a 720p window) does the choice go over COMMEND, and then the report and the commendations rise a line to make room.
        - **Reading: a cut name over a second line.** At 720p with a few bookmarks, the report is already down to its last lines ("... AND 14 MORE LINES"). Raised a line, the commendations' title ran into the report's money line (`dt screenshot --hud --route frontier:7 --report derailed --commend --commend-pick "Bartholomew Fenwicke"`, looked at both ways).
    - **The skip** (`Hud.SkipLine`): "SKIP : HOLD [SPACE]", with the crew's votes after it under the vote ("SKIP : HOLD [SPACE]   2/5").
    - **Staged:** `dt screenshot --hud --report --commend --commend-pick [name]` (`Hud.StagedCommendPick`; only a networked night has a picker of its own). The cold line is `--hazards cold`, as before.
    - **Verified:** `HudTests.TheHudSaysHowDeepTheColdIs` (the name alone, in the form), and `HudTests.TheCommendationPickerAndTheSkipSayTheActionAndItsKey`. That test covers the picker and the skip in the form, at every TEXT SIZE's canvas in a 720p and a 1080p window and on a headset's panel. It checks a short name, a twenty-letter one and one given: every line is inside the frame, and a short name always stays on one line at 1080p.
358. **The upkeep heard (AU1, queue #95; D1's notes 331 and 346, [orchestrator.md](design/orchestrator.md) §5.1).** The jobs the train makes as it runs had D1's synth tells (`hotbox`, `lamp-gutter`) but no checklist lines, and the hands on them made no sound.
    - **The faults' lines.** `state-hotbox`: the dry journal's squeal (`journal`: real bell metal frozen into a held ring at 1.45 kHz with a fifth over it, catching once a wheel turn at 3.2 Hz, with the journal's grind under it; `screech`: thin plate driven harsher, seizing and slipping) and the box smoking (`cooking`: grease crackling and spitting, a thin hiss). `state-gutter`: the wick spitting in clusters with the chimney ticking (`wick`), and the flame starved, lapping and tearing (`flame`, the junction lamp's). They're swapped in for D1's synths the way #205 swapped main's (install.py `TELL_SOUNDS`), D1's tier, range and params kept: "heat" lifts the squeal's pitch and level and brings the smoke in from halfway, "gutter" raises the sputter and the flutter. D1's synths are the fallback (tools/audio/synth-defs), and the takes are levelled to them through the game's own mixer (`swaplevel.py hotbox lamp-gutter`, with the heat at 0.7 and the guttering at 0.6: `SWAP_GAIN_DB` +4 and −16, within half a dB after).
    - **The hands (`crew-upkeep`).** `grease`: a lever grease gun worked at the box, a stroke a second, the grease squirting and spitting on the hot iron, held while a crewmate's hold at a hot box goes on (`HotBoxes.Within` and their `ActionProgress`, as the breach's boarding reads it). `greased`: the box gone cool, the last of it hissing off, but not when it went cool by catching (one that was within a second of `fireAfter` caught; its car's fire is the sound). `trim`: a guttering lamp's wick wound up a few brass clicks and the flame catching steady, as the guttering stops with the lamp still lit; gone out instead, it's the lamp going off (`crew-lamps.car-lamp-off`).
    - **Pinned:** `UpkeepSoundTests`: a greased box hisses once and a caught one doesn't; the gun's heard while a crewmate's at the box and not once it's cool; a trimmed lamp's heard and one gone out isn't.
    - **Not yet:** #93's coupling working loose (D1) when it lands; the director's Keep or Redo.
372. **Toys a lamp finds (queue #109, C1; the director, 8 Oct, on what's found at a stop: "a bit of a brighter more unique look to them so that they stand out from the background as interactable objects. Do this with good texture work, not VFX").** B4's finds atlas (note 326) answered the director for the village finds. The toys are found in the same cupboards and cellars and on the same doorsteps, but they were still drawn in their first paint: library wool and plaster tinted dark, averaging 37–68 (sRGB) against the atlas's 172. On a house's boards under a lamp they were brown lumps.
    - **Their own paint and cloth** (`tools/models/recipes/train_stores.py`, `toy_*` materials). Each part is tinted to come out at a chosen colour on its library layer: the bear in honey mohair, worn paler at the paws, with a brass button eye; the horse in ivory, a pillar-box red saddle and a pine board; the doll's porcelain and a dusty-rose smock with auburn hair; the pig's pink; the music box in polished walnut, red velvet and bright brass; the drummer in red, blue and green tin. The textures now average 93–145. The layers keep their wear, so they still read as old. The extinguisher, the kit and the shot locker keep their own materials.
    - **Not done by:** a glint, an outline or a light. That's the director's "not VFX". The gloss is the library layers' own: the spec bake takes gloss from the layer's map, not the material's roughness, so lowering roughness on the glazes changed nothing and isn't relied on.
    - **`dt screenshot --toys [h]`:** the six on the floor `h` m (default 1.6) under the eye, in an arc in front of it. In one of B4's searched houses: `--searched --toys --route frontier:7 --at 10250 --cam 10254.5,88.6,1.6 --target 10252,95,0.4 --lantern --fov 75`.
    - **Verified:** `dt art check` (no piece over budget; triangles unchanged), `PropArtTests`, `LookTests`, `HouseInteriorArtTests`, `StopArtTests`. Looked at: the six in the house before and after.

368. **The steam lift (A1, queue #105; spec D.2: "requires the locomotive coupled nearby and venting pressure to power it. 2 crew. Ties loading directly to the boiler; you're at zero pressure while it runs"; D.3: "steam lift fails through resource conflict: the boiler can't do two jobs").** The one module in the Wiki's Loading table that was never built (spec D.2's conveyor line and tipple, which the Wiki doesn't list, are still to come). The mine head has it now, beside its winch and crates (facilities.json `kinds`: `["lift", "winch", "crates"]`): two 2-person modules at one stop, D.3's "someone is alone somewhere".
    - **How it works:** a headframe over the shaft out on the site's side, where the mine head's buildings already put theirs (StructureKit's, 25 m back from the layout point and 16 m out, so the sim's and the art's agree), its chute out over the spur. Someone holds the lever (`Run.LiftLeverInReach`); the engine stands with its middle within `lift.steamReach` (56 m) of the chute (`EngineInReach`: the first three cars behind it come under the chute in reach; the rest are the winch's and the crates'); and the cab's vent is held open. Then the vented steam winds the skip instead of going into the air: each point of pressure vented is 1/`steamPerSkip` (20) of a wind, and a wound skip tips `perSkip` (0.25) of a car-load of ore down the chute into the car under it (within `tolerance`), out of `ore` (3) car-loads. No car there, it's on the ballast; a full one overflows and strains, as the spout's does. The winding engine is machinery, loud (`Run.Machinery`).
    - **"Zero pressure while it runs":** `Boiler.VentedSteam` is what the vent actually let go each step: its full rate (boiler.json `ventRate`, 12 a second) while there's pressure, and with the gauge run down only what the fire's making after the engine's own heating and auxiliaries. So a full boiler winds about four skips (a car-load) at once, then the gauge sits at nothing and the lift goes at the fire's pace (a standing full firebox about 1.8 a second, about 1 a second to the lift after heating: a skip in about 20 s), and the engine pulls nothing until the vent's shut and the gauge is back over `powerFloor`. Walking the next car under the chute waits on the fire.
    - **Readings:** "venting pressure to power it" is the cab's vent, held by someone in the cab (the driver), so the 2 crew are the lever and the vent: one on the ground, one in the cab. "The locomotive coupled nearby" is the engine standing in reach of the headframe's steam line, with no hose to couple (a distance, `steamReach`); the train is walked under the chute a car at a time as under the spout. The mine head keeps its winch and crates: added, not swapped.
    - **Bots:** `StopPlan.LiftTarget` (the spout's, limited to cars that come under the chute with the engine in reach) and a `Lifting` leg after the loading: the driver walks each car under the chute and vents while the shunter's on the lever (`Site.LeverHeld`, last tick's, host only: the "steam!" a driver hears), and holds the train still while it winds; the shunter's `Lift` stands at the lever and holds it while a car with room stands under the chute. At an ordinary mine head the winch and crates fill the spur's four empties first, so a bot crew rarely needs the lift; it works it when there's room left.
    - **Presentation:** the lever's prompt is `LIFT : HOLD [E]   CAR n% FULL`, `WINDING   CAR n% FULL`, or `NO CAR UNDER THE CHUTE`; in the cab, the vent's `VENTING` reads `STEAM TO THE LIFT` while it's winding; the crew's spout pose at the lever. The greybox draws the ore bin on its legs astride the track, the trough from the headframe down to it, the skip on its guides as far as it's wound, the ore gauge, the lever (down while it winds) and ore falling as a skip tips. Protocol 37: the run record's sites carry the ore left, the skip's wind and whether it's winding. Audio is AU1's: the winding engine and the tip are a line on the audio checklist (the machinery's loudness already counts for the Choir).
    - **Verified:** `SteamLiftTests` (7): the mine head has it beside its winch, off the crates; it winds only with a hand on the lever and the engine venting into it, and each skip lands in the car under the chute; with the fire out the boiler's steam is all the skips there are, the gauge ends at nothing, and fired again it winds again; with the gauge at nothing and a full fire it winds at the fire's pace and the pressure comes back once the vent's shut; only an engine within reach winds it (the first three cars come under in reach); with no car under the chute the ore's on the ballast; a client sees it. `StopCrewTests.AtTheMineHeadTheDriverVentsIntoTheSteamLiftWhileTheShunterWindsIt`: a bot crew, through intent alone, with no crates and the cars run in empty, walks the cars under the chute ("Lifting"), winds it ("winding") and loads more ore than the winch's sleds hold, and leaves whole. `HudTests.AtTheSteamLiftsLeverThePromptSaysTheCarUnderTheChuteAndTheCabSaysWhereTheSteamsGoing`. `dt facility drill mineHead`: an ordinary crew still leaves with the spur's cars full (395 s, 6/6). `dt screenshot --route deepTerritory:3 --site --facility mineHead --lifting [--wind 0.6]`: the bin over car 1, the trough down from the art's headframe, the winding house beyond.
342. **Signs off the train heard (AU1, queue #79; D1.1's note 327 left the hook).** A crewmate afoot at a stop is shown a pair of eyes at the lamp's edge, toward where a creature lives there (`World.Watcher`), and `GameAudio.Watched` plays `sign.<kind>` (`GameAudio.SignCue`, `Director.Key`'s names) once as they appear, from the eyes, at 0.7. Until now it played each creature's own movement (`SignFallback`), which was at least the same animal, but louder than a sign should be and sometimes its approach.
    - **The line:** `sign` on the audio checklist, one cue per creature. "A sign means only that it's there; a tell means it's coming", so each is the creature moving off, never its voice or its tell, from its own body parts (`tools/audio/recipes/signs.py`). The Ribbits are wet skin shifting in grass and one soft hop away, no throat. The Soot Children are small bare feet over cinders and soot in the air, never the call. The Whistler is its legs and body through brush with the siphon shut. The Grumbler is a heavy scuttle behind a wall and a low mutter, with nothing rasping in its gnaw's 1.4–2.2 kHz.
    - **Out there:** every take is heard 15–22 m off in the open night: the air takes a little off the top, a touch of the night's room has its tail cut short (one every 12–24 s never piles up a wash), and moving off pulls it darker and quieter. −24 LUFS, under the tells.
    - **The Gaunt and the Followers** stay silent (the line marks them so): their sign is the eyes alone, as their tell is silence.
    - **Installed and hooked** (L1; `levels.py` counts a line keyed by `Director.Key` as hooked). `CreatureSoundTests.ASignShownAfootIsHeardOnceAsItsOwnSoundAndTheGauntsIsItsEyesAlone` pins it: once as it starts, the fallback where the checklist has nothing, the Gaunt silent, and the game's four installed.
    - **Not yet:** the director's Keep or Redo on the eight candidates (the first of each plays meanwhile).

360. **The armoured engine's damage, and the rest of #76's armour (queue #97, E1; note 338's "not yet").** The hood (note 338) cased the boiler inside the engine's armour, but its damage was still drawn on the boiler. The rupture's tear (note 277) sat inside the corridor, so the burst's steam blew out of a hood with no hole in it, and a damaged boiler's leaks (`DamageKit.Leaks`) came from inside the plate.
    - **The tear is in the hood** (`TrainKit.RuptureSeam`, `HoodFace`): on the left side at the same place along the engine (the cab's back + 2.7 m, between two seam straps). It sits 0.9 m above the deck, below the feed pipe, and stands proud of the hood's straps so they don't cross the hole. It's drawn 1.7 times its boiler size (`RuptureSize`): a blown-out plate on a 14 m side, which reads from the line where the boiler's own seam didn't. `Effects.Rupture` follows the seam, so the burst and the hiss come out of it. An engine without a hood (none now) keeps the boiler's seam.
    - **The leaks come through the hood's side** above the feed pipe, wherever the boiler's split seam is along it.
    - **The gouges, flaps and breach** (`DamageKit.Engine`) already land on the hood: its walls are the engine's `CabWall` side sheets, so nothing changed there.
    - **Wrecked, the headlamp's glass cracks and a running board bends** (`DamageKit.CrackedLamp`, `BentBoard`; the checklist's "next" for the engine's damage). A star of dark cracks and a shard gone sit over the lens while it still burns, struck in one of the open wedges between the saltire's bars where they show (the lamp put out is still `SceneArt.HeadlampOut`'s). A length of one running board has its outer half torn off its brackets and hanging at a slant, with the gap left black.
    - **Plate over the bogies** (`TrainKit.BogieSkirt`, every car): a riveted skirt from the underframe to 0.32 m above the rail, the wheelbase long and a little more, with its foot bevelled back to the ends. A slot at axle height keeps the journal boxes in sight, so the hot box (note 331) still shows, and the wheels still read turning under it. Braced with straps, like the hood.
    - **The gun car's casemate: the shield is it.** The guns slide along their roof rail (T93) from car to car, so a fixed casemate on the gun car would pin them or fight them. Each gun's riveted shield (note 338, `GunShield`) turns and slides with it, which is the casemate the reference's turret was.
    - **Verified:** shots: `dt screenshot --view rupture --ruptured 30` (the tear in the hood, hissing), `--integrity 0.2,1 --view rupture` (a leak out of the hood's side), `--integrity 0.05,1 --view headlamp` (the cracked lamp), `--upgrades secondGuardCar --survey --view hotbox --car 3` (the skirts under the gun car and the next). `EffectsTests` holds the seam on the hood's outer face, between its deck and roof; `PerfBudgetTests` and the Game suite are green.

361. **The Ribbit rebuilt organically (G1, queue #98; the director, 8 Oct 2026: "Redo the Ribbit the way you did the Gannet").**
    E1's #29 (note 291) had fused the Ribbit's body, but the director's call on the Gannet's first pass ("boxy and rigid, not
    organic at all") held for it too. Rebuilt the Gannet's way (note 340):
    - **One skin** (`tools/blender/ribbit.py`): smooth volumes (rump, loins, chest, a slung belly, the haunches folded over
      the hind legs, hare's feet, a toad's shoulders and arms to the palms, the neck's folds, the skull with eye mounds,
      lids, glands, nostrils and a rolled lip, the ears' fleshy stalks, the throat's sac, hip bones, spine knuckles, warts),
      each a solid for `rig.fuse`'s union and a term in a signed-distance field blended over its own radius. The union's
      voxels are settled onto that field before QuadriFlow (`rig.fuse`'s new optional `settle`, off for every other model),
      so limbs grow out of the body with flesh in the creases. The jaw is a second skin made the same way; eyes, teeth,
      tongue, ear blades, fingers and toes sit over them.
    - **Its colour baked** (`tools/models/recipes/ribbit.py`): warts, wrinkles, the sac's folds and the veins from a sculpted
      high copy into one 2048 atlas's normals and occlusion; wet grey-white skin, grey-green down the back, a paler
      pink-veined belly and sac, pink ears with red veins, milky eyes.
    - **Unchanged:** every bone (the tongue's stretch and the throat's swell, `CreatureArt`), the seven clips, pivot, scale and
      facing; nothing in the sim. 7,792 triangles (distance copy 3,329), inside the beast's budget.
    - **Verified:** `art clearance --only ribbit` clean, `art check`, `CreatureArtTests`, `CreatureBodyTests`; stills
      `docs/design/creatures/ribbit-{closeup,swell,tongue,devour}.png`.
374. **Powder to the guns, the fourth upkeep job (queue #111, D1; GDD App. F.3, the director, 7 Oct 2026: "on the train, still relatively boring from point A to point B ... threats attacking the train tower-defense style, to give the gunners something to do"; [orchestrator.md](design/orchestrator.md) §5.1 U4, §8 question 3: U4 was the outline's proposed first).**
    - **What it is.** A gun fires what's in its ready rack (`GunState.Rack`, combat.json `guns.rack` 6), not its whole stock. `Ammo` keeps its meaning, the gun's rounds for the night (24), so the stores, the lineside drops, the upgrade, the save, the run's cost and the radio all go on counting it unchanged; the rest of it (`Guns.Stowed`) is down in the powder locker, the shot locker the art already draws in the guard van's front corner (App. C.3: "an iron-bound chest in the gun car's front corner"). The engine has no locker: its gun's share is in the guard van's too, a walk down the train. `rack` 0 is the gun as before (its whole stock at it).
    - **The carry.** Empty hands within 1.3 m of the locker (`Guns.AtLocker`), a Use press: a charge (`BodyKind.Powder`, the powder bag prop) in the hands (`Bodies.Handle`'s `fetch`). Light: ladders are climbed with it. At a gun whose rack isn't full, Use held 2 s (`chargeSeconds`) fills it (`Guns.Fill`) and the charge is spent; Use there doesn't put it down (`keep`). The rack fills from that gun's stock first, then from the other guns' (a pool, in the order they stand; their stocks move with it). A rack run dry leaves nothing to load (its last shot sets no reload); filled, it wants powder, ball and ram again.
    - **Why a rack, not a magazine count.** Keeping `Ammo` as the stock and adding the rack as a part of it touches nothing that counts powder; only firing and loading read the rack (`Guns.Ready`). A carried charge isn't drawn from the locker until it's loaded, so one dropped or thrown off the train costs nothing but the walk.
    - **The tell.** At the gun with the rack empty: THE RACK'S EMPTY: POWDER FROM THE GUARD VAN (NO SHOT when there's none left anywhere). Seated: THE GUN: n IN THE RACK, m BELOW. At the locker: TAKE A CHARGE, and how many rounds are left; with a charge at the gun, FILL THE RACK and its progress.
    - **Bots.** A gunner whose rack is dry goes for powder itself (`GunnerBot.Powder`): up out of the seat, down the guard van's hatch ladder beside its gun, along the van to the locker, a charge, back up the ladder, and Use held at the gun; from another car's roof its legs take it along to the van. The rack is back inside half a minute. A walker bringing it while the gunner keeps firing is the outline's crew job; bots don't split it yet (they do now: note 377).
    - **Tests that met it:** `GunTests.SustainedFireBringsTheSwarm` and `EnemyTests.AGunnerWhoSpraysFromTooFarBringsTheChoirDownOnHimself` keep the rack fed (a walker bringing the powder; spraying from one rack of six no longer loads the meter enough to bring the Choir, which is the rack doing its job), and `UpgradeTests.ACooledGunFoulsLessOften` fires with no rack: both are about something else. `HoundRunTests`' gunner answers a run of two as before.
    - **Verified.** `GunPowderTests` (6): each gun leaves with its rack full and the rest stowed, the engine's in the guard van; a rack run dry has nothing to load or fire; a charge taken at the locker and held at the gun fills the rack in its time, and it wants its reload; the engine gun's rack comes from the pool, and an empty locker gives nothing; no rack is the old gun; a gunner bot goes down the hatch for powder and brings it up, in order, inside 30 s. `HudTests.ARackRunDryAndThePowderLockerSayWhereThePowderIs`. Protocol 39 (the vehicle record carries the rack).

375. **The crew in the air and on a lurching car (queue #112, E1; the art checklist's `crew-gap` "next": "a stumble when the train sways, and a jump between roofs").**
    - **The leap** (crew_clips.py `jump`, `CrewPose.Jump`). A crewmate going up off a jump had no pose of their own: `CrewActs` had one only for falling (faster than 3 m/s down), so the walk or run played in mid-air. Now rising faster than 0.5 m/s (`Rising`; a step off a ledge never rises) is the leap, played once from the spring. The clip pushes off the back foot with the arms swung up, then gathers both knees under the chest, leant into it, the arms reaching for the far roof and the eyes on it. Over the top the sim says nothing until they're falling, so `SceneArt` holds the leap for 0.75 s from its start (`JumpHoldSeconds`) rather than flicker to the walk. In first person it isn't work in view (`OwnArms`), and a tool stays in the fist.
    - **The stumble** (crew_clips.py `stumble`, `CrewPose.Stumble`). On a car straining on a bend taken too fast (`BendStrain.PerCar`, App. F.1's overspeed telegraph) at 0.5 or more (`StumbleAt`: past halfway to off, where the eye's judder is plain and the flanges' haze comes on), a crewmate stood, walking or on the gap fights for footing. They are thrown one way onto a foot stepped wide, the hips over it, the arms flung out (the thrown side low to catch, the other high), then back over the other way, low and knees soft. Busy hands (a wheel, a lever, a carry) keep their act. `GreyboxScene` hands its strain to `SceneArt.BendStrain` before the crew are drawn. Art only: the sim's own lurch throws them off later still (`Lineside`), and C1's #107 leans the car (`CarLean`) from the same strain.
    - **Staging:** `dt screenshot --act jump,jump,jump --view crewside` (each further into the leap, up off the roof); `--crew --strain 0.9 --view crew` (the roof crew stumbling; `Staging.Crew` now puts them in car 2's frame, as a live crewmate is).
    - **Verified:** `CrewActsTests.TheActIsReadOffTheirState` (rising is the leap) and `TheLeapIsHeldOverTheTopAndACarStrainingOnABendHasThemStumbling`. `dt art clearance --only crew` adds no failures (the same 18 older ones). Contact sheets: `dt art clip crew jump --yaw 90`, `dt art clip crew stumble --yaw 0`.

376. **Bot nights that run hot (D1.2 for D1, queue #113; note 328's open end: "the harness has no top-speed driver yet").** `dt harness --express [m/s]` (21 if no speed's given; `HarnessOptions.Express`, `ConductorBot.Express`): the director's playtest, "kept the train hot the whole time and didn't stop for anything".
    - **The driver** works no stops: no spur, no loading, no switch set back for one (`ConductorBot`'s stop block is skipped). It runs at the express speed over the boards and the line's authority, braking only for a bend it would come off on (`HotBend`: under each bend's derailing speed, the plan's `ADerail` × 0.85, in time at half the rake's rated brake, looking as far ahead as a stop from the top speed takes). Everything else is as before: the Track Doll on the rail, a Holdout, a crewmate left behind, the fire, the Stoker.
    - **Found: the boards hold a train under the hound run.** The line speed is 20 m/s on Local, 18 on Frontier, 16 on Dead Lines and 14 on Deep Territory (tiers.json `lineSpeed`), and the hauling driver keeps to it. So the run (note 328, `fromSpeed` 19) comes only to a train run over the boards, except on Local. That is the top-speed strategy it was made to answer, but it's worth the director knowing: it's question 4 in orchestrator.md §8 (only above 19, or at any speed?).
    - **The first express night** (frontier:7, `--bots 4 --enemies --express`, 900 s):
        - The train held about 21 m/s between bends and covered 11.7 km against the hauling night's 5.4.
        - A hound run came at 125 s: four runners; the gunner fired 3 rounds, killing 3 and scattering 1; none aboard.
        - Three crewmates died: the gunner dragged off by a Dragger, one hunted down by Ribbits after being left behind, and one walker who jumped at speed. The train stood twice, about 2 minutes each, for crewmates left behind (T96).
        - Running hot is deadly for the walkers on the roofs: a director's-eye finding, not a bug here.
    - **Verified:** `ExpressTests.TheExpressDriverRunsOverTheBoardsTakesNoStopsAndStaysOnTheRails` (frontier:7, a driver alone, 420 s: the hauling driver keeps under the 18 m/s line speed; the express one passes 20 m/s, never stands once away, goes further, and doesn't derail).

379. **The orchestrator's pacing targets judged (D1.2 for D1, queue #116; [orchestrator.md](design/orchestrator.md) §4: "each is a `balance.json` check once it's built").** `dt balance` reports two of §4's targets on the nights with a crew of two or more (the crews the census steers, note 345), from balance.json `pacing`:
    - **P1** (`slackOverSeconds`, 30): no crewmate spends more than that many seconds at or past the census's `slackPress` (150 s) in a night. It is read from the harness's `threats.slack` as `BalanceRow.SlackOver`.
    - **P3** (`engaged`, 45–60 %): something engaged for that share of the night out on the line, as 1 − the harness's pacing `quietShare`; `BalanceRow.QuietShare`.
    - **Advisory** (`advisory`, true): reported and flagged, never failing the sweep (`BalanceCheck.Advisory`; the report's `pass` is every check passing or advisory), so the nightly soak doesn't turn red on a target the director hasn't set. Off, a miss fails the sweep like the others.
    - **The first reading** (frontier:1, crew 4, 6 cars, 900 s): P1 31 s (just over); P3 77 % engaged (the night is busier than the outline's target, which was a guess, not a measure). Both flagged, the sweep passing.
    - **Not yet judged:** P2 and P5 (the guns' targets and the hound runs on a hot night) need express sweeps (note 376's `--express` in `dt balance`); P4 and P7 are App. B.1's cooldown and terminus silence, already in the harness's pacing; P6 (grabs at stops) and P8 (solo, one at a time: `LiveCrewTests`) are tests, not sweeps.
    - **Verified:** `BalanceTests.ThePacingTargetsAreReportedAndAdvisoryTheyNeverFailTheSweep` (a night slack 120 s past and 35 % engaged: both flagged, the sweep passing; within targets both pass; advisory off, a miss fails it) and `ACrewOfOneHasNoPacingTargets`.
382. **Walkers out of the armoured engine (queue #119, D1; found in a 45-minute bot night with upkeep, 8 Oct).** Since the hood (#76, note 338) the cab is at the engine's front with the boiler cased behind it, and the cab's back is plated across the boiler; the ways out are the corridors either side of it. A walker on the engine's deck walked straight back along the centreline (`_direction = 1`, "the engine belongs to whoever is working the cab") into that plating, and stood there: in the night's trace one of two walkers spent most of it at the cab floor's spawn point (z −4.85) holding a car fire three cars back as its trouble, and 7 of 8 guttering lamps went out.
    - **The way out** (`RoofWalkerBot.OutOfTheEngine`): over to the left corridor's mouth inside the cab, down it to the deck behind the smokebox, out along T90's footplate beside the coupler plate, and sideways down onto the plate; there the walker's way out of any gap takes it up the engine's end ladder onto the hood's roof. Null for an engine with no cab (as before).
    - **The jump from the hood's roof:** the roof stops over the smokebox, short of the engine's end (`Half − BoilerToEnd`), so "near the end" is measured from there on the engine; the gap to car 1 is then jumped as any.
    - **Verified:** `EngineWayOutTests.AWalkerInTheCabGetsOutOntoTheCarRoofs` (out onto car 1's roof inside 11 s; before, still at the cab floor after 40 s).

378. **The rescue matched to the grab (queue #115, E1; the art checklist's `crew-rescue` "next": "matched to the victim's clip, and a pull free from a mouth").** A friend hauling someone free played `haul` (down on a knee at their collar), or `haul_up` for a friend over an edge below, whatever had hold of them. Now `CrewActs.Rescue` finds the holding creature nearest the held friend (every machine mirrors the enemies) and plays the rescue for its grab (`RescueOf`, App. A.1):
    - **Out of the Car Hugger's mouth** (`pull_mouth`; D1's swallowed rescue, note 310): feet braced, the front leg straight against the pull, the body leant far back, both fists at the waist's height heaved in, then a fresh grip hand over hand.
    - **The Tippy Toesie's fingers prised off a face** (`pry_off`; App. A.5's smother): squared up, feet wide, both hands up at the face, the fingers wrenched off to one side and then the other, the body leant into it.
    - **Lifted away by the Whistler or the Choir** (`haul_down`): reached up overhead for the legs, then the whole weight dropped onto them, knees bending, the fists hauled down to the chest.
    - **A Dragger's, over the edge**, is still `haul_up`; the rest (the Ribbit's tongue, a pin) still `haul`.
    - Art only: the sim's rescue (the grab broken by a friend in reach) is unchanged.
    - **Staging:** `dt screenshot --threats --hugger swallow --rescue --view swallow` (a friend pulling the swallowed one; `Staging.SwallowRescuer`), and `--act pull_mouth,pry_off,haul_down`.
    - **Verified:** `CrewActsTests.TheRescueIsMatchedToWhatHasThem`; `CreatureArtTests` carries the new clips (and note 375's) in the crew's list. `dt art clearance --only crew` adds no failures (the same 18).
334. **The Moose heard (AU1, queue #73; G1's note 339, docs/design/creatures/moose.md §4).** G1's nine lines on the audio checklist have 30 candidates (`tools/audio/recipes/moose_tells.py`, `moose_acts.py`), each in its own band and rhythm, so no other creature's tell is mistaken for it (spec A.1, A.4). The first of each is installed, and `GameAudio.MooseSounds` hooks them off the record alone, as G1 answered on #247: its `MooseMode` in Height, its aggro in Extra2, its rams in Health (1 + rams).
    - **Grazing** (aggro under `listenAt`): the slow chew held, with browse torn, a sac's wet creak and a low grunt now and then. **Listening** (`listenAt` to `warnAt`): the chewing stops dead and nothing plays; the silence is the tell. **Warning** (`warnAt` up): a cough-like grunt, a run of teeth clacks and a hoof raked back, every 1.2–2.8 s.
    - **Squaring up:** two stamps 0.38 s apart and a snort, as it begins. **Charging:** its hooves and its wheeze held, brush breaking now and then. **Snagged:** the wood groaning and a bellow, then the rack grinding, held. **Searching:** its heavy breathing and sniffing held (not a snort, which is the square-up's), the rack knocking on a wall now and then.
    - **A ram:** a deep iron boom through the car on each `RamCount` step, so it lands on the shudder, and the rack scraping the plates 0.2 s after.
    - **A train going by:** grazing and short of warning, with the train moving over 1 m/s and a car within `trainPassAt` (the art's `trainPass` clip's rule, and the sim's +25 aggro on the same condition), a long call after it and the verge thrashed, once a pass.
    - **Pinned:** `CreatureSoundTests.TheMooseIsHeardGrazingFallsSilentListeningWarnsAndChargesAndBoomsOnEachRam`. All eight lines are at L1 (`levels.py`).
    - **Not yet:** the director's Keep or Redo; the hooves stay one loop whatever the ground (the charge is on ballast and earth).
354. **The town's stones underfoot, and the ground's (AU1, queue #91; the director, 8 Oct 2026: "Theres a super weird squishy footstep sound when I walk on the stones in the town"; App. F.1, build 1121: "Footsteps on the ground sound wrong; on wood and grates they're good").** The ground's footsteps, every set off the train, were a boom or a soft wobble a step.
    - **The stones' own steps were soft.** The `cobbles` set (a stop's streets, a halt's platform) and `concrete` (inside a stop's buildings) were built on Kenney's concrete footsteps, which are soft soles: 99% of each step under 1 kHz, a damped 250 Hz wobble at heel and toe. That reads as a squish, not stone. `tools/audio/recipes/crew_feet.py`'s `stone` builds each contact as a hard boot on rock instead: the heel's crack (a few ms of noise from 1.2 kHz up, and a tick), the stone's dead knock (three broad modes at 0.4–2.3 kHz, choked within 20 ms, so no pitch), a 25 ms thump of weight with no ring, and the boot's own sole click. Outdoors there's sand between the setts and no room; indoors the same step has less sand and the short hard room. Walk, run, jump, land and scuff on both are rebuilt and installed, centred 1.8–2.6 kHz where they were 300–390 Hz. On the audio checklist the cobbles and concrete candidates are replaced, not added beside the old ones, since the old ones were what the director heard.
    - **Pinned:** `CrewAudioTests.BootsOnStoneCrackRatherThanSquish` renders the installed walk, run and land on stone and wants as much over 1 kHz as at 100–500 Hz. The soft ones were 7 to 17 dB under.
    - **The rest of the ground boomed.** `dirt` (packed earth, the forest floor) was Kenney's wooden steps lowpassed at 900 Hz under the boot lowpassed: two slow swings of 40–60 Hz at heel and toe, 89% under 250 Hz. `grass` had the boot lowpassed at 700 Hz under its swish, a sub wobble each step. `ballast`'s crunch had no heel (a 200 ms hiss) and its pad of weight (pink noise lowpassed, mostly sub) a boom under it, as did `mud`'s. Now each step's weight is `tup`, a short dead knock at 150–260 Hz, high-passed at 110 Hz and choked within 30 ms. Dirt is that tup with the packs' real crunch thinned and darkened to dry crumbs and needles, grit, and a twig's tick now and then. Grass is its swish with the wobble high-passed out, a rustle of stalks, and a soft tup. Ballast gets a stone heel (a choked knock at 0.4–1.3 kHz) under the crunch, with everything under 90 Hz cut. Mud keeps its squelch and suck, with everything under 80 Hz cut. The boards, grates, plate, roof and coal are the train's and untouched: the director likes the first two.
    - **Pinned:** `CrewAudioTests.TheGroundUnderfootIsAStepNotABoom` wants what's under 120 Hz at least 8 dB under the step (250 Hz–4 kHz) on dirt, grass and ballast, and 3 dB on mud. The old dirt was 7 dB over, grass 3 under, ballast 6 under, mud level; the car's boards are 10 under.
    - **A walled town's streets were the land under them.** B2's walled towns (queue #74, note 335) draw their streets in beaten stones (the `ballast` texture) and their lanes in mud (`ground_mud`) as strips over the ground (`WorldArt.Streets`), but `GroundTexture` didn't know they were there: underfoot was the land beneath, grass or the shore's red mud, so a street of stones played the grass set's soft steps. That's the squish the director heard in the town. `GroundTexture` now takes the stop's town (`Footing.Ground` passes `world.Town`) and, after what's built at the stop, asks `TownWay`: on a street (along it from `S0` to `S1`, within half its width of `D`) the stones; on a lane's strip of mud (the same strips `Streets` draws, from one `LaneMids`, so what's drawn and what's heard can't drift apart) the mud; off them, the land as before.
    - **Pinned:** `CrewAudioTests.AWalledTownsStreetsAreItsStonesUnderfootAndItsLanesItsMud` stands a town of 3000 at a generated stop and walks its streets and a lane through `Footing.Ground`. Without the change the streets were `grass`.
381. **The grain elevator modelled (queue #118, C1; GDD §18's set pieces, the art checklist's `grain-elevator`).** The grain elevator was still the kit's: three plain cylinders 26 m high with a box on them. It was the weakest of the demo's facilities beside the modelled headframe, chemical tank and watchtower (facility_pieces). Now it's built as a prairie concrete elevator is (`tools/models/recipes/facility_pieces.py` `grain_elevator`, 612 triangles against a budget of 3000):
    - **The silos:** four slip-formed concrete bins in a row along the track, 8.8 m across and 26 m high, touching, with interstice walls closing the gaps between them. The slip form's pour lines every 1.5 m and the rain streaks off the gallery's eaves down the line side are baked onto the shell. Each is 28-sided in the game mesh, so it reads round from the track.
    - **Over them:** the bin floor's gallery in rusted corrugated iron, its windows dark but one lit; and the leg house over the far end, another 12 m up under a pyramid roof (where the bucket elevator's legs run), one window lit. A caged ladder runs up the near silo. At the foot, the receiving shed stands on the line side, its doorway dark.
    - **The spout:** swung down from the gallery to 6 m over the track and 2.5 m out from its centre (a car's side is 1.5 m out), banded, its canvas sock hanging, held up by two stays from the leg house. It's dressing: the sim still pours from the site's bin on its legs, 80 m along (`spout.back`).
    - **One layer at 1024:** some 4,500 m² of concrete and iron would get about 13 cm a texel at the props' 512. `cook.finish` takes a `size` now (unset, it's 512 as before), and the elevator's layer is a hero layer: GreyboxRenderer keeps those in arrays of their own (up to 64; the creatures and crew use about 20).
    - **Where:** StructureKit's `GrainElevator` case sets it where the kit's silos stood, 15 m out on the site's side, and keeps the kit's silos as the fallback when the model isn't there. At frontier:7's elevator that's 19 m off the spur and 25 m back from the site's layout point.
    - **`dt screenshot --site --facility <kind> --building [m]`:** a facility's buildings rather than its machinery. The camera stands 50 m along its track and 5 m out at a crewman's eye, looking up at what stands `m` out (19 by default, the elevator's silos). The site's other set-piece cameras are unchanged.
    - **Verified:** `dt art check` (612 triangles against the large prop's 8,000 and the facility's 90,000), `PropArtTests`, `StopArtTests`, `LookTests`. Looked at: the turntable, and frontier:7's elevator at night and at dawn, before and after.

384. **The Gannet heard (AU1, queue #121; G1's note 340 and its four lines on the audio checklist; design `docs/design/creatures/gannet.md` §4).** The Gannet landed with no sound. It now has its tells and its acts, read off its record as the art reads it.
    - **What plays.** `GameAudio.GannetSounds` goes by its `GannetMode` (in Height), the spine's phase and time, and its Health:
        - **Soaring or climbing** over the train: its call or a great wingbeat every 2.5–6 s (`tell-gannet-calls`).
        - **Hanging over a walker:** nothing. The calls stop, and the silence is the tell.
